author: ffffffpy
body: ## Description Add a read-only knowledge processing dashboard for observing the current execution state of the knowledge ingestion pipeline. The dashboard aggregates existing processing spans, Asynq task states, and Wiki pending operations into nine logical stages: * Document parsing * Document chunking * Index construction * Multimodal processing * Post-processing orchestration * Summary generation * Question generation * Knowledge graph extraction * Wiki synthesis Each stage is aggregated by knowledge, processing attempt, and logical stage. Internal fan-out tasks such as individual images, question batches, graph chunks, Wiki pages, and their retries are presented as a single parent-stage progress entry instead of separate tasks. The dashboard shows: * Knowledge items currently running in each stage * The number of knowledge items waiting or retrying * Aggregated progress for multimodal, question, graph, and Wiki processing * Per-knowledge processing pipeline details * Knowledge base filtering and title search * Automatic and manual refresh * Read-only queue and processing-state inspection * Degraded behavior when the Asynq queue snapshot is unavailable * Support for both Asynq and Lite execution modes This feature is observability-only. It does not modify task scheduling, workers, retries, queue priorities, processing state transitions, or knowledge-processing execution paths. ### Implementation notes * Reuses the existing knowledge processing span data. * Reads Asynq queue state through a read-only inspector. * Reads Wiki pending operations without changing their state. * Separates processing attempts so stale tasks are not merged into the current attempt. * Aggregates fan-out spans in the repository layer to avoid loading large numbers of graph, image, and question child spans into memory. * Marks truncated queue counts as unreliable instead of presenting incomplete counts as exact values. * Adds database indexes for dashboard queries. * Adds frontend request guards to prevent stale responses from replacing newer dashboard data. ### Known limitation Stage drawer pagination currently builds the state of all active knowledge items and then paginates the filtered result in memory. Its cost is proportional to the number of active knowledge items, not the number of historical completed items or fan-out child spans. This is expected to be sufficient for the current workload. Repository-level stage filtering and database cursor pagination can be added later if the deployment regularly has approximately 1,000 or more concurrently active knowledge items. ## Type of Change * [ ] 🐛 Bug fix * [x] ✨ New feature * [ ] 💥 Breaking change * [ ] 📚 Documentation update * [ ] 🎨 Refactor * [x] ⚡ Performance improvement * [x] 🧪 Test * [ ] 🔧 Configuration / Build / CI ## Related Issue N/A ## Testing Run the following backend checks: ```bash go test ./internal/... go test -race ./internal/router/... -run ProcessingQueueSnapshot ``` Run the following frontend checks: ```bash cd frontend npm run test npm run type-check npm run build ``` Manual verification: * Opened the knowledge processing dashboard. * Verified the nine logical processing stages. * Verified filtering by knowledge base and keyword. * Verified automatic and manual refresh. * Verified stage queue drawers and knowledge processing details. * Verified multimodal, question, graph, and Wiki progress aggregation. * Verified that completed historical knowledge items are not loaded into the active dashboard. * Verified that the dashboard does not expose task control actions. * Verified the empty state and queue-data degradation message. ## Checklist * [ ] `make fmt && make lint && make test` pass locally * [x] Self-reviewed the code * [x] Added/updated tests covering the change * [x] Added Swagger annotations and localized frontend text * [x] No breaking changes * [x] Confirmed that the dashboard is read-only and does not modify workers or task execution ## Screenshots / Recordings Add screenshots showing:

author: danielrozin
body:
## Summary
Fixes link-equity cannibalization from aversusb.net serving the same comparison at **two competing `/compare/` URLs** (one per entity ordering).

**Audit (read-only, run vs prod 2026-06-21):** `166` duplicate ordering clusters out of `2093` `/compare/` rows (`1927` distinct comparisons). Script: `scripts/dan-1265-audit-duplicate-orderings.ts`.

## What this does
**Consolidation (301 + canonical)**
- `compare-ordering-redirects.generated.ts` — generated `retired → survivor` map for all 166 clusters. **Survivor = the page with real traffic** (viewCount); zero-traffic ties default to the alphabetically-sorted slug (matches `comparisonSlug()` generation order).
  - 10 clusters had a trafficked survivor — e.g. `adidas-vs-nike → nike-vs-adidas` (534K views), `china-vs-usa → usa-vs-china` (1.2M), `ford-vs-tesla → tesla-vs-ford` (456K). Blind alphabetical canonicalization would have redirected these **strong pages into empty ones** — avoided.
  - 156 were 0/0 alpha ties.
- Entity-alias case from the audit: `paramount-plus-vs-peacock → paramount-vs-peacock` (survivor by Semrush rank 39 vs 57).
- `compare-redirects.ts` merges generated + alias + manual (xbox/ps5) maps → permanent edge 301s via `next.config redirects()`, with a self-loop/chain guard.
- **Archived the 167 retired DB rows** (`status=archived`) so they drop from the sitemap (already applied to prod; the edge redirect survives row deletion).

**Source prevention — no more dual-ordering generation**
- `sortComparisonSlug()` canonicalizes a slug by alpha-sorting its `-vs-` segments.
- `/api/comparisons/generate`: refuses to regenerate a known retired duplicate (serves the survivor) and forces **new** comparisons to a single canonical ordering, so `A-vs-B` and `B-vs-A` can never coexist.
- `/compare/[slug]`: a brand-new reverse ordering with no page yet `301`s to the canonical sorted ordering before generating.

## Verification
- `npm run build` passes.
- Redirect map: 168 entries (166 ordering + alias + xbox), 0 chains/loops; sample directions verified (`roomba-vs-roborock → roborock-vs-roomba`, `adidas-vs-nike → nike-vs-adidas`).
- Post-deploy: confirm `curl -I /compare/roomba-vs-roborock` → 308/301 to `/compare/roborock-vs-roomba`, and survivor pages emit self-referencing canonicals.

Closes DAN-1265. Audit context: DAN-1264.

## Summary
- Fix the production Vercel deploy failure introduced by running historical Drizzle migrations during `migrate:on-deploy`.

Production deploy failed before Next build, inside `pnpm --filter @intro-builder/web migrate:on-deploy`:

Failed query: ALTER TABLE "templates" ALTER COLUMN "source" DROP NOT NULL;

The production database has historical schema drift from before deploy-time migrations were enabled. author: mattmre
body:
## Summary

The PR-A4 headline campaign on **real data** (SciFact, MiniLM base / mpnet swap, offline GPU, 3 seeds, `query_encoder_swap` arena), produced by the merged driver (#273). Commits the aggregate manifest + auto-generated results doc. Per-run JSONs are regenerable via the deterministic seeded driver and omitted to avoid ~10 MB git-history bloat.

This answers the sprint's central question — *does the supervised closed loop actually recover retrieval after an encoder upgrade on real data?* — honestly.

## Real-data result (mean over seeds 42/1337/7)

| Condition | Baseline | Final NDCG | Reading |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| C0 frozen | 0.819 | 0.006 | encoder upgrade is catastrophic |
| C2 re-embed-original | 0.819 | 0.006 | **== C0: the oracle is genuinely defeated on real data** |
| C2O oracle (re-embed new space) | 0.819 | 0.813 | recovery is possible (upper bound) |
| C3a bounded supervised | 0.819 | 0.159 | **fires + writes 3/3; ~25× above frozen** |
| C4a unbounded supervised | 0.819 | 0.206 | unbounded > bounded |

Budget sweep (C3a, seed 42) **plateaus**: 30→0.159, 200→0.173, 1000→0.181, 2000→0.182. Three-seed confirm @2000 steps: 0.164 ± 0.015.

**Honest reading:** detection-triggered bounded correction recovers a measurable fraction of catastrophic encoder-upgrade drift (0.006 → ~0.18), scaling with budget up to a plateau, but does not close the gap to the full-re-embed oracle (0.81). Ordering C0=C2 < C3a < C4a ≪ C2O. Partial recovery with a **characterized capacity ceiling** — not merely under-training (the sweep plateaus), which closes the budget caveat Tier B raised in PR-A2b.

## Runtime Evidence

EVIDENCE: committed `experiment_runs/drift-recovery/swap/swap-campaign-manifest-2026-06.json` (force-added; `experiment_runs/` is gitignored, per PR-5 precedent) holds all 22 runs' baseline/final/recovery/applied/norm rows; `docs/drift-recovery-swap-results-2026-06.md` renders the tables above. The full campaign ran offline (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=1`) on GPU peaking at ~5 GB of 24 (no OOM; shared night-work untouched). Actuator firing is real: C3a/C4a applied=3/3 runs with mean correction norm ~0.51.
SMOKE: floor — the driver + experiment unit suites are green (#273); this PR is data artifacts only (no code), so the production code path is the already-merged, Tier-B-100 driver.

## Brutal Honesty

L1/L2/L3/L11: none — data-only PR. L4: none — the result is reported exactly as measured; C3a does NOT beat the oracle and that is stated plainly; partial recovery is not dressed as full recovery. L5/L8: per-run JSON trajectories are not committed (regenerable via the deterministic seeded driver) — the committed manifest is the durable aggregate evidence and the driver is deterministic+seeded; full reproduction requires the offline HF model/dataset cache (CD-A2-01), disclosed. L13: the "characterized ceiling" claim is backed by the committed budget-sweep plateau (30→2000 steps: 0.159→0.182), not asserted — a reviewer can read the rows.

This PR contains no code; the modeling + driver were adversarially reviewed to BHS 100 in #272 and #273.

body:
## O que muda

A aba **Conciliação** hoje cruza PDF × Open Finance comparando apenas a **contagem** de lançamentos e listando duplicatas. Faltava o que foi pedido: comparar os **totais de gastos e receitas** entre as fontes para um mês (ex.: **maio/26**).

Este PR adiciona um **placar de totais por mês** no topo da aba:

| | PDF / arquivos | Open Finance | Diferença |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gastos | R$ … (n) | R$ … (n) | ± R$ … |
| Receitas | R$ … (n) | R$ … (n) | ± R$ … |

- **Seletor de mês** — default para **maio/26** (`2026-05`) quando existe, senão o mês mais recente.
- **Diferença = PDF − Open Finance**: positiva = PDF trouxe mais no mês (banco ainda não sincronizou, período fora da cobertura do Open Finance, ou possível duplicata só de um lado). Verde quando bate, âmbar quando diverge.

## Detalhes técnicos

- `totaisPorMes()` em `src/lib/conciliacao.ts`: agrega por **data real do movimento** (`mesReal`) — e não pela competência da fatura — para que uma compra de maio caia em maio nas **duas** fontes. Soma só valores em **BRL**; linhas em moeda estrangeira são contadas à parte e sinalizadas.
- `PlacarMes` em `src/components/tabs/Conciliacao.tsx`: seletor de mês + tabela, reaproveitando os dados já carregados pela aba (nenhuma consulta extra ao banco).

## Notas

- Diagnóstico apenas — **nada é alterado no banco**, igual ao resto da aba.
- Os números reais não aparecem aqui no PR porque dependem do seu login (RLS do Supabase). Após o merge, abra a aba **Conciliação** e selecione **Mai/26** para ver o placar com os seus dados.

## Report bundle snapshot + Download-report link + picker validation feedback

Three follow-ons that complete the report-bundle workflow: the bundle now carries the live posture, the overview
can download it in one click, and a bad date range tells you why — building on the combined report bundle, the
date-picker, and the server-side range validation.

### Features
- **Latest snapshot in the report bundle.** `GET /admin/alerts/digest-report` now includes the current
  `sloDigest()` snapshot (window/delivery ratios, worst routes, mute/catch-up state, deltas) — as a `snapshot`
  object in the JSON and a leading `# snapshot` key,value section in the CSV — so a reviewer sees the live
  posture alongside the historical rows in one artifact.
- **"Download report bundle" link.** The overview date-picker gains a link that downloads the digest-report CSV
  for the current from/to in one click (the UI counterpart to the bundle endpoint), instead of pulling the
  history and audit CSVs separately.
- **Picker validation feedback.** When Apply (or a quick-range) produces a bad range, `applyDigestRange()` now
  reads the endpoint's HTTP 400 and shows the message ("'from' must not be after 'to'", etc.) in the picker note
  without pinning the view — previously the bad fetch failed silently.

### New files
- `src/test/java/com/example/imini/AlertDigestReportSnapshotDownloadValidationTest.java`

### Changed files
- `AlertSink.java` (4-arg `digestReportCsv(mute, snapshot, history, audit)` adding a `# snapshot` section;
  3-arg form retained for back-compat).
- `AgentController.java` (digest-report endpoint includes `alertSink.sloDigest()` as `snapshot` in JSON and the
  CSV bundle).
- `AlertsOverview.java` ("Download report bundle" link + `downloadDigestCsv('report')` path; `applyDigestRange`
  surfaces the 400 error in the note and leaves the view unpinned).
- `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `TESTING.md` (cases 540-542).

### Behavior change
- Additive and backward-compatible: the bundle gains a `snapshot` (existing `mute`/`history`/`audit` unchanged),
  a new overview link, and the picker now reports errors it previously swallowed (a UX improvement, same
  endpoints). The 3-arg `digestReportCsv` still works. No new config keys, no migration.

### Honest scope
Pure logic is unit-tested and runtime-verified (9 assertions): the 4-arg `digestReportCsv` emits an ordered
`# snapshot` section and the 3-arg form omits it; the overview renders the Download-report link resolving to the
digest-report endpoint; and `applyDigestRange` contains the `!x.ok` check, the error-message throw, and the
unpinned-on-error path. The rewritten `applyDigestRange` and the report download were additionally
**exercised with `node`** — a good range pins and shows the window, an inverted range surfaces the server's
validation message without pinning, and the report download builds the correct
`/admin/alerts/digest-report?format=csv` URL. The **bundle endpoint's actual JSON/CSV bytes and the live DOM
fetch/note behavior run against a live Spring context / browser — CI/boot-smoke-verified, not exercised
offline** (the composing CSV builder, the snapshot map, and the rendered JS are what's tested here); the
history/audit reads return data only against a real database (empty offline, as before).

### Testing
`./mvnw -Dtest=AlertDigestReportSnapshotDownloadValidationTest test`; full `./mvnw test`. Manual:

inline error with no pinned view. See TESTING.md cases 540-542.

author: alex-place
body:
## CSF-Omni — deterministic best-fit codec for CSF-Pack

Adds `src/csf/omni.py` and wires it into `csf_pack` as a 4th codec (`codec="omni"`) alongside `zstd`/`zlib`/`store`. Backward-compatible: v0.8 zstd/zlib/store archives still read byte-for-byte.

**What it is:** a best-fit engine that runs the whole panel (store/zlib/bz2/lzma/zstd/brotli + a byte-delta transform) per blob, round-trip-verifies each candidate, and emits the smallest behind a 7-byte self-describing **CRC-32** header. Deterministic (stable sort, identical bytes every run).

**Honest result (round-trip-verified, vs the shipped zstd-19):**
- Single streams: **+2.8% / +16.3% / +6.5%** (text+code / JSONL memory / cube-delta).
- Multi-file archive: only **+2%** over `zstd`+shared-dict (`use_dict=True`), at ~7x the encode — so **zstd stays the default**; omni is the opt-in max-ratio tier for single-stream cold/archival blobs.
- Upper envelope: beats every other codec on every stream, **ties** the brotli frontier within its header — it does **not** beat brotli's raw bytes (no PPMd/paq available; not fabricated).

**Safety/quality:** the CRC catches corruption a raw zstd/brotli frame returns silently; `portable=True` restricts to stdlib codecs. A 6-agent adversarial review found & fixed 2 defects (corrupt brotli → silently-wrong bytes → CRC + `ValueError` decode contract; a docstring over-claim → envelope wording). 153 CSF tests pass.

**Docs/report:** `docs/CSF-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION.md` §2.7.1 + the served report at `/reports/csf-compression-benchmark.pdf`.

**Tests:** `tests/test_csf_pack.py` — omni round-trip (parametrized), CRC integrity, payload-envelope.

author: ozzy-3
body:
## 目的

カバレッジを「計測のみ（advisory）」から **overall 閾値ゲート（enforce）** に引き上げる。`--no-verify` / Web 編集 / 自律 run でも回帰を CI で検知できるようにする。

Closes #258

## 実装上の重要な発見（方式変更の根拠）

当初は Bun 標準の `bunfig.toml` `[test] coverageThreshold` で済む想定だったが、**Bun 1.2.23 では overall 閾値ゲートとして機能しない**ことを検証で確認した:

| 形式 | 挙動 |
|---|---|
| per-metric object / sub-table（`{ line=.., function=.. }`, `[test.coverageThreshold]`） | parse はされるが **enforce されない**（function=0.999 でも EXIT 0） |
| scalar（`coverageThreshold = 0.9`） | **per-file 適用**。`src/index.ts`・`src/cli/commands/mcp-serve.ts` 等のエントリポイント（func ~0%）があるため、overall が 90/94 でも閾値 0.50 すら fail |
| lcov reporter | line カウントが text reporter（人間が見る値）と乖離（lcov line 47% vs text 94%） |

→ ネイティブ機構では「overall の floor」を表現できないため、**text reporter の `All files` 行を parse して overall の line/function を独立に判定する小スクリプト**でゲートする方式を採用した。

## 変更内容

- `scripts/coverage-gate.mjs`: `bun test --coverage` を実行し、出力（coverage 表は stderr）をそのまま通しつつ `All files` 行から overall の line/function を抽出して floor 判定。テスト失敗（非ゼロ終了）はそのまま伝播。floor は `COVERAGE_MIN_LINE` / `COVERAGE_MIN_FUNCTION`（percent）で上書き可。
- floor: **line ≥ 90% / function ≥ 87%**（実測 line 94.17% / func 90.27% の数 pt 下。routine churn で即赤にしない保守値。#260 のテスト強化後にラチェット）。
- `package.json`: `test:coverage` script 追加。
- `bunfig.toml`: 新規（`coverageSkipTestFiles = true`＋方式の経緯コメント）。
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`: `Test (with coverage)` を `bun run test:coverage` ゲートに置換。
- `AGENTS.md`: CI 品質ゲート節を更新（advisory → enforced、ローカル再現方法）。

## テスト計画 / 検証

- `bun run test:coverage` → green（`line 94.17% (≥ 90%), function 90.27% (≥ 87%)`）。
- ゲート発火確認: `COVERAGE_MIN_LINE=99 bun run test:coverage` → **EXIT 1**（floor 未達メッセージ）。
- `bun run typecheck` / `bun run lint`（biome）/ `bun run lint:md` すべて通過。
- pre-commit（taplo/actionlint/biome/yaml/markdownlint/gitleaks/trivy/commitlint）通過。

## フォローアップ

- #260（テスト手薄領域の強化）マージ後に floor をラチェット引き上げ（別 PR）。

body:
## Summary

Adds multi-team support on top of the previously single-team app. Teams run multiple seasons; each **team-season** has its own independent roster drawn from a **global player pool**, plus its own games and a manual depth chart. Players remain global identities (one player can be on many team-seasons, once per team-season).

## What's included

**Data model**
- New `Team` entity. `Season` gains `teamId`, an independent `roster` (global player IDs, deduped), and a manual `depthChart` (per field position, ordered; pitcher excluded). `AppSettings` gains `activeTeamId`.
- One-time, idempotent **migration**: wraps existing data into one team + one season (roster = all current players), runs on first read and on backup restore (v1 backups). Existing games keep their `rosterSnapshot`, so history is preserved. Deterministic active-season selection.

**API**
- New `/api/teams` and `/api/teams/[id]` routes (auth-gated like seasons). `teams` added to `/api/bootstrap`, `/api/state` export/restore, and `FullBackup` (v2).

**Store / UI**
- Team + season CRUD; roster add/remove (incl. adding from the global pool); nav **Team ▸ Season switcher** (switch-only); season rename; team/season management in **Settings**.
- New games snapshot the **active season roster** (lineups constrained to it).
- **Depth chart**: field-based per-position view reusing the lineup field style (no pitcher), with touch-friendly ▲/▼ reorder + desktop drag.
- Dashboard gains **Season vs Career** stat scope (derived purely from game participation).
- New **Players** master list page (global pool: CRUD, team-season memberships, add-to-season).

**Integrity & mobile**
- Deleting a season/team also deletes its games (no orphans). Removing a player prunes them from rosters and depth charts.
- Mobile fixes: touch reorder, Players table horizontal scroll, wrapping confirm rows, Team-card state re-sync on team switch.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run build` all pass.
- `npx vitest run` → **463/463 assertions pass** (3 files report a pre-existing Windows `EBUSY` temp-dir teardown flake in `afterAll`, also present on `master`; all assertions within pass). Added unit/integration coverage for team/season/roster/depth-chart store actions, the migration (fresh + upgrade paths), team API routes, and season-vs-career stat scoping.

author: blamechris
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 (client + protocol) of the identity-key rotation handoff (#5616). Today a legitimately-rotated daemon identity is indistinguishable from an attacker to a pinned client — both refuse + force a manual re-pair. Phase 1 (#5977) shipped the crypto (`signIdentityRotation`/`verifyIdentityRotation`) and the `tryRotationHandoff` decision tree, **but the clients never passed the cert into the decision**, so the handoff could never fire. This PR wires the transport → decision path so a pinned client can chain its pin forward when a valid continuity cert is presented.

The **server-side cert minting + presentation** (which carries genuine security-design decisions — rotation trigger, cert storage, single-hop vs chain) is split out to **#6198** for maintainer input.

## Changes

- **protocol** — add optional `newIdentityKey` + `rotationCert` to `ServerAuthOkSchema` (eager `auth_ok`; `key_exchange_ok` has no dedicated schema and is read raw). Dist rebuilt.
- **store-core** — surface both fields from `handleAuthOk` + `handleKeyExchangeOk` (same `typeof === 'string' && truthy → value, else null` validation as `serverKeySig`).
- **app + dashboard** — thread the two fields from the parsed handshake message through `verifyServerIdentityOrRefuse` → `decideKeyPinWithPairingIdentity`, on **both** the eager and discrete paths. The `rotate-pin` persistence already existed (#5978).

## Why this is safe

**Behaviour-preserving when no cert is present** (today, always): absent fields → `null` → `tryRotationHandoff` finds no cert → refuses, byte-identical to current behaviour. The change is purely additive and **fails closed** — it can only ever turn a refusal into a re-pin when a cryptographically valid cert + a live new-identity signature both verify (logic already audited + tested in #5977).

## Tests

Extended the store-core handshake-e2e harness (`fake-ws.ts` + `handshake.test.ts`) with a rotation matrix exercising the production decision path end-to-end:
- valid cert → **chains the pin forward** (re-pins to the new identity, no re-pair)
- **forged** continuity cert (attacker who never held the old secret) → refused
- **replayed** cert whose new identity did NOT sign the live exchange key → refused (liveness)
- pin already matches the current identity → cert ignored, plain connect
- un-rotated daemon with a genuine mismatch + no cert → still refused (manual re-pair)

Plus `handleAuthOk`/`handleKeyExchangeOk` parser unit tests for the new fields.

The harness's `handleAuthOk` + `rotate-pin` persistence were updated to mirror the real clients exactly, so the matrix runs the same decision + pin-write path production does.

## Verification

- store-core: **1714** pass (+ typecheck clean)
- protocol: **340** pass (+ typecheck clean)
- app: **2035** pass (+ typecheck clean)
- dashboard: **4030** pass (+ typecheck clean)

Related to #5616 (epic). Server-side produce half tracked in #6198.

author: gords2
body:
Fixes #1170.

`testCliCellAreaM2` runs:

```sh
test "`h3 cellAreaM2 -c 85283473fffffff | xargs printf '%.3f'`" = '265092558.128'
```

`printf`'s `%f` conversion uses the **system locale**'s decimal separator. On a locale such as `en_SE.UTF-8` (which uses `,`), the pipeline produces `265092558,128`, so the comparison against the expected `265092558.128` fails — which blocks the build (e.g. the Arch AUR package, as reported).

`h3` itself outputs the value correctly (`265092558.1282817721`); only the test's `printf` post-processing is locale-sensitive.

Fix: run `printf` under the C locale so the decimal separator is always `.`:

```diff
-"cellAreaM2 -c 85283473fffffff | xargs printf '%.3f'"
+"cellAreaM2 -c 85283473fffffff | xargs env LC_ALL=C printf '%.3f'"
```

`env LC_ALL=C` is used (rather than a bare `LC_ALL=C printf`) because `printf` is launched by `xargs`, which doesn't interpret `VAR=value` env assignments. This is the only CLI test fixture that uses `printf`, so no other tests are affected.

author: julianshen
body:
## What

Any canvas element now takes an optional **drop shadow** — a `shadow` object `{ color, blur, x, y }`, toggled and edited in the Properties panel (colour swatch + blur/X/Y). Works for shapes (box **and** clip-path polygons — unlike stroke), text, and images.

## How

- **Canvas** — a CSS `filter: drop-shadow` on the shared `base` style, so it applies to every element type and follows the *painted* shape (clip-path included, so a triangle gets a triangle shadow).
- **Gate** — validated as a nested object (`isShadow`: all of `color` hex / `blur` ≥0 / finite `x`,`y`, no extras).
- **Export** — a pptx outer `shadow`, derived from the same object: `x/y` → polar offset/angle (clockwise-from-east, matching `atan2` in screen coords), px → pt.

Single-sources the softness in `lib/elements.js`: `SHADOW_OPACITY` (a fixed soft alpha) + `dropShadowCss` (canvas filter) + `DEFAULT_SHADOW` (the toggle seed). 

**Opacity parity:** the canvas `opacity` style dims the *whole* element including the filter output, so the canvas shadow is `SHADOW_OPACITY × elementOpacity`. The export bakes the same factor into `shadow.opacity` (pptx has no element-wide opacity — fill, line, and shadow each carry their own), so the two match.

## Testing

TDD across all layers: `dropShadowCss` (elements), the nested gate validator (deckUtils), the drop-shadow filter on any element incl. clip shapes (SlideRenderer), the Props toggle + field edits (PropsPanel), and the pptx outer shadow with the opacity×opacity parity (pptxExport). body: Establishes a CI-runnable BASELINE for the GhosttyTerminalView (GTV) typing/render hot path so the god-file refactor (notably the planned handleAction inversion) can prove it did not regress frame/keystroke timing. Source changes plus a measurement test: 1. debug-log probe unmask: the DEBUG typing/turn probes emit per-event latency (elapsedMs/totalMs/turnMs/trackedMs) and the typing probes lead with path=. The redactor treated path= as sensitive and, because the numeric keys were absent from knownDebugFieldNames, swallowed every probe number as . Fixed by adding the probe value keys to knownDebugFieldNames and, for the three typing.* probe prefixes only, treating path= as a non-sensitive instrumentation identifier. Real filesystem path= is still redacted (covered by test). 2. handleAction dispatch timing: GhosttyTerminalView.handleAction RENDER/SCROLLBAR/CELL_SIZE cases are now timed (terminal.handleAction.) so the refactor inversion is measurable before/after. 3. DEBUG IME socket seam: debug.terminal.simulate_marked_text / simulate_unmark_text drive setMarkedText/unmarkText on the focused terminal view, so the IME hot path can be exercised deterministically from XCUITest (the socket text/key paths bypass NSTextInputClient). 4. GTVHotPathPerfUITests: launches a tagged DEBUG build with CMUX_KEY_LATENCY_PROBE=1 + tagged CMUX_DEBUG_LOG, creates a workspace, runs warmup + a keyDown burst (app.typeText), an IME burst, and a 4000-line render burst, then parses the tagged log and records median/p95/n per path, printing a JSON summary between GTV_PERF_BASELINE_JSON_BEGIN/END for recovery from CI logs. After recipe for the refactor: run this same test on the handleAction-invert branch and compare; pass = no statistically meaningful median/p95 regression (run-to-run noise established by running the baseline twice). Generated with Claude Code --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a CI-friendly performance baseline for `GhosttyTerminalView` typing and render hot paths. This lets us verify the upcoming `handleAction` inversion doesn’t slow keystrokes or frames. - **New Features** - Time `handleAction` dispatch for `RENDER`, `SCROLLBAR`, and `CELL_SIZE` as `terminal.handleAction.`. - Add DEBUG control socket seams `debug.terminal.simulate_marked_text` and `debug.terminal.simulate_unmark_text` to exercise IME paths. - Add `GTVHotPathPerfUITests` to run keyDown, IME, and 4000-line render bursts, parse the tagged debug log, and emit median/p95 JSON for paths like `terminal.keyDown`, `terminal.setMarkedText`, and `terminal.handleAction.*`. - **Bug Fixes** - Unmask typing/turn probe fields in the debug redactor: keep `path=` for typing probes and preserve keys like `elapsedMs`, `totalMs`, `turnMs`. Real filesystem `path=` remains redacted (with tests). - Refresh Swift file-length budget entries for touched files to satisfy CI. Written for commit 69c74dff120072243999adcf813370a5e39f6829. body:
## Problem
After PR #30 + #31, `/trends` rendered the summary but still returned **HTTP 500** once a real row existed. Root cause: the pipeline's `top_products` shape didn't match what the page reads.

- Pipeline wrote: `{slug, name, one_liner, primary_url, signal_count}`
- Page expects (`apps/web/lib/db.ts` `WeeklyTrendProduct` + `app/trends/page.tsx`): `{name, slug, platform, description, score}`

`PlatformBadge` calls `platform.slice(0, 2)`; with `platform === undefined` it throws during render → 500 (partial HTML still flushes, which is why the data was visible in the response body).

## Fix
Map `top_products` to the page contract. `platform` is the snake_case badge key the page colours by (`github` / `hacker_news` / `product_hunt` / `youtube` / `reddit` / `x`); `description` = `one_liner`, `score` = `signal_count`.

## Follow-up after merge
Re-run the `Weekly Hot Trends` workflow so the stored row is rewritten with the correct shape (upsert on `week_start`), then confirm `/trends` is 200.

author: drysius
body:
## Bug: `call(v => console.log(v))` / `ee.on(ev, v => console.log(v))` bailava

O arrow capturava `console` e a análise de captura não o reconhecia como não-captura → "expression arrow". Causa: o **caminho de disco** (`module_entry`, usado por `rts run`/`test`) computava `ambient_fns` de `prelude.funcs` **só** (funções), omitindo os singletons top-level do prelude (`const console = new Console()`). O caminho single-string já usava `prelude_fn_names` (que inclui esses via SHAPE scan).

## Fix
`module_entry` passa a usar `super::prelude_fn_names(p)` (tornado `pub(super)`) — a **mesma** do outro caminho. Adiciona os `const x = new C()` singletons do prelude ao set ambiente → um arrow callback lendo `console` é tratado como referência top-level (resolve via gcell), não captura unsound. Data-driven, sem name list.

## Validação
- Repro: `call(v => console.log(v))` → 7; EventEmitter com **arrow** listener `ee.on("x", v => console.log("arrow", v)); ee.emit("x", 9)` → `arrow 9` (combina com o callback bridge #1703).
- suíte `measure_new`: **346 → 349** (+3).
- `cargo test -p rts-codegen-new`: **736 → 737**; gate sem HARD; zero regressão.

Desbloqueia o padrão ubíquo de arrow callback com `console` + arrow listeners de EventEmitter.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.14.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.14.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some messages were being written to stdout, making ``coverage json -o
  -`` useless for capturing JSON output. Now messages are written to stderr,
  fixing `issue 2197`_.

- Fix: ``CoverageData`` kept one SQLite connection per thread that recorded
  coverage, but never closed them when those threads terminated. On long runs
  with many short-lived threads this leaked one file descriptor per dead
  thread, eventually failing with ``OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files``.
  Connections belonging to terminated threads are now closed and dropped.
  Fixes `issue 2192`_.  Thanks, `Matthew Lloyd <pull 2193_>`_.

- Fix: when using sys.monitoring, we were assuming we could use the
  ``COVERAGE_ID`` tool id.  But other tools might also assume they could use
  that id.  Pre-allocated ids don't really make sense, so now we search for a
  usable one instead. Fixes `issue 2187`_.

- Following `the advice of cibuildwheel <no-13t_>`_, we no longer distribute
  wheels for Python 3.13 free-threaded.

.. _issue 2187: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2187
.. _issue 2192: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2192
.. _pull 2193: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2193
.. _issue 2197: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2197
.. _no-13t: https://py-free-threading.github.io/ci/#building-free-threaded-wheels-with-cibuildwheel

.. _changes_7-14-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the HTML report used typographic niceties to make file paths more
  readable by adding a small amount of space around slashes. Those spaces
  interfered with searching the page for file paths of interest. Now the report
  uses CSS to accomplish the same visual tweak so that searches with slashes
  work correctly. Closes `issue 2170`_.

- `Add a 3.16 PyPI classifier <hugo-316_>`_ since we test on the 3.16 main
  branch.

.. _issue 2170: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2170
.. _hugo-316: https://mastodon.social/hugovk/116588523571204490


.. _changes_7-14-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Feature: now when running one of the reporting commands, if there are
  parallel data files that need combining, they will be implicitly combined
  before creating the report. There is no option to avoid the combination; let
  us know if you have a use case that requires it.  Thanks, `Tim Hatch
  <pull 2162_>`_. Closes `issue 1781`_.

- Fix: the output from ``combine`` was too verbose, listing each file
  considered. Now it shows a single line with the counts of files combined,
  files skipped, and files with errors. The ``-q`` flag suppresses this line.
  The old detailed lines are available with the new ``--debug=combine`` option.

- Fix: running a Python file through a symlink now sets the sys.path correctly,
  matching regular Python behavior. Fixes `issue 2157`_.

- Fix: ``Collector.flush_data`` could fail with "RuntimeError: Set changed
  size during iteration" when a tracer in another thread added a line to the
  per-file set that ``add_lines`` (or ``add_arcs``) was iterating. The values
  passed to ``CoverageData`` are now snapshotted via ``dict.copy()`` and
  ``set.copy()``, which are atomic under the GIL. Thanks, `Alex Vandiver <pull
  2165_>`_.

- Fix: the soft keyword ``lazy`` is now bolded in HTML reports.

- We are no longer testing eventlet support. Eventlet started issuing stern
  deprecation warnings that break our tests. Our support code is still there.

.. _issue 1781: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1781
.. _issue 2157: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2157
.. _pull 2162: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2162
.. _pull 2165: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2165


.. _changes_7-13-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.5
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: `issue 2138`_ describes a memory leak that happened when repeatedly
  using the Coverage API with in-memory data. This is now fixed.

- Fix: the markdown-formatted coverage report didn't fully escape special
  characters in file paths (`issue 2141`_). This would be very unlikely to
  cause a problem, but now it's done properly, thanks to `Ellie Ayla
  <pull 2142_>`_.

- Fix: the C extension wouldn't build on VS2019, but now it does (`issue
  2145`_).

.. _issue 2138: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2138
.. _issue 2141: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2141
.. _pull 2142: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2142
.. _issue 2145: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2145


.. _changes_7-13-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.4
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the third-party code fix in 7.13.3 required examining the parent
  directories where coverage was run. In the unusual situation that one of the
  parent directories is unreadable, a PermissionError would occur, as
  described in `issue 2129`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: in test suites that change sys.path, coverage.py could fail with
  "RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration" as described and fixed in
  `pull 2130`_. Thanks, Noah Fatsi.

- We now publish ppc64le wheels, thanks to `Pankhudi Jain <pull 2121_>`_.

.. _pull 2121: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2121
.. _issue 2129: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2129
.. _pull 2130: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2130


.. _changes_7-13-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: in some situations, third-party code was measured when it shouldn't have
  been, slowing down test execution. This happened with layered virtual
  environments such as uv sometimes makes. The problem is fixed, closing `issue
  2082`_. Now any directory on sys.path that is inside a virtualenv is
  considered third-party code.

.. _issue 2082: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2082


.. _changes_7-13-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: when Python is installed via symlinks, for example with Homebrew, the
  standard library files could be incorrectly included in coverage reports.
  This is now fixed, closing `issue 2115`_.

- Fix: if a data file is created with no read permissions, the combine step
  would fail completely. Now a warning is issued and the file is skipped.
  Closes `issue 2117`_.

.. _issue 2115: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2115
.. _issue 2117: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2117


.. _changes_7-13-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Added: the JSON report now includes a ``"start_line"`` key for function and
  class regions, indicating the first line of the region in the source. Closes
  `issue 2110`_.

- Added: The ``debug data`` command now takes file names as arguments on the
  command line, so you can inspect specific data files without needing to set
  the ``COVERAGE_FILE`` environment variable.

- Fix: the JSON report used to report module docstrings as executed lines,
  which no other report did, as described in `issue 2105`_. This is now fixed,
  thanks to Jianrong Zhao.

- Fix: coverage.py uses a more disciplined approach to detecting where
  third-party code is installed, and avoids measuring it. This shouldn't change
  any behavior. If you find that it does, please get in touch.

- Performance: data files that will be combined now record their hash as part
  of the file name. This lets us skip duplicate data more quickly, speeding the
  combining step.

- Docs: added a section explaining more about what is considered a missing
  branch and how it is reported: :ref:

author: ohah
body:
## 의도

[config GUI](../blob/main/docs/config-gui.md) **S0-1b** — 즉시-저장 세팅 GUI의 write-back 토대. 사용자가
세팅 화면에서 필드를 바꾸면 **그 키만** config 파일에 즉시 반영해야 한다(결정: 즉시 저장, config-gui §10).
현재 사이드바 ⚙ 토글이 2키를 하드코딩으로 쓰던 걸 **임의 키로 일반화**한다.

## 구현

- `src/config/serialize.zig`: `updateForKeys(original, config, keys) -> []u8` — 넘긴 키들의 **현재 값만**
  `configKeyValues`(스키마 직렬화 단일 출처)에서 골라 `updateConfigText`로 부분 갱신. **override-only by
  construction** — 넘긴 키만 쓰므로 기본값 40개를 파일에 안 쏟고, 주석·다른 줄·미파싱 키는 보존. `configKeyValues`에
  없는 키(`keybind`·`theme.preset`·오타)는 `valueForKey` null이라 스킵(호출처 자체 직렬화).
- `src/config.zig`: `updateConfigForKeys` 재출력.
- `src/platform/macos/app_session.zig`: `serializeSidebarConfig`를 `updateForKeys`로 재구현 — `bool→"true"/"false"`
  손코드 중복 제거. **출력 byte-identical**(같은 2키·같은 값·같은 `updateConfigText`)이라 사이드바 ⚙ 토글 동작 보존.
  GUI(CS-4-5)도 같은 경로(바뀐 필드의 키를 넘김).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHANGE["GUI/⚙ 토글: 키 K 변경"]
  CFG["Config(K 갱신)"]
  UFK["updateForKeys(original, config, [K])"]
  CKV["configKeyValues(config) → valueForKey(K)"]
  UCT["updateConfigText(original, {K: value}) — 부분 갱신"]
  FILE["config 파일 (K만 갱신, 나머지·주석 보존)"]
  CHANGE --> CFG
  CFG --> UFK
  UFK --> CKV
  CKV --> UCT
  UCT --> FILE
```

## 설계 결정: 즉시-저장 = per-key (full-config diff 아님)

원래 S0-1b 계획은 "전체 config override diff"(기본값 위 + 원본에 있는 키)였으나, **즉시-저장**(각 변경이 그 키를
바로 씀, 사이드바 ⚙와 같은 결)으로 결정돼 **per-key가 더 맞다**: 변경 키만 쓰면 override-only가 자동이고, 전체 diff·
revert stale-line·dirty 비트마스크가 불필요하다. 코드도 더 작다.

## 문서 정합성

- `docs/settings-page.md` S0-1b 행·`docs/config-gui.md` §7/§8: per-key(`updateForKeys`)로 ✅ 갱신.

## clean-room 근거

- maru 자체 직렬화 위에 얇은 일반화. 외부 참조 없음. VT/renderer 변경 없음 — N/A.

## 전략 영향 평가

- 동작 보존: 사이드바 write-back 출력 byte-identical(같은 2키). 손코드 중복(bool→문자열) 제거로 단일 출처 강화
  (스키마 직렬화가 값을 정함). config는 forgiving·SSOT=파일 유지. 의존성 추가 없음.

## 테스트

author: stanleyrya
body:
This change addresses an issue where the `endDate` of events spanning midnight were incorrectly pushed backward by exactly 24 hours during ICS-to-JSON parsing. The root cause was that `Intl.DateTimeFormat` configured with `hour12: false` in `en-CA` locale formats midnight as `24:xx` (h24) instead of `00:xx` in newer Node.js versions. This caused `new Date(..., 24, ...)` to wrap to the next day when calculating the `provisionalUTC` difference, incorrectly subtracting 20 hours instead of adding 4. Changing `hour12: false` to `hourCycle: 'h23'` guarantees a 00-23 format and correct UTC offsets.

## Summary

- Adds a lock/unlock toggle (🔒) to the AI Analysis panel in the artwork detail view — fields are read-only by default and require a deliberate unlock → edit → Save flow
- User edits (`artist`, `year`, `medium`, `school`, `description`, `wikipedia_url`) are stored in a separate `user_meta` key alongside `ai_meta`, so AI re-analysis never overwrites manual entries

## Key design decisions

- **Separate storage** (`user_meta` vs `ai_meta`): eliminates the re-analysis conflict entirely — AI always writes to `ai_meta`, users always write to `user_meta`, they never collide

- **404 on unknown IDs**: endpoint now returns 404 for content IDs not in `artwork_meta.json` instead of silently creating empty entries
- **Server response as source of truth**: `saveRename()` and `saveMetaEdit()` update in-memory state from the server response rather than manually reconstructing it

author: colonelpanic8
body:
## Problem

Speed-flip detection was failing badly in two directions, and the root cause was the same: it gated on the **velocity impulse** of the dodge, which is estimated by subtracting boost compensation from the velocity delta — an estimate that's noisy and, on real speed flips, frequently reads *backward*.

- **Recall:** on a replay recorded as ~all speed flips, the detector found **0 of 40**. At supersonic speed a dodge can't add forward velocity, so the `forward_delta ≥ 80` gate, the backward impulse, and a `cancel_score` that's low for real flips all rejected genuine speed flips.
- **Precision:** on a confounder replay, the leftover signals were too blunt.

## Approach: rotation only

A speed flip is a *cancelled diagonal dodge that air-rolls flat*. Its defining traits are all in the car's **orientation trajectory**, which boxcars gives reliably — no impulse estimate needed:

1. **Cancel** — the nose doesn't pitch over (`max_forward_rotation ≤ 45°`).
2. **Inverts but recovers** — the air-roll sweeps the up-vector past horizontal but **stops short of going fully end-over-end** (`max_up_rotation ∈ [90°, 170°]`). Confounders (full barrel rolls / uncancelled flips) carry all the way to ~180° and are rejected. The evaluation window is extended to 0.50s so the roll plays out.

All velocity/impulse gates are removed.

## Results on the labelled fixtures

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Recall (all-speed-flip drill) | 0 / 40 | **26 / 37 non-wavedash dodges** |
| Precision (confounder replay) | 25 FPs* | **1 FP** |
| Reviewed clip fixtures | pass | **pass** |

\*after the rotation-only rewrite but before the inversion gate; the original impulse-gated detector got few FPs only because it rejected almost everything.

The ~11 recall misses are mostly `max_forward_rotation > 45°` — uncancelled/flubbed flips, correctly rejected.

## What's in the PR

- **`DodgeRotation` on `DodgeEvent`** — every dodge now carries its orientation-trajectory features (onset pitch/roll/yaw, nose-pitch dip, up-vector inversion) over a 0.45s window. Boost-independent, and the basis for classifying any dodge.
- **Rotation-only speed-flip detection** — the rewrite above.
- **Two labelled fixtures + `movement_dodge_audit`** — a zero-speed-flip (confounder) replay and an all-speed-flip drill, pinned by whole-replay precision/recall tests (`#[ignore]`'d: full-replay/slow, run with `--ignored`). The audit tool dumps every dodge's features as a labelable TSV.

## Caveats

- The `170°` inversion threshold is **tuned on these two replays** — it's a real improvement on what we can measure, but generalization needs validation against real-game replays (drills overlap too much to push further without overfitting; a `cancel_score` second gate reached 0 FP but broke confirmed flips, so it was dropped).
- Three obsolete impulse-based unit tests are `#[ignore]`'d; rotation-based side-flip/wavedash rejection is follow-up work.
- The precision/recall fixtures are currently RED-by-design (1 FP, recall below the aspirational bar) — they're the targets to drive toward, not yet green.

author: fudster
body:
Closes #12793. Follow-up from #11930.

Stale Forgejo LFS objects accumulate on the 50Gi Longhorn PVC, and reclaiming disk needs **two layers** — deleting LFS objects (ext4 frees inodes only) and then a filesystem trim to unmap the freed blocks from the volume. Without both, GC "succeeds" while disk usage stays flat. PR #12892's `git_gc_repos` cron is git repo GC, not LFS, and does nothing for the block-reclaim layer.

## Changes

**Forgejo** (`apps/kube/forgejo/application.yaml`)
- Add scheduled `[cron.gc_lfs]` (`@every 168h`, `OLDER_THAN = 168h`) alongside the existing `git_gc_repos`; bump `config-revision`.

**Longhorn** (`apps/kube/storage/manifests/`)
- New `recurring-jobs.yaml`: `forgejo-filesystem-trim-weekly` (Sun 03:00) + `forgejo-snapshot-weekly` (Sat 02:00, retain 2), scoped to a dedicated **`forgejo-reclaim` group**.
- `removeSnapshotsDuringFilesystemTrim: true` in `values.yaml` — global equivalent of per-volume `unmapMarkSnapChainRemoved=enabled`, so trim also reclaims space trapped in the snapshot chain (the ~18.5 GiB stuck case in #11930).
- Wire `recurring-jobs.yaml` into the kustomization.

**Docs** (`apps/kube/forgejo/README.md`)
- GC → trim → verify `actualSize` runbook + the volume-label binding step.

## Verified against the live cluster (`admin@kbve`, Longhorn v1.9.1)
- RecurringJob CRD **v1beta2** is the served/storage version → manifest uses it.
- Setting key **`remove-snapshots-during-filesystem-trim` exists** (was `false`) → `values.yaml` key is valid.
- PVC `gitea-shared-storage` → volume `pvc-0d5edbf3-…` (matches the issue), actualSize ~9.2 GiB.
- `kubectl kustomize apps/kube/storage/manifests` renders both RecurringJobs.
- **Scoping label applied** to the forgejo volume: `recurring-job-group.longhorn.io/forgejo-reclaim=enabled`.

## Design call — scoped, not cluster-wide
Longhorn auto-labels **every** volume into the built-in `default` group (confirmed: ~46 volumes, incl. 200–322 GiB DB volumes, several near capacity). A `default`-group snapshot/trim would fan out cluster-wide — a weekly snapshot of all DB volumes is real overhead and risk, counterproductive for a space-reclaim ticket. So the jobs target a dedicated `forgejo-reclaim` group bound only to the LFS volume.

**Trade-off (hidden state):** the group binding is a label on the CSI-created Volume CR, so it lives outside git and must be re-applied if the PVC is recreated. There's no clean GitOps-native way to scope a recurring job to one dynamically-named volume without minting a dedicated StorageClass (which would require recreating the 50Gi PVC). Documented in `recurring-jobs.yaml` + the README runbook; the label is already applied on the live cluster.


## Deferred scope

Cluster-wide `filesystem-trim` (other ~45 volumes incl 200–322Gi DBs) is intentionally **out of scope** here — tracked in #12915. This PR proves the GC→trim→reclaim loop on the single Forgejo LFS volume first to avoid I/O risk on database volumes.

author: mattwoolly
body:
## What

Task **137** (`tag: cmake_formats`) — refine `cmake/Formats.cmake`'s per-platform format resolution + the configure-time "no unvalidated artifact" validator gate, and register the `cmake_formats_*` configure-time ctests so the §2.2 F-1..F-8 / ADR-011 C1-C8 / ADR-024 contract is **asserted**, not merely hoped.

This is a **CMake configure-time** change. Its coverage is the configure-time `cmake_formats` ctests, NOT a Catch2 `-R <tag>` selector — no fake Catch2 test was added for a cmake-only change.

## Changes (`cmake/Formats.cmake` only, plus the task frontmatter)

Per the EDIT WAIVER: only the gate side Formats.cmake consumes was touched. `cmake/Validators.cmake` (task 138) and `mw_validator_wired`'s interface are **untouched**; `core/`, `plugin/`, and the labels snapshot are **untouched**.

- **`(format,platform)->validator` map**: removed dead-code in the VST3 branch and traced the sparse §2.1 matrix — VST3 needs `pluginval` everywhere + Steinberg `validator` on macOS only; AU = `auval`+`pluginval` (macOS-only, F-3 FATAL elsewhere); CLAP = `clap-validator`; Standalone = `standalone-smoke`; LV2 = `lv2lint`+`lv2_validate` (Linux + `MW_BUILD_LV2`, F-6).
- **Per-platform DEFAULT sets** made explicit + traced (macOS VST3+AU+CLAP+Standalone; Linux VST3+CLAP+Standalone +LV2 when `MW_BUILD_LV2`; Windows VST3+CLAP+Standalone). An unrecognized host now defaults to the **empty** set rather than silently claiming Windows'.
- `mw_resolve_formats` gate semantics, the F-4 (AAX) FATAL, and the report's stable `platform=`/`resolved=` lines are **unchanged** — the report only gains appended columns. The ADR-011 gate is not weakened.
- **New `cmake_formats_*` configure-time ctests** (silent-pass rule; the task's tag word):
  - `cmake_formats_resolved_<platform>` — POSITIVE: resolved set obeys F-1..F-8 and every resolved format's required validator is wired (ADR-011 C5).
  - `cmake_formats_reject_au_off_macos` / `_aax` / `_force_unwired` — NEGATIVE: re-run the **real** gate from a child `cmake -P` and pass only when it `FATAL_ERROR`s (F-3 / F-4 / F-5).

## Validators are UNWIRED locally BY DESIGN

The validators (pluginval / auval / Steinberg `validator` / clap-validator / lv2lint+lv2_validate) are **not installed** on this dev box — that is the ADR-011 "no unvalidated artifact" gate working as intended. Locally only `standalone-smoke` is fully wired, so the gate hard-removes VST3/AU/CLAP and resolves to `STANDALONE`. (`auval` itself is found on macOS, but AU still hard-removes because it also requires `pluginval`, which is absent.) In CI, the wired validators let the rest flow through.

## Verification (real pasted output)

```
$ export CPM_SOURCE_CACHE=$HOME/.cache/CPM

author: magyargergo
body:
## Problem

`gitnexus analyze --pdg` aborts at the end ("Saving metadata..." ~98%) with:

```
double free or corruption (out)
[1]  ... IOT instruction  gitnexus analyze --pdg
```

This is native heap corruption (glibc SIGABRT) — pure JS can't double-free.

## Root cause

LadybugDB is single-writer and its `Connection` is **not safe for concurrent query execution**. Two things issue queries on the same module-singleton `conn` during analyze:

- the **WAL-checkpoint driver** (`wal-checkpoint-driver.ts`) on a 5s `setInterval` → `conn.query('CHECKPOINT')`, and
- the analyze **pipeline** holding that same `conn` for a long COPY.

`--pdg` adds the `BasicBlock` + `REACHING_DEF / CDG / POST_DOMINATE / TAINTED / CALL_SUMMARY / TAINT_PATH` tables, so a COPY outlasts the 5s tick. The checkpoint then runs concurrently with the in-flight COPY on one connection → two libuv workers mutate shared native state → heap smash (caught at a later `free()`, hence "at 98%"). Without `--pdg` the writes finish inside the tick window, so the overlap rarely fires.

## Fix

- New `src/core/lbug/conn-lock.ts` — `withConnLock`, a promise-chain mutex.
- Every singleton-`conn` helper now runs its full query **+ result drain** inside the lock: `queryAndDrain` (when `targetConn === conn`), `executePrepared`, `executeWithReusedStatement`, `flushWAL`, `tryFlushWAL`, `getLbugStats`, `deleteAllInterprocTaintPaths`, `deleteAllCallSummaries`.
- `if (inflight) return` reentrancy guard in the driver `tick()` so overdue ticks can't stack checkpoints.
- `streamQuery` is intentionally **not** wrapped (read path; its per-row callback can re-enter the adapter, and the driver is inactive there).

## Reproduction & validation

- **Repro:** concurrent `conn.query(bigWrite)` ∥ `conn.query('CHECKPOINT')` on one raw `@ladybugdb/core` connection → native crash; the *identical* workload serialized → stable.
- **Fix validated end-to-end:** drove the same overlap through the real locked adapter (init + real WAL driver + write ∥ 2×CHECKPOINT) — clean.
- New unit tests: `conn-lock.test.ts` (no overlap / FIFO / throw-releases) and `wal-checkpoint-driver-reentrancy.test.ts` (mock + fake timers). Existing `lbug-load-overlap*` + `lbug-adapter-wal-schema` + `analyze-wal-checkpoint-failure` still pass.

> Note: `@ladybugdb/core` 0.17.1 also segfaults on its own "Maximum database size reached" (16 GiB) error path — a separate latent native bug, orthogonal to this crash (worth a follow-up issue).

body:
## What

`min_length` is only enforced for `ResBody::Once` and `ResBody::Chunks`, whose total length is known before compression. For streaming bodies (`ResBody::Hyper` / `ResBody::Stream`) the length is unknown, so they are compressed unconditionally — meaning a tiny streamed body can still end up *larger* once `Content-Encoding` and framing overhead are added.

This was undocumented and surprising. Added a note to both the `min_length` field and the `min_length(..)` setter explaining the limitation. Docs only — no behavior change (buffering a stream just to measure it would defeat streaming).

author: auser
body:
## Summary

Plan 200 dependency/budget-gates slice: a new `xtask check-duplicate-majors` gate.

A duplicate major — one crate resolved at two semver-incompatible versions — compiles both copies into the build: more build time, more shipped code, and two incompatible copies of a type across the dependency graph. The OCI/TLS stack is the standing offender (`http`/`hyper`/`reqwest`/`base64` 0.x↔1.x); de-duplicating it is an open dependency-roadmap goal (rehomed from Plan 126). This gate stops the set from **growing** while that work proceeds, and ratchets down as duplicates are removed.

- Reads `cargo metadata --locked` (the full resolved graph, deterministic from `Cargo.lock` regardless of host), groups packages by name, and flags any name with two or more semver-incompatible compatibility keys (major for `>=1.0`, minor for `0.x`).
- Fails on any duplicate-major **not** in a committed 42-crate `ALLOWLIST` baseline seeded from today's tree. Removing an entry is free (the gate flags stale entries as a ratchet-down hint); adding one must be justified in the PR.
- Pure compat-key / detection / regression / stale-entry logic is unit-tested (8 tests). Wired into the CI **Lint** lane next to `check-closure-budget`.

Marks the Plan 200 dependency/budget-gates rollup box partial (`[~]`): binary-size budget (needs a release build to measure), the OCI/TLS dedup itself (blocked on the `oci-client`/`reqwest`/`aws-lc-rs` decision), and the remaining cleanup items stay open.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p xtask` — 148 tests pass (8 new).
- `cargo run -p xtask -- check-duplicate-majors` → `clean (42 known duplicate-major crates, all allowlisted)`.
- `cargo fmt -p xtask -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

author: jl-calda
body:
## What

Expands the engine-native function library (Phase 2 refinement) with five spreadsheet-style families, registered **engine-wide** on the shared mathjs instance so they work in **both** worksheet math regions and table cells:

| Family | Functions |
|---|---|
| **Math** | `ROUNDUP` `ROUNDDOWN` `MROUND` `CEILING` `FLOOR` `INT` `QUOTIENT` `SUMSQ` `SUMPRODUCT` |
| **Statistical** | `COUNT` `COUNTA` `COUNTIF` `SUMIF` `AVERAGEIF` `GEOMEAN` `HARMEAN` `LARGE` `SMALL` |
| **Logical** | `IF` `IFS` `SWITCH` `IFERROR` `IFNA` (lazy) · `AND` `OR` `NOT` `XOR` |
| **Text** | `LEN` `LEFT` `RIGHT` `MID` `UPPER` `LOWER` `PROPER` `TRIM` `SUBSTITUTE` `FIND` `SEARCH` `CONCAT` `TEXTJOIN` `REPT` `VALUE` |
| **Date** | `DATE` `YEAR` `MONTH` `DAY` `WEEKDAY` `EDATE` `EOMONTH` `DAYS` `DATEDIF` `DATEVALUE` |

## How / key decisions

- **`table.ts` vs `math.ts`:** the card said "engine-native in `table.ts`", but `table.ts` is the spreadsheet-cell *evaluator* — the real function library is the shared mathjs instance in `math.ts`. Per discussion, the families register there via `registerLibraryFunctions(math)` (alongside `matrix.ts`/`iterators.ts`). One registration reaches both worksheet regions and table cells, so nothing is injected into the table scope (no duplicate wiring). **`graph.ts` and `recalc.ts` are untouched.**
- **UPPERCASE Excel-style names** so mathjs's lowercase builtins (`round`, `mod`, `and`, `or`, `concat` = matrix concat, `mean`, …) stay 100% intact — the same "new names, not overrides" rule the ∑/∏/∫ operators followed.
- **Lazy logicals via `rawArgs`:** `IF/IFS/SWITCH/IFERROR/IFNA` evaluate their argument nodes lazily against the call scope (proven `iterators.ts` mechanism), so the untaken branch isn't computed and `IFERROR` can catch a throw (unit mismatch, undefined name).
- **Pure & deterministic:** everything is sync, no I/O. Dates are serial numbers computed from explicit args via `Date.UTC` — **no `TODAY()`/`NOW()`** (a clock read would break the determinism tests). Text casing is locale-independent.
- **Unit-aware where meaningful:** math rounding rounds the magnitude and reattaches the unit; `SUMSQ`/`SUMPRODUCT`/`SUMIF`/`AVERAGEIF`/`GEOMEAN`/`HARMEAN` flow units through; text/date are dimensionless.

## Files

- New: `lib/calc/functions/{shared,math,statistical,logical,text,date,index}.ts` (+ adjacent `*.test.ts`) — pure factories that take the `math` instance (cycle-free).
- Edited: `lib/calc/math.ts` (wire `registerLibraryFunctions`), `lib/calc/reference/functions.ts` + `reference/tree.ts` (representative catalog entries + new "Date & time" category), `DECISIONS.md`.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` ✓  ·  `npm run lint` ✓  ·  `npm run build` ✓
- `npm test` ✓ — **698 passed** (70 files), incl. 43 new function-family tests and the reference-catalog integrity/anti-drift checks (every new worked example evaluates live).

author: amerenda
body:
## Summary

Adds two synthesis-enforcement stages to the LiteLLM pre-call hook, which fire before the existing orphan-cleanup and context-budget stages:

**Stage -1 (signal, ≥5 tool calls):** Appends a hard directive to the last tool result message — `[SYSTEM: You have now made N tool calls. DO NOT call any more tools. Write your final answer now.]` — so the model can't reason past the system-prompt limit.

**Stage -1b (force, ≥8 tool calls):** Strips `tools` and `tool_choice` from the request entirely, making it physically impossible for the model to call more tools.

## Why hook-level instead of system prompt only

System prompt guidance (`"after 5-6 tool calls, STOP"`) was already in place but the model reasoned through it — Qwen3-35B-think kept making 12-15 tool calls on research prompts, eventually hitting a 400 context overflow. The hook modifies the actual request payload, which is authoritative.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `stress_tool_calling.py --stress repeat --repeat-n 3` — verify 9/9 pass, finish=stop
- [ ] Send the K8s MCP research prompt to OWU → should synthesize after ≤8 web searches

author: feruzm
body:
## Problem

On the login dialog's **Choose Extension** picker, clicking **Hive Keeper** did nothing but spin, never opened the Keeper extension, and after 60s showed an `Extension request timed out. Please try again.` toast.

## Root cause

Keeper is the only extension that has adopted the Hive Unified Wallet Protocol: it owns `window.hive`, flags itself with `window.hive.isKeeper`, and registers a `com.ecency.keeper` entry in `window.hive.providers[]`.

The web app resolved/detected Keeper by gating on `window.hive_extension`. Keeper sets that flag **only in its content-script (isolated) world**, so it is never visible to page scripts. That made the direct branch dead code and forced Keeper resolution through the providers registry, whose instance did not round-trip the sign callback. The result was a 60s hang with no popup.

`window.hive_extension` is also not reliable for detection, so a Keeper-only browser additionally surfaced a phantom **Keychain** row (Keeper aliases itself onto `window.hive_keychain` for backward compatibility).

## Fix

- Resolve and detect Keeper via the page-visible `window.hive.isKeeper` flag, targeting the live `window.hive` object directly (the instance Keeper wired its own response listener to). Use the providers registry only as a fallback for when another wallet owns `window.hive`.
- Drop every reliance on `window.hive_extension` (`getHiveKeeperInstance`, `getDetectedExtensions`, `hasAnyHiveExtension`, and the `hasKeyChain` gate in `global-module`).
- Suppress Keeper's `window.hive_keychain` self-alias so it no longer appears as a separate Keychain choice (a real Keychain never sets `isKeeper`).
- Type `window.hive` as `HiveWalletApi` (`isKeeper`/`providers`) and document that `hive_extension` is not page-visible.

No extension changes are required: the Keeper extension implements the protocol correctly (providers registry, `extension_id` routing, and the `extension_id` validation whitelist are all present). This was an integration issue on the web side.

## Tests

- 4 regression tests: Keeper signs through the live `window.hive` rather than a stale providers entry, `isKeeper` detection, and the self-alias dedupe.
- Full web suite passes (1610 tests). No new type errors in the changed files.

## Note

Bug reported alongside this (broken Keychain logo in the picker) was a transient 429 on the static asset host, not a code issue (`images.unoptimized` serves the asset directly).

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
`syncAgentServiceBinding` always threw `agentGatewayConfig.getForAgent is not a function` in production, so agent→provider bindings were never written to `unigateway.toml` (and the recently added `provider_not_found` warning never surfaced). Root cause is a CommonJS circular `require` resolved in the wrong order.

The two modules require each other at load time:

```
admin/AgentGatewayConfig.js   --require-->  llm/agentServiceSync.js
llm/agentServiceSync.js       --require-->  admin/AgentGatewayConfig.js
```

`server.js` loads `AgentGatewayConfig` first. While it is still mid-load (its `module.exports` not yet assigned), it requires `agentServiceSync`, which requires `AgentGatewayConfig` back and captures its **empty** exports object. `AgentGatewayConfig` later replaces `module.exports` wholesale, so `agentServiceSync`'s captured reference stays empty → `agentGatewayConfig.getForAgent` is `undefined`. The throw was swallowed by the best-effort `try/catch` in `setForAgent`, so the failure was silent.

Fix: drop the top-level require in `AgentGatewayConfig` and require `syncAgentServiceBinding` lazily at its single call site, so resolution happens at call time when both modules are fully initialized.

```diff
-const { syncAgentServiceBinding } = require('../llm/agentServiceSync');
 ...
 if (saved?.llm_auth_mode === 'gateway' && saved.provider) {
+    const { syncAgentServiceBinding } = require('../llm/agentServiceSync');
     try {
         sync = await syncAgentServiceBinding(agentId);
```

Verified by loading the modules in production order (`AgentGatewayConfig` first) and calling `syncAgentServiceBinding('kimi-code')` with `NODE_ENV=production`:
- before: `THREW -> agentGatewayConfig.getForAgent is not a function`
- after: runs normally (`{synced:false, reason:"missing_config"}` — the expected no-toml path, not a crash)

## Purpose

The agent-registry external (`git@github.com:stevencarpenter/agents.git`) is actively curated, so
a weekly `refreshPeriod` left local agents stale for too long. Drop it to hourly so `chezmoi apply`
picks up registry changes within the hour.

## Change

`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` — agent-registry `refreshPeriod` `168h` → `1h`. The `tpm` external is
left at `168h` (stable upstream plugin; no reason to re-pull it more often).

Reminder baked into the comment: `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals` forces an immediate pull right
after pushing a registry change, regardless of the period.

## Scope / impact

- Affects only machines with capability `agents = true` (currently `personal-mac`).
- Trade-off: re-pulls the registry on any `chezmoi apply` where the cache is >1h old (adds a brief
  SSH `git pull`); applies within the hour still use the cache.
- Independent of #102 (that fixes the install invocation in the post-apply hook; different file).

## Verification

- `chezmoi execute-template --file .chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` → renders `1h` for agent-registry,

author: nickcrew
body:
## Summary

A design note defining the vocabulary and the core quality mechanic behind every
AI-action button: **Generate / Sharpen / Refresh / Start over / Deepen** (+ a
deferred **Refine → Polish** rename). Docs-only — no code changes. It is the spec
that #31 ("standardize AI-action button styling and labels") implements.

The load-bearing idea: AI operations on an artifact are **three distinct
generation modes**, not one re-run verb — distinguished by what prior content is
in the model's context and *how it is framed*:
- **Sharpen** (the default) shows the prior draft as *external* work to critique,
  with authorship hidden — the model evaluates it with critical distance instead
  of defending its own output. This is the "see yourself, sharpened" mechanic.
- **Start over** generates from scratch (heavy, rare).
- **Refresh** folds an upstream change into the existing draft (edit-preserving).

It also separates the **quality axis** (which mode runs) from the **safety axis**
(version history + rollback), so the user controls outcomes by *time-travel after
the fact*, not by picking the mechanic up front (which would be a false choice).

## Why

#31 framed this as one re-run verb with inconsistent paint. The audit
(below) shows the real problem is that semantically different operations share —
or randomly diverge in — label and style. Defining the verbs first means the
styling pass repaints *correctly-labelled* buttons instead of freezing the
current confusion in a shared component.

## Alternatives considered

- **Skip the note, just restyle (the literal #31).** Rejected: would standardize
  the paint while leaving "Regenerate" on buttons that should be "Sharpen", and
  bake in the from-scratch-vs-critique conflation.
- **Two verbs (Deepen + one re-run word).** Rejected after the behavioral
  definition landed: Refresh (content-in-context) and Start over (from-scratch)
  are different generator calls, and blind-critique (Sharpen) is a third — three
  modes are real, not vocabulary bloat.
- **Expose the mode as a user choice.** Rejected: false choice — users pick the
  "safe"-feeling option and forfeit the quality mechanic. Version-history rollback
  is the safety net instead.

## Verification

Docs-only; no build/test impact. Content grounded against the code:
- Audit citations (~45 buttons / 14 files) were agent-gathered then
  mechanically verified; color and verb misclassifications corrected.
- Snapshot claims checked against `resumeStore`/`coverLetterStore`/`pipelineStore`
  and ADR-0005 (apply-time immutability ≠ revision history).
- `Button` primitive `primary` = neutral (`--text-primary`), confirming no AI
  treatment exists today.

```
markdownlint / link check: n/a (no CI doc linter configured)
```

## Risk & blast radius

None at runtime — adds one design note + one NAVIGATOR row. Risk is only that the
spec is wrong; this PR exists to review it before any code moves.

## Open questions / follow-ups

- Version-history **scope** (which artifacts) and **retention** (N revisions vs
  time window) — net-new, touches persistence tiers.
- Which surfaces get **Refresh** vs Sharpen-only.
- **Sharpen icon** — reuse `Sparkles` or a dedicated mark.
- Implementation splits into Tier 1 (vocab + the shared `ai` Button variant, onto
  the M12 waves) and Tier 2 (the Sharpen critique generator path, version history,
  Refine→Polish). To be filed as follow-ups once the spec is agreed.

Refs #31

author: trilamsr
body:
## Summary

`scripts/check-stale-refs.sh` over-flags when a deleted file's stem is itself a tracked file. Deleting a suffixed variant — e.g. `regatta.yaml.operator-runtime` (stem `regatta.yaml`) or `foo.yaml.bak` (stem `foo.yaml`) — made the gate grep `\b(basename|stem)\b`, so every legitimate reference to the live `regatta.yaml` was reported as stale, blocking the deletion with a false positive.

Fix: in the basename-vs-stem branch, skip the stem when it names a still-tracked file. The stem only widens the grep when it does NOT resolve to a tracked path — preserving the original script-stem case (delete `foo.sh`, flag bare `foo` refs) the feature was designed for.

```
if [ "$bn" = "$stem" ] || git ls-files --error-unmatch "$(dirname "$f")/$stem" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  pattern="\\b${bn}\\b"
else
  pattern="\\b(${bn}|${stem})\\b"
fi
```

`$(dirname "$f")` yields `.` for root-level files, so the probe becomes `./stem` — handled correctly.

closes MAY-260

## TDD (RED first)

Two commits, RED-test-first:
1. `test:` — adds `run_case_keep` helper + Case 5 (suffixed-variant deletion must spare the live stem ref → expect pass) + Case 6 (non-tracked stem still flags). Pre-fix Case 5 FAILS:

```
FAIL suffixed-variant deletion spares live stem ref: want exit=0 got=1
     | check-stale-refs: stale references to deleted files detected:
     |   --- foo.yaml.bak ---
     |   ./docs/notes.md:1:See foo.yaml for config.
     |   ./foo.yaml:1:kept content of foo.yaml
check-stale-refs_test: 1 failed, 5 passed
```

2. `fix:` — applies the tracked-stem skip. Post-fix all 6 cases pass:

```
check-stale-refs_test: all 6 case(s) passed
```

Case 6 (delete `foo.sh`, stem `foo` not tracked, bare `foo` ref remains → still exit 1) proves the legit stem-match the feature was built for is unaffected.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/check-stale-refs_test.sh` → all 6 pass (exit 0).
- `make check` → green for this change. One unrelated flake (`TestServe_AuthzPolicyHotReload_OnSIGHUP`, a 5s SIGHUP log-needle timeout in `cmd/regatta`) passed on isolated re-run; cannot be affected by a shell-gate edit.
- Self-check: gate run against this PR's own worktree → `no file deletions in PR diff` (this PR deletes nothing, so it is clean against itself).

## A+ rubric scorecard

| # | Row | Self-rating | Note |
|---|-----|-------------|------|
| 1 | Correctness | A | Root-cause fix; tracked-stem probe via `git ls-files --error-unmatch`. |
| 2 | TDD / test order | A+ | RED test committed first (`c75c1ee`), fix second (`0f791f1`); RED output captured above. |
| 3 | Edge cases | A | Root-level files (`dirname`→`.`), `bn==stem` short-circuit, non-tracked stem still flags. |
| 4 | Deletion / footprint | A | +1 condition, no new files beyond a test helper; no new deps. |
| 5 | Comments WHY-not-WHAT | A | Single WHY comment explaining the suffixed-variant false-positive. |
| 6 | Naming / clarity | A | `run_case_keep` mirrors existing `run_case`. |
| 7 | Security | A | No untrusted input path change; same grep surface. |
| 8 | Docs | A | Algorithm comment block unchanged; behavior is narrower, not new vocabulary. |
| 9 | CI gate hygiene | A | Gate passes on itself; co-located `_test.sh` extended. |
| 10 | Reproducibility | A+ | Each case stands up a throwaway repo; deterministic. |

```release-notes
[FIX] check-stale-refs no longer flags live references to a file when a suffixed variant sharing its stem is deleted (MAY-260)
```

이전 시도들(hide/show, 화면밖 park, opacity)이 전부 borderless 스카이림 위로 못 올라갔습니다.

## 핵심 통찰
아바타 오버레이가 되는 이유: **시작 시 화면 안에 만들어진 투명·topmost 창이 절대 숨겨지거나/화면밖으로 가거나/opacity가 바뀌지 않음** — 그냥 그 자리에 떠 있고, **렌더러가 내용을 그리고/지움**.

## 수정 (오버레이와 동일 라이프사이클)
- 메인은 창을 시작부터 **화면 안 + 보임 + topmost('screen-saver') + 클릭통과**로 유지. 게임이 전체화면 되기 전에 top band 선점 후 절대 hide/move/opacity 안 함.
- **카드의 표시 여부는 렌더러가 소유**: 메인이 `quickchat:opened`/`quickchat:dismissed`만 보냄 → `QuickChatApp`이 summon 중에만 카드를 그림(아니면 완전 투명 root).
- summon: `setIgnoreMouseEvents(false)` + `moveTop` + `focus`. dismiss(blur/Esc/전송): `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)`. hide/move/opacity 없음.
- preload에 `quickChat.onDismissed` 추가.

이건 오버레이의 라이프사이클을 **그대로** 복제한 것이라, 오버레이가 뜨는 조건(borderless/창모드 전체화면)이면 같이 떠야 합니다. (독점 전체화면은 여전히 인젝션 필요.)

author: kapil971390
body:
## What

`DirNames` in `lib/fs/basicfs.go` called `os.OpenFile` directly, bypassing the `BasicFilesystem.OpenFile` wrapper where `alwaysOpenFlags` (`O_NOFOLLOW` on Unix) is applied.

A symlink whose final path component points to a directory would be silently followed by `DirNames`, listing the target directory's contents — inconsistent with the hardening introduced for `Open`/`Create` in #10739.

## Why

`alwaysOpenFlags = syscall.O_NOFOLLOW` (Unix) is defined in `basicfs_unix.go` and applied at line 252 of `basicfs.go` inside `OpenFile`. Any method that calls `os.OpenFile` directly bypasses this flag.

## Fix

Route `DirNames` through `f.OpenFile` instead of `os.OpenFile`. The explicit `f.rooted()` call is also removed since `f.OpenFile` already calls it internally.

```diff
-func (f *BasicFilesystem) DirNames(name string) ([]string, error) {
-	name, err := f.rooted(name)
-	if err != nil {
-		return nil, err
-	}
-	fd, err := os.OpenFile(name, OptReadOnly, 0o777)
+	fd, err := f.OpenFile(name, OptReadOnly, 0o777)
```

## Testing

- Existing `TestDirNames` tests continue to pass
- On Unix: `DirNames` on a path whose final component is a symlink-to-directory should now return `ELOOP` or `ENOTDIR` instead of silently listing the symlink target

Identified via static analysis of the diff introduced by #10739.

author: slepp
body:
## Summary

`hew_datetime_now_nanos` maintained its own private `static EPOCH: OnceLock<Instant>`, initialised independently of the process-wide monotonic epoch in `hew_runtime::monotonic`. The datetime clock and every runtime subsystem (timer, scheduler, crash, supervisor, swim) were therefore not guaranteed to share epoch zero, making cross-subsystem time deltas unreliable.

`hew_datetime_now_nanos` now returns `hew_runtime::monotonic::monotonic_ns() as i64` directly. The private epoch is removed. `hew-std` already carried a path dependency on `hew-runtime`, so no new crate edge is introduced. The `i64` cast is annotated with `#[expect(clippy::cast_possible_wrap)]` and the ~292-year rationale.

The `LESSONS.md` P0 `monotonic-epoch-single-clock` row is strengthened to cover the cross-crate case: trigger now catches per-module `static EPOCH`, apply mandates the shared accessor, with the `MetricsRing.epoch` instance-local dashboard field as the documented exemption.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p hew-std`: 631 passed
- `cargo test -p hew-runtime`: 2308 passed
- `now_nanos_shares_the_runtime_process_epoch`: passes on fold-in; fails with `hew_datetime_now_nanos read 120ns, below the 20000000ns slept` when the private-epoch body is restored — assertion has teeth
- `tests/hew/datetime_test.hew`: 5/5
- `tests/hew/instant_methods_test.hew`: 5/5
- Preflight: ready-to-push

## Out of scope

No changes to `hew-runtime/src/monotonic.rs` itself — the runtime module landed in a prior consolidation pass and is unchanged here. No other stdlib time functions were touched.

Fixes #2060
