author: linuxdynasty
body:
## Summary
Fixes #3378. `GET /api/v0/services/{service_name}/story` hung past the 60s curl budget at 900-repo scale (481,728 graph nodes), breaking the console Service Story tab (it surfaced the aborted fetch as a misleading "unauthenticated" error).

## Root cause
`go/internal/query/service_story_seam.go` → `enrichServiceQueryContextWithOptions` (shared by service story and service context) calls `loadUncorrelatedCloudResourceCandidates` whenever a service has no materialized `cloud_resources` — the common case at scale. That function used an **unlabeled anchor**:

```cypher
MATCH (n)
WHERE (n:CloudResource)
  AND (coalesce(n.name,'') CONTAINS $query OR ... 11 more predicates ...)
ORDER BY n.name
LIMIT $limit
```

On NornicDB an unlabeled `MATCH (n)` is not pushed down to a label scan, so the planner scanned **all 481,728 nodes**, evaluated a 12-way `CONTAINS`/`=` predicate per node, and sorted the entire matched set by name **before** `LIMIT` applied. That whole-graph scan is the dossier hang. All other story/context graph queries are already `Repository{id}`/`Workload{id}`-anchored; this was the only unbounded one.

## Fix (root cause, not a blanket timeout)
- Anchor the CloudResource label in the MATCH pattern (`MATCH (n:CloudResource)`) so the scan is bounded to the label population — the shape the static query-plan gate (`hot-cypher.yaml`) already enforces by rejecting unlabeled anchors. The result set is byte-identical (same predicates, projection, ordering, bound), so candidate truth is preserved.
- Over-fetch one row beyond the service-story item limit (50) so the handler surfaces `uncorrelated_cloud_resources_truncated` instead of silently capping (Eshu truncation-truth rule). The stage timer now also emits a `truncated` boolean.

## Tests (TDD: failing first, then fix)
- `TestCloudResourceCandidatesUseInfraSearchSourceFields` — asserts the labeled MATCH anchor, rejects `MATCH (n)` / `WHERE (n:CloudResource)`.
- `TestCloudResourceCandidatesOverfetchToDetectTruncation` — asserts limit+1 over-fetch and explicit truncation.
- Updated `TestLoadUncorrelatedCloudResourceCandidatesUsesBoundedServiceSelector` and the three `TestEnrichServiceQueryContextKeeps*AWSCloudResourceAnchorAsCandidate` fakes to track the new shape.

## Verification
- `go test ./internal/query -run 'ServiceStory|Story' -count=1` → 180 passed
- `go test ./internal/query -count=1` → 3094 passed
- `go test ./cmd/api ./internal/mcp -count=1` → 638 passed
- `go vet ./internal/query` → clean
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/query` → clean
- `scripts/verify-query-plan-regression.sh` → pass
- `scripts/verify-performance-evidence.sh` → pass (evidence note added to `docs/public/reference/cypher-performance.md`)
- `git diff --check` → clean

## Notes / scope
- No live PROFILE: no local NornicDB-New checkout is present, so per `cypher-query-rigor` this is documented as a no-regression-by-construction shape fix (all-node scan strictly removed). Recommend an operator PROFILE before/after on a production-cardinality stack to confirm wall-clock.
- The console "map timeout/abort to explicit 'timed out' state" ask (#3378 ask 2) is a frontend change and is **out of scope** for this backend PR.

author: vampik33
body:
## Problem

When the nightly-develop orchestrator failed to dispatch `dev-publish.yml` to a repo (e.g. `greentic-llm`, whose `develop` branch lacked the caller → `gh workflow run` 404), the run only showed the generic:

```
✗ greentic-llm — dispatch failed
```

The actual reason was **swallowed**. `dispatch()` is invoked as `run_id=$(dispatch "$full")`, which captures its **stdout**. The `err()` helper echoed its `::error::…` annotation to stdout, so the real messages emitted inside `dispatch()` —

- `Failed to dispatch dev-publish.yml in <repo>: <reason>` (line ~234)
- `Timed out detecting dispatched run for <repo>` (line ~252)

— were captured into the `run_id` variable and discarded (the caller ignores the value on failure). They never reached the job log.

## Fix

Route `err()` and `warn()` to **stderr**:

```sh
err()  { echo "::error::$1" >&2; }
warn() { echo "::warning::$1" >&2; }
```

- GitHub Actions parses `::error::`/`::warning::` workflow commands from **both** stdout and stderr, so the annotations still render.
- stderr isn't captured by the `$(dispatch …)` substitution, so the real error now appears in the log.
- `warn()` gets the same treatment — semantically correct (warnings → stderr) and pre-empts the identical latent bug if it's ever called from a captured context. `log()` stays on stdout (it drives the tier progress display, which is intentionally captured-free).

`mint_token_for_org`/`ensure_token_for_org` already use `>&2`; this aligns the two general helpers with that convention.

Verified with `bash -n`. Surfaced while diagnosing the 2026-06-21 nightly failure.

body:
## Summary
Builds on the NovaOS Desktop companion app with two new apps, a big browser
performance pass, and several bug fixes. 10 commits; no kernel changes.

## New apps
- **Browser** (`apps/browser.py`): address bar, back/forward/reload/home, search.
  Uses Qt WebEngine (Chromium) automatically **if installed**, otherwise a
  built-in lite engine (requests/urllib + QTextBrowser) that loads real pages.
  Clean, parsed DuckDuckGo search results (real URLs unwrapped from DDG redirects).
- **Network** (`apps/network.py`): a **sandboxed** Wi-Fi manager + a live taskbar
  indicator. It is virtual — turning Wi-Fi off / connecting / disconnecting only
  affects NovaOS Desktop (gates the Browser) and **never touches the host's real
  Wi-Fi** (no `nmcli radio/connect/disconnect`; read-only scans only).

## Browser performance
- Two-phase load: text paints immediately, images fill in afterward
  (time-to-first-text on a heavy Wikipedia page: **12.56s → 0.69s**).
- Pooled keep-alive connections via `requests` (no TLS handshake per image).
- Strips `<script>/<style>/<svg>` and caps document size for fast layout.
- In-memory LRU caches (pages + images) → instant back/forward & revisits.

## Fixes
- Desktop icon labels were clipped — panel now sizes to content.
- Crash when closing the Browser/Network window mid-load (signal emitted on a
  deleted C++ object) — background threads now emit safely.
- Start menu "Log out" → "Power off".
- WebEngine-ready: `AA_ShareOpenGLContexts` set before the QApplication.

## Notes
- For full CSS/JS pages, install `python3-pyqt5.qtwebengine`; the Browser then
  auto-switches to Chromium with no code changes. The lite engine is the
  zero-dependency fallback.

## Test plan
- `cd desktop && ./run.sh` — open apps from desktop icons / Start menu.
- Browser: load a site and search; back/forward; close mid-load (no crash).
- Network: toggle Wi-Fi off → Browser shows offline; host Wi-Fi stays connected.
- Headless smoke: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 -m novaos_desktop --selftest`.

author: roeap
body:
## What

Move the Unity Catalog DDL statement types + planner out of `deltalake-datafusion` and into `datafusion_unitycatalog::sql` (merged as [unitycatalog-rs#199](https://github.com/unitycatalog-incubator/unitycatalog-rs/pull/199)), where they sit next to the managed-write and catalog-resolution primitives they already depended on.

## Why

The UC DDL layer already depended inward on `datafusion_unitycatalog::managed` and `unitycatalog-client` — it was a SQL/planner skin over `datafusion-unitycatalog` hosted in the wrong repo. Co-locating it makes `datafusion-unitycatalog` the single home for the UC↔DataFusion integration and removes a cross-repo dependency edge. The managed `CREATE TABLE` path is now an intra-crate call there.

## What stays in `deltalake-datafusion`

- The `HFParser` SQL front end and the Delta `VACUUM` command — `VACUUM`/`OPTIMIZE` are Delta-table maintenance, not Unity Catalog concerns.
- The parser imports the UC statement types from `datafusion_unitycatalog::sql` and `deltalake_datafusion::sql` **re-exports** them, so the host keeps a single SQL facade.

## Blast radius

- **Hydrofoil: no source changes** — the re-export facade preserves all `deltalake_datafusion::sql::{...}` imports.
- **Cedar policy layer: no changes** — it matches the extension node purely by its `name()` / `fmt_for_explain` string contract, which is preserved and pinned by a test in `datafusion-unitycatalog`.
- `unitycatalog-*` deps pinned to merged rev `fc17c0c`; now-unused deps dropped from `deltalake-datafusion`.

## Validation

- `datafusion-unitycatalog` sql module: 8 passed (incl. Cedar-contract test)
- `datafusion-cedar`: 30 passed
- `deltalake-datafusion`: 5 passed (parser + VACUUM round-trips)

author: jensholdgaard
body:
## RFC 0017 green `.1` — audit leaf creation (`TemplateChange::Created`)

First green slice of RFC 0017. A read-time template registry (`.2`) must recover a leaf's **version-1** tokens after the originating rows age out, but the miner never audited initial leaf creation — only widenings. This adds the missing event.

### Changes
- **`ourios-core`** (`audit.rs`): new `TemplateChange::Created { new_version, new_template }`; `event_kind` ordinal **6** / `event_type` `template_created` — **append-only** per RFC 0005 §3.7 (existing `0`–`5` unchanged, old readers tolerate via the `Unknown` path). Not a merge.
- **`ourios-parquet`**: writer maps `Created` to `(new_version, new_template)` with `old_version`/`old_template` **NULL** (no prior template); reader handles `Created` *before* the `old_*` requires (which would reject those NULLs for the widening kinds). Writer→reader round-trip test added.
- **`ourios-miner`** (`cluster.rs`): `create_new_leaf` emits `Created` (canonical tokens via `format_template`) on the same `AuditSink` / WAL-before-ack path as the widening events — covering both the fresh-leaf and lossy-zone allocation sites.

### Contract change (explicitly surfaced)
RFC 0017 §3.1 **supersedes RFC0001.1** ("fresh-leaf creation does not emit an audit event"). Leaf creation now emits a `template_created` event. It remains a **non-merge** (`merges_total` unchanged), so RFC 0001's merge-counting contract is untouched. The RFC0001.1 acceptance test (`rfc_internal.rs`) is overturned to assert the amended contract; the amendment is recorded in RFC 0017 §1.

Widening/type-expansion/rejection tests now filter the leading `Created` event (`drain_changes` helper / inline filters) so they stay decoupled from the per-leaf creation count — **not** a weakening: the creation contract has dedicated coverage (`fresh_leaf_emits_created_event` + the RFC0017.1 acceptance tests).

### Tests
- Fills the RFC0017.1 red stubs (core append-only schema; miner emit) and removes their `#[ignore]`.
- Adds the `Created` Parquet round-trip.
- All `ourios-core` / `ourios-parquet` / `ourios-miner` tests green locally; `cargo fmt --check` + `clippy -D warnings` clean.

Next: `.2` (`derive_template_registry`).

author: dieterolson
body:
💡 What: Implemented a fast path for XML string escaping during custom recursive serialization and utilized `.extend()` on list buffers.
🎯 Why: Profiling revealed that standard library `xml.etree.ElementTree._escape_attrib` and `_escape_cdata` functions account for a disproportionate amount of time during MJCF serialization. Since typical MJCF structures do not frequently contain special characters that require XML escaping (like `<`, `&`, `\n`), unconditionally invoking the standard library escaping function for every string introduces significant unnecessary processing overhead.
📊 Impact: Reduced the `_fast_serialize_node` execution time from ~3.13ms to ~2.47ms during serialization.
🔬 Measurement: Run `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_benchmarks.py --benchmark-only -o addopts=""` to verify build performance.

author: riox432
body:
Closes #967

## Summary
Replaces the dead-end Android update flow (which only opened the GitHub release **web page**, forcing the browser to be the install source) with a proper **in-app self-update** using the platform-native `PackageInstaller` Session API. The repository already computed the direct `.apk` URL (`UpdateResult.downloadUrl`) but the UI never used it — now the "Download" button downloads, verifies, and installs the APK with CivitDeck itself as the install source.

Scope is **Android only**; Desktop/iOS are unchanged. No `commonMain` / shared-VM changes.

## Approach (researched + Codex-reviewed)
Per the design review, the Activity-bound install flow is kept out of `core-domain` (no `expect/actual` `AppInstaller`) — the shared `UpdateViewModel` stays discovery-only. New Android-local pieces in `androidApp/.../ui/update/`:

- **`ApkInstaller`** — downloads the APK to app-private cache (`HttpURLConnection`, no new dependency), integrity-verifies it, and commits a `PackageInstaller.Session` (`MODE_FULL_INSTALL`).
- **`UpdateInstallController`** — state machine (`Idle/Downloading/Verifying/NeedsUnknownAppsPermission/Installing/Success/Failed/Cancelled`) + one-shot effects; folds the `PackageInstaller` `IntentSender` broadcast (runtime receiver, `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED`) back into state. No Activity reference.
- **`UpdateInstallHost`** — owns the Activity-bound mechanics: launches `ACTION_MANAGE_UNKNOWN_APP_SOURCES` (re-checks permission on return) and the system install confirmation; renders the progress/error dialog.

Manifest: adds `REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES` (Play policy is inapplicable — GitHub-only distribution). `release.yml` now publishes a `*.apk.sha256` checksum asset.

## Integrity / security
- Verifies the downloaded APK's **package name** matches and its **signing certificate set matches** the running app (defends against a swapped APK even if release metadata were tampered with).
- Accepts APK Signature Scheme **key rotation** (single-signer lineage) to avoid false negatives.
- Rejects **downgrades / equal builds** (`longVersionCode` check).

## Codex review applied
- Block back/outside dismissal of the dialog mid-install (was unregistering the receiver and dropping the terminal `STATUS_*`).
- Re-throw `CancellationException` (no longer mis-reported as a download failure); download runs under `runInterruptible(Dispatchers.IO)` so it's cancellation-cooperative.
- Handle `trySend` failure for the confirmation effect.
- Added version-code downgrade check + key-rotation lineage acceptance.

## Verification
- `./gradlew :androidApp:assembleDebug` — green
- `./gradlew detekt` (root, all modules) — green
- No shared/feature/core/iOS/Desktop modules touched, so their CI jobs are unaffected.

## Notes / follow-ups
- The published `*.apk.sha256` asset is not yet consumed at install time — the signing-cert check is the stronger primary gate; wiring optional checksum verification through `UpdateResult` is a possible follow-up.
- Silent self-update is intentionally not attempted (not reliable for a normal sideloaded app); each install shows the system confirmation, as expected for GitHub-Releases distribution.

## Summary
This trims two small but high-confidence large-cluster hot paths: topology no longer re-lists Argo Rollouts once per Service, and resource detail activity requests are scoped to the resource name server-side instead of fetching kind+namespace history and filtering in the browser. Because the timeline store now filters by name before applying endpoint limits, busy namespaces are less likely to starve a resource detail page of that resource’s own events.

- Reuses the Rollouts already fetched during topology construction by indexing them by namespace before Service selector matching.
- Adds `name` support to `/api/changes` by threading it into the existing timeline `QueryOptions.Names` filter.

author: kevinhirsch
body:
## Summary

Seven targeted a11y and content fixes from J4 specialist consolidation (5 read-only specialists × J4 telemetry). All are source-level fixes with no runtime dependencies or design changes.

- **J4-08 (LAUNCH-BLOCKING)** `orwellDecision.js`: Add `confirmLabelFor(kind, binding)` helper and use it in the catch block. Previously, a failed submit on a `self-evict` card would restore the confirm button to `"Confirm — this is binding"` instead of `"Confirm — leave the game (final)"` — silently dropping the irreversibility signal at the most consequential decision in the game (WCAG 4.1.2).

- **J4-09 (HIGH)** `orwellDecision.js`: Pre-declare the `.odec-err` container with `role="alert" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true"` during `render()` instead of dynamically injecting it in the catch block. Dynamic live-region injection is unreliable across AT/browser pairs (WCAG 4.1.3).

- **J4-10 (HIGH)** `orwellDecision.js` + `style.css`: `.odec-err` now uses `var(--color-error, var(--red))`. Added `--color-error: #b83245` in `:root.light` — fixes the 3.0:1 contrast failure on white (#e06c75 on #fff). Dark theme unaffected (~5.7:1). (WCAG 1.4.3)

- **J4-11 (HIGH)** `orwellDecision.js`: Dismiss `×` button gets `min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;`. Previously 32×31px — below the project's 44×36 coarse-pointer floor and WCAG 2.5.5 enhanced target. (WCAG 2.5.5 / 2.5.8)

- **J4-12 (HIGH)** `orwellDecision.js`: `card.setAttribute("aria-describedby", CARD_ID + "-note")` + `note.id = CARD_ID + "-note"`. SR users now hear the decision context + the "your selection only" / irreversibility instruction when focus lands on the card, before tabbing into options. (WCAG 4.1.2)

- **J4-13 (POLISH)** `orwellDecision.js`: "Just color" (film/TV production jargon for "presentational only") → "No stakes here" in the non-binding comp-round note. First-time players and non-native English speakers misread "just color" as a literal color reference.

- **J4-14 (POLISH)** `orwellSeasonProgress.js`: `aria-description` (draft ARIA 1.3, inconsistent AT support) → `aria-describedby` + visually-hidden `<span>` with the same description text (WCAG 1.2-safe approach).

**J4-22/25 closed:** error button inconsistency and visual dismiss size were duplicate findings merged into J4-08 and J4-11 respectively.

## Test plan

- [x] `frontend/tests/test_j4s5_decision_card_a11y.py` — 13 new source-pinned checks covering all 7 fixes
- [x] Full FE suite: **1814 passed** (0 failures, 0 regressions vs 1785 baseline before J4 set #4 + the 13 new J4 set #4 tests + 13 new J4 set #5 tests)

author: kadyapam
body:
## Summary

Fixes the deterministic `commands=0` wedge surfaced in `pft_flow_test`
(noetl/ai-meta#120). The fan-in / reduce barrier (this repo's #142)
defers a multi-upstream target until every statically-declared upstream
is terminal. For an **open / asymmetric loop join** — a back-edge
`U -> T` whose forward return path is absent, so `T` does NOT
forward-reach `U` — the static `build_incoming_arcs` back-edge filter
cannot strip `U` (structurally the arc is indistinguishable from a
genuine fan-in). `U` never runs on the taken path, so the barrier
defers **forever**.

`pft_flow_test`'s `setup_facility_work` has in-degree 2 (`start` +
the never-taken `load_next_facility` cursor back-edge) → after `start`
completes the drive returns `commands=0` every poll and never
dispatches the next step. Shared `orchestrate-core`, so the in-server
drive and the off-server / plugin drive wedge identically.

## Fix

At barrier-check time, count an upstream as a *pending* dependency
only if it is **live on the current path**:
- done / skipped are already filtered (terminal),
- an upstream that is not in-flight **and** not forward-reachable from
  any live step (running steps + the step driving this pass + steps
  entered earlier in this pass) can never run → must not block.

New `live_reachable` helper computes the frontier-reachable set.
`build_incoming_arcs` and the static back-edge filter are unchanged
(still correct for closed loops); the runtime liveness check is what
distinguishes an open back-edge from a genuine fan-in. Genuine
fan-in (a live parallel branch still running or reachable from one)
and closed loops are unaffected.

## Tests

- New `test_open_loop_back_edge_does_not_block_dispatch` (sibling to
  `test_build_incoming_arcs_excludes_loop_back_edge`): the target of
  an open back-edge dispatches once its real upstream completes; also
  pins that the static helper still keeps the arc (can't strip it).
- `cargo test --lib`: 133 pass, 0 fail. `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean.
- Existing genuine-reduce (`test_reduce_step_*`) and closed-loop
  (`test_build_incoming_arcs_excludes_loop_back_edge`,
  `test_fan_in_convergence_is_not_treated_as_loop_back`) tests stay green.

## Kind validation (prod-exact gate: PUBLISH_ONLY=true / STATE_BUILDER=server / PLUGIN_DRIVE=true)

Image built with this fix, loaded into kind, server rolled (worker kept
at v5.40.2 / 119-rehydrate; the rebuilt orchestrate wasm is re-seeded
on server boot). 2×2 minimal variants (all with the `batch_slots`
iterable):

| Variant | back-edge | construct | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V4 neither | ✗ | ✗ | COMPLETE | COMPLETE (2.0s) |
| V1 back-edge only | ✓ | ✗ | **WEDGE** | **COMPLETE (2.0s)** |
| V2 construct only | ✗ | ✓ | COMPLETE | COMPLETE (8.1s) |
| V3 both | ✓ | ✓ | **WEDGE** | **COMPLETE (8.1s)** |

Spot-checks stay green: `fanout_reduce_phase6`, `pagination/cursor`,
`pagination/basic`, `loop_test`. `pft_flow_test` now dispatches
end-to-end (start → setup → process → validate → check_results — no
wedge). Cutover invariants on real runs hold: roots=1, dangling=0,
walk==rows (single unforked chain), terminals=1, catalog_zero=0,
`__orchestrate__` event rows=0, materializer sole writer.

Refs noetl/ai-meta#120

author: mohsen1
body:
Goal: green

## Summary
A `readonly` (incl. `static readonly`/`protected readonly`) class property in an ambient context (`declare class` / `.d.ts`) may carry a literal initializer, matching tsc. tsz emitted a spurious `TS1039` ("Initializers are not allowed in ambient contexts") for **every** initialized ambient class property.

Structural rule: When a class property in an ambient context has an initializer, tsc accepts it without error if the property is `readonly` and the initializer is a string/numeric/negated-numeric literal; a `readonly` property with a non-literal initializer is `TS1254`; a non-readonly property is `TS1039`. tsz now applies the same rule in the class-property grammar check (`crates/tsz-checker/src/state/state_checking_members/ambient_signature_checks.rs`), mirroring the existing ambient-*variable* logic.

## Root cause
The class-property check emitted `TS1039` whenever `initializer.is_some() && (has_declare || in_declared_class)`, with no `readonly`/literal gating. The correct logic already existed for the variable path in `statement_checks.rs` (`is_const + is_valid_const_initializer -> TS1254 else TS1039`); this reuses its `is_valid_const_initializer` helper (made `pub(crate)`).

## Verification
- Boundary probe matches tsc 6.0.3 exactly:
  - `static readonly A = "x"`, `readonly B = 1`, `readonly E = -1` → accepted (was 3× false `TS1039`).
  - `static prefix = 5` (non-readonly) → `TS1039`.
  - `readonly D = 1 + 2` (readonly, non-literal) → `TS1254`.
- `cargo test -p tsz-checker --test ambient_readonly_literal_initializer_tests` — 4 passed (positive + the two negative controls + a binder-name variation).

Discovered via a differential canary sweep on ts-morph (`packages/ts-morph/src`), which uses `static readonly` literal members in ambient declarations. Reduces false-positive churn (Fast-adjacent per #14102).

## Summary

PR #720 merged at 6957f68 but GitHub's 3-way auto-resolution kept master's old `.gitignore` content instead of the cherry-picked patterns from commit 90fb8d0 (which added `_claude_run_secret*.txt` and `.tmp_local_secrets/`). This follow-up restores the leak-vector patterns as a single focused commit.

## What this restores

- `_claude_run_secret*.txt` — wildcarded so variants like `_claude_run_secret_v2.txt` or `_claude_run_secret.env.txt` are excluded, not just a single literal filename.
- `.tmp_local_secrets/` — transient operator secret scratchpad convention.

The existing `bandit-report.json` exact match (already on master) covers the static-analysis output; no broader pattern was added to avoid overmatch.

## Why a follow-up PR

PR #720 is already merged at 6957f68. Amending the merged PR would require revert + re-merge, which is non-trivial on the GitHub side. The cleanest path is this focused single-file PR.

## Why this PR should not auto-conflict on the rebase

The change is purely additive — two lines appended at the END of `.gitignore`. Master does not currently have these patterns, so the follow-up PR vs master is non-conflicting for the auto-resolver.

## Verification after merge

On master:
```
git check-ignore _claude_run_secret.txt _claude_run_secret_v2.txt .tmp_local_secrets/x
```
all three should print the path (i.e. be ignored).

## Security note

A Personal Access Token was previously pasted into this PR description and has been **redacted**. Redaction does not undo exposure — that token MUST be rotated at https://github.com/settings/tokens regardless of merge state.

author: mickzijdel
body:
## Summary

Grid layouts should rely on the container's `gap` for spacing between items rather than margins on the items themselves. While auditing every grid in the codebase, I found the uneven gaps that appear on mobile (and at the end of a desktop column) come from grid items carrying their own margins instead of using `gap`.

The main culprit is `CardComponent`, which hard-codes a default `mb-4`. When a card is placed directly as a grid item — especially with `h-full`, which stretches the card to fill the grid cell — that extra bottom margin sits on top of the grid `gap`, producing inconsistent spacing. Most grids already work around this with `mb-0`, but the workaround was applied inconsistently.

## Changes

Pass `mb-0` (alongside `h-full` for equal-height cells) on cards that are direct grid items, so spacing comes purely from the grid `gap`:

| File | Grid |
|---|---|
| `shared/pages/public/_events_grid.erb` | public events grid |
| `shared/_video_link_gallery.erb` | video link gallery (`lg:grid-cols-2`) |
| `admin/events/_reviews.erb` | event reviews grid |
| `admin/marketing_creatives/categories/_index_results.erb` | category grid |
| `admin/marketing_creatives/categories/show.html.erb` | profiles grid |

Also fixed `.team-grid` in `shared/_admin_show_team_members.erb`: it uses `gap` correctly on desktop, but when it collapses to a single column on mobile, the uniform row gap no longer separated one team member from the next (role/user pairs ran together). author: lujuldotcom
body:
Closes #28761

This change updates bookmark card favicon selection to prefer standard favicons before falling back to Apple Touch Icons.

The previous implementation explicitly prioritized apple-touch-icon entries with a width of at least 180px:
```
const appleTouchIcon = sizes.find(item => item.rel?.includes('apple') && item.sizes && item.size.width >= 180);
return appleTouchIcon || svgIcon || pickDefault(sizes);
```
As a result, bookmark cards could display an apple touch icon even when a site provided a dedicated favicon intended to represent its identity across browsers and platforms.

The updated implementation:
- Prefers SVG favicons when available.
- Uses the default favicon selection logic while excluding Apple Touch Icons.
- Falls back to apple-touch-icon only when no standard favicon can be resolved.

This preserves support for Apple Touch Icons while allowing bookmark cards to better reflect the site's primary favicon.

author: omjomjomj
body:
A bug-review pass across the timeline editing, agent/networking, and search/media subsystems. This PR fixes the four highest-impact confirmed defects (data-corruption and silent-failure class). Each was verified by reading the surrounding code.

## Fixes

**1. Visual-index cache poisoning (high)** — `Search/Indexing/VisualIndexer.swift`
A transient decode/sampling failure (locked file, unmounted volume, momentary ImageIO failure, unreadable video track) caused `save(rows: [], vectors: [], …)` to write a valid, *current* header with `count: 0`. Because `needsIndex` then returns `false` forever, the asset became permanently unsearchable. Now throws `VisualIndexerError.noContent` instead of caching an empty index, so the coordinator's `failedIds` (batch-scoped) retries it on the next pass.

**2. Asymmetric path-prefix check (high)** — `Models/MediaAsset.swift`
`url.path.hasPrefix(projectURL.path)` matched without a trailing separator, so an asset in a sibling directory sharing the project's name prefix (e.g. project `/x/Proj`, asset `/x/ProjectAlt/clip.mp4`) was stored as a corrupted `.project` relative path and read as offline after reload. Now compares against the project path plus a trailing `/`.

**3. SSE `error` event mishandling (high)** — `Agent/Clients/AgentClientTypes.swift`
The `error` case called `continuation.finish(throwing:)` without `return`, so the loop kept yielding past finish; and when the `message` field was absent it did nothing, silently swallowing the API error and ending the turn as if it succeeded. Now returns after finishing and surfaces a generic error when `message` is missing.

**4. Keyframe-split interpolation loss (medium)** — `Editor/ViewModel/EditorViewModel+ClipMutations.swift`
When splitting a clip between two keyframes, the inserted boundary keyframe on the right half used the default `.smooth` interpolation, silently changing the authored curve (`.linear`/`.hold`) of the opening segment. Now carries the governing keyframe's interpolation.

## Not addressed (reported, lower priority)
Other findings from the review left for follow-up: timeline volume keyframe +6 dB vs +15 dB ceiling mismatch, `runLoop` potential spin on empty `tool_use`, `cancelIndexing` blocking on `waitWhileExportActive`, `Float16` infinity in embeddings, `TimelineRuler` divide-by-zero at fps==1, stale `lastError` after retry, and MCP HTTP partial-read framing.

## Testing
The toolchain is macOS-only (AVFoundation/AppKit, arm64), so this could not be compiled in the review environment. Changes are minimal and self-contained.

author: woodid012
body:
The ladder reads scores from the stored final_totals snapshot, while the
results page calculates live. The snapshot was written client-side on every
results render — including mid-round — so a partial, in-progress tie (e.g.
Round 12 Miguel vs Cuts) could be frozen in as a phantom "draw" and never
corrected, leaving the ladder disagreeing with the results.

Persist Final Totals authoritatively from /api/consolidated-round-results,
but only once every game in the round is complete, using the exact numbers
the results page renders. Writes happen only when a stored total actually
changes, and the cached ladder from that round onward is cleared so it
rebuilds from the corrected totals. The client no longer stores totals, so
incomplete rounds can never seed a false draw.

author: hangie
body:
## Summary

Fixes #454. For a symbol whose canonical handle names a **project** module (e.g. a namespace sibling registered via `.pyeye.json`) that is **also** pip-installed, the forward-goto edges (`imports`, `callees`) resolved to the installed copy and labelled the stub `scope:"external"`, while `resolve`/`inspect` resolved the same handle to the project copy (`scope:"project"`). Same canonical handle, two definition sites, two scopes — a canonical-handle/scope-consistency violation.

**Root cause:** Jedi's `goto(follow_imports=True)` follows the environment `sys.path`, where an installed copy outranks the namespace `added_sys_path`; `resolve`/`inspect` instead anchor via `find_module_file` (the project boundary).

**Fix:** `build_stub` reconciles `scope` to `"project"` when an externally-classified target's canonical handle names a project module (`_names_project_module` → `find_module_file` over `source_roots` + `project_path` + `additional_paths`, excluding `added_sys_path`/env). Stdlib / pure-external handles return `None` and stay `external`. The `find_module_file` probe is gated behind a non-empty `additional_paths` (sibling roots) so the common single-project `callees`/`imports` expansion does no per-stub filesystem I/O. Only `scope` is reconciled (the stub carries no file; line spans stay as Jedi reported — they match for the common same-version case). Fixes `imports` **and** `callees`, since both flow through `build_stub`.

Surfaced while dogfooding the `namespace-jaraco` scenario (#447) and flagged by the `pyeye-verify` rubric's cross-repo-correctness dimension.

## Approach

TDD:
- **RED** — `test_external_edge_target_reconciles_to_project_definition_site` failed with `scope='external'`.
- **GREEN** — minimal reconciliation in `build_stub` + `_names_project_module` helper.
- Guard test `test_genuinely_external_target_stays_external` ensures stdlib handles are not over-reconciled.

The end-to-end *cause* (Jedi preferring an installed copy on the environment path) can't be reproduced deterministically in CI without installing a second package, so the regression test targets the fix seam (`build_stub`); the full path stays covered by the live `namespace-jaraco` dogfooding scenario.

## Known residual (by design)

Reconciliation fixes the `scope` **label**, not the stub's line span. `build_stub` reads `line_start`/`line_end` straight off the Jedi name, which is the copy the forward-goto walked (the installed one); only `scope` is flipped to `project`. So in the **version-skew** sub-case — installed copy a *different version* than the registered sibling — a stub can read `scope:"project"` with a `line_start` measured in the *installed* file (e.g. `ExceptionTrap` at line 50 there vs line 70 in the sibling). The stub's two facts then anchor to different files.

Why this is bounded and not a live bug:
- **Common case = no discrepancy.** The sibling normally *is* the dependency (same version, identical content), so the lines coincide.
- **Stubs carry no `file`,** so nothing can be mis-read from a stub alone — a consumer re-anchors via the `handle` (`inspect`/`resolve`), which resolves to the **project** definition site and returns the correct `location`. Only the stub's informational line hint can be stale.
- It only drifts under installed-vs-sibling **version skew**.

Full unification would re-locate the symbol inside the project file per stub — exactly the per-stub `find_symbol` / multi-file re-resolution the redesign avoids and which the decision log lists as rejected. Documented in the `#454` DECISIONS entry; left as-is deliberately.

## Test plan

- [x] Original RED→GREEN tests pass; guard test ensures stdlib handles stay external
- [ ] Added since the original run (pending CI): `additional_paths` perf short-circuit + branch-coverage tests (`module`-kind whole-handle path, single-component-handle guard, perf-guard skip) — **not yet re-run locally; relying on CI**
- [x] pre-commit (black, ruff, mypy, detect-secrets, conformance linter, markdownlint) pass
- [x] End-to-end verified in-process on the **real** jaraco repos: `resolve` and `expand(imports)` both report `project`

## Notes

- Decision-log entry added/updated (`docs/decisions/DECISIONS.md`) — now also records the `additional_paths` perf gate and the line-span residual above.
- Follow-up: the `namespace-jaraco` baseline + `pyeye-verify` rubric line (shipped in #447) can now be updated to reflect that the import/trace edges resolve consistently with `resolve`.

Fixes #454

Stacked on `feature-drsuapi-bind-transport` (#684), which is stacked on #682. The base is set to the Phase 2 branch so this diff shows only Phase 3; GitHub retargets it down the stack as each parent merges.

### Summary
Implements the DCSync critical thread on the bound handle: resolve a target account to its objectGUID (IDL_DRSCrackNames), then replicate that single object's attributes (IDL_DRSGetNCChanges, EXOP_REPL_OBJ). Values come back still-encrypted; PEK/RC4 decryption is the next phase.

### What changed
- **ms-drsr `CrackNames` / `ResolveToGUID`**: IDL_DRSCrackNames (opnum 12), projecting DS_NAME_RESULTW into friendly results; ResolveToGUID cracks an account name to DS_UNIQUE_ID_NAME and parses the `{guid}`.
- **ms-drsr `ReplicateSingleObject`**: builds the V8 GETCHGREQ with EXOP_REPL_OBJ + a GUID-addressed DSNAME, walks the V6 reply's REPLENTINFLIST linked list into `ReplicatedObject`s (GUID, DN, attributes); returns the prefix table + raw V6 reply for the later decryption pass.
- **Constants**: DS_NAME_FORMAT, DS_NAME_ERROR, EXOP, DRS_OPTIONS ([MS-DRSR] 4.1.4.1.x, 5.40, 5.41).

### Root Cause (wire-correctness fixes surfaced here)
- **GUID encoding bug**: idlgen mapped the IDL GUID/UUID types to `windows/guid.GUID`. That struct's Go layout ends in a `uint64`, so under the reflective NDR codec it serialises to **18 bytes in the wrong byte order** rather than the 16-octet uuid_t wire form — corrupting every GUID on the wire, including the bind's `puuidClientDsa`. Fixed by making `structures.UUID` a fixed 16-octet type with guid.GUID conversions (mirroring the endpoint mapper's proven `EptUUID`) and switching all `guid.GUID` struct fields to it. The endpoint mapper code documents exactly this hazard.
- **`DSNAME.StringName`**: the IDL is an inline conformant array `[size_is(NameLen+1)] WCHAR StringName[]`; idlgen had emitted a `unique` pointer. Fixed to `conformant`, plus `NewDSNameFromGUID` for the EXOP_REPL_OBJ addressing form.

### How Verified
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `go test` on the touched packages — clean; `-tags integration` build + vet — clean.
- Unit tests: UUID 16-octet wire order + round-trip; GUID-addressed DSNAME round-trip behind a unique pointer (hoisted conformant count + 16-octet GUID); DRS_MSG_GETCHGREQ_V8 and DRS_MSG_CRACKREQ_V1 union round-trips (switch Tag + arm + nested pNC / array-of-strings + NULL referents).
- Live integration test (`integration` tag): connect → ResolveToGUID(target) → ReplicateSingleObject → assert the object returned with attributes. Gated on DRSUAPI_TEST_HOST + DRSUAPI_TEST_TARGET.

### Test Coverage
- **Added:** `structures/dsname_test.go`, `structures/getchgreq_test.go`; extended `ms-drsr/integration_test.go` with TestCrackAndReplicate.

### Scope of Change
- **Files changed:** drsuapi `structures/` (UUID, DSNAME, constants, 8 guid.GUID→UUID field sweeps, NTDSAPIClientGUID return type) + tests; new `ms-drsr/{crack_names,get_nc_changes}.go`.
- **Behavioral changes outside the DCSync thread:** the GUID-encoding fix changes how every drsuapi GUID field serialises — this is a correctness fix (the prior encoding was wrong on the wire), and it is what makes the Phase 2 bind actually correct.

### Notes
Not yet wire-validated against a live DC; the integration test is the acceptance gate. For EXOP_REPL_OBJ the source-DSA GUID (uuidDsaObjDest/uuidInvocIdSrc) is left NULL — sufficient for single-object replication; full-NC and strict servers want the real DSA GUID from IDL_DRSDomainControllerInfo (a later step). Returned attribute values are still encrypted (Phase 4 decryption).

author: jonathanmos
body: ### What does this PR do? RUM-16551 replaced GradientDrawable.mFillPaint reflection with the public getColor() API, which returns only the raw fill colour. AppCompat stores tints applied via DrawableCompat.setTintList() in the private Drawable.mTintFilter field, which is inaccessible on API 30+ (Android 11's catch-all hidden-API enforcement) and was also not read by the new code on API 24–28. This caused tinted button backgrounds to appear as invisible white ShapeWireframes instead of falling back to the image wireframe path. Fix: return null from resolveGradientDrawable (Q mapper) and resolveGradientDrawableNPlus (M mapper) when drawable.colorFilter is null, restoring the image wireframe fallback which correctly renders the tinted appearance. author: rezabaita12
body:
## What

Adds two GitHub-native security layers to complement the existing CI gate:

- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** — weekly grouped dependency updates for `cargo` (root workspace), the Bun `npm` client (`clients/bun`), and pinned `github-actions`.
- **`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`** — CodeQL SAST for `rust` + `javascript-typescript` (`security-extended` queries), running on push/PR to `main` and weekly. Free on this public repo.

## Why

Existing CI already covers `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo audit`, `gitleaks`, `bun audit`, and `lizard` complexity. This PR fills the two remaining gaps:

- **Semantic SAST** (CodeQL) — clippy is a linter, not security analysis; this matters given the `unsafe` FFI boundary in `crates/engine/src/ffi.rs`.
- **Graph-level dependency alerts** (Dependabot) — flags newly disclosed advisories even when no push triggers `cargo audit`, and auto-bumps vulnerable deps.

Pairs with the repo settings already enabled out-of-band: secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot alerts + security updates, and the "Protect main" branch ruleset.

## Notes

- CodeQL **default setup** is intentionally left `not-configured` so this advanced workflow is the sole scanner (the two would conflict).
- Once merged, the `Analyze (rust)` / `Analyze (javascript-typescript)` checks can be added to the ruleset's required status checks.
- No engine/ABI/storage-seam changes — config + CI only.

body:
## What
Adds `packages/protocol/src/providerCompletionRequest.test.ts` — pins the bounds and routing-identity invariants of `providerCompletionRequestSchema`, the egress envelope that leaves the OS for a provider endpoint. `index.test.ts` parses it once on the happy path and reads back `requestContext` fields; the payload bounds were unpinned.

## Authority angle — egress-request bounds + routing-target identity
- **Routing target named and non-empty** — `id`/`sessionId`/`providerProfileId`/`modelId` are each `min(1).max(256)`: a request can never go out with an empty `providerProfileId`/`modelId` (no anonymous routing target) nor an unbounded identifier.
- **Message payload bounded non-empty** — `messages` is `min(1).max(200)`: always at least one turn, count capped (no zero-message call, no unbounded transcript dump).
- **Attachments count-capped** — at most 6 multimodal riders.
- **Output ceiling is a capped positive int** — `maxOutputTokens`, when present, is a positive int ≤ 32_000: a caller can raise the adapter default but cannot request unbounded generation nor a zero/negative ceiling.
- **Plain-object strip** — an unknown key is stripped.

## Safety
Test-only. No protocol/schema/behavior change. No network/secret/DB. Generic OS only.

author: madmax983
body:
🔒 Warden: [security fix]
🦠 Threat: The `Hologram` struct exposed its dimensions (`width` and `height`) and `data` vector publicly. This allowed arbitrary external code to modify the dimensions without resizing the underlying vector. A subsequent call to `.reconstruct()` would use the invalid dimensions to compute an index, resulting in an out-of-bounds slice panic and leading to a Denial of Service.
🛡️ Defense: Privatized the `width`, `height`, and `data` fields to enforce encapsulation, providing read-only getters for external consumers. Additionally, injected a boundary check `assert_eq!(self.width * self.height, self.data.len())` at the start of `.reconstruct()` to ensure state integrity. Migrated tests to inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules to allow for controlled internal fuzzing without compromising the public API.
💥 Severity: High - Denial of Service due to out-of-bounds panics caused by missing encapsulation.
🧪 Verification: Modified chaos tests to run via internal modules to verify panics are correctly caught using bounds checks without crashing downstream.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

gate now does it automatically.

`tests/smoke/test_token_audience.py` reuses the existing session `viewer_token`

  fails *before* strict `aud` validation (`api/app/auth.py`) could lock out the app.

author: briangflett
body:
Activates **migrate-on-deploy**, now that Preview has its own auto-branched Neon DB (Neon native integration, configured 2026-06-21).

`vercel.json` buildCommand runs `pnpm db:migrate:deploy && pnpm build`:
- **Preview** deploys migrate their own throwaway Neon branch (isolated from prod).
- **Production** migrates only on merge to `main`.

`db:migrate:deploy` = `drizzle-kit migrate` reading `DATABASE_URL` from the deploy env directly, so Vercel injects the correct per-environment database. **CI is unaffected** (CI runs `pnpm build` directly, not the Vercel buildCommand).

### ⚠️ Before merging
Confirm prod has **no un-applied migrations** — the first prod deploy after merge runs `db:migrate:deploy` against prod (idempotent/no-op if prod's schema already matches `drizzle/migrations/`).

### Proof
A throwaway PR (`claude/t2-proof`, branched off this one with a trivial migration) verifies the migration lands on an isolated **preview** branch and the preview deploy succeeds — confirming prod isolation. That PR will be closed without merging.

```
Header:  count(u32) + entry_start(u32)

Data:    embedded sub-files (.anm + .pxb + .png)

- `.anm` — 动画帧序列定义
- `.pxb` — 引擎原生像素缓冲区

author: tamnd
body:
Slice 3 of encryption at rest. Slice 2 sealed the WAL and shipped the public option but left the key fixed at create time. This makes the key epoch movable.

## What lands

RotateEncryptionKey advances an open encrypted database to the next key epoch. It checkpoints the log so no half-old frames remain, derives a fresh DEK off the same master key at the bumped epoch, and persists a new descriptor durably before swapping the in-memory scheme. Pages already on disk keep their old-epoch seal and are read lazily under the epoch that wrote them, so a rotation rewrites one page rather than the whole file.

The caller's key does not change. The rotation bumps an internal epoch off the same master, distinct from a passphrase change, which is a later slice.

## On-disk format

The AEAD envelope grows a 4-byte cleartext epoch trailer after the nonce, so a reader knows which key to derive before it can decrypt. The epoch is bound into the AAD on both page and WAL seals, so a flipped trailer fails authentication and surfaces as a wrong-key error rather than decrypting under the wrong key. Overhead moves from 28 to 32 bytes, absorbed by the reserved-trailer mechanic the engine already reads dynamically. The descriptor version moves from 1 to 2, so the earlier encrypted format fails cleanly at open instead of misdecrypting. kv is unreleased, so no version-1 file exists outside a test.

Compact stays the full re-encryption path: it rebuilds the file and reseals every page at a fresh epoch 0, for callers who want no page left under a superseded epoch.

## Surface

Exposes kv.RotateEncryptionKey and the kv.ErrNotEncrypted sentinel for a rotation requested on an unencrypted database.

## Tests

Crypto: a rotated scheme opens an old-epoch envelope and a fresh seal records the new epoch; the tamper test now covers the epoch trailer.
db: lazy coexistence across a rotation read back after reopen, descriptor epoch advance on disk, new-epoch WAL recovery across a crash, reject-on-plaintext, wrong-key after rotate.
Facade: write-rotate-write-reopen round-trip reading both generations, plaintext refusal.
Full module suite passes.

## Summary

Adds `docs/INTERPRETATION_IMPROVEMENTS.md` — a log of **how to read and narrate** the Engine's evidence better, distinct from `RULE_CHANGELOG.md` (which tracks calculation rules). Surfaced by a blind relationship-domain review where the **timing was correct but the *reading* of the evidence was not**.

**No-calibration premise intact:** every entry is a *generalizable* interpretation rule. No engine math is changed and no per-native fact is encoded.

## Eight domain-general relationship-reading fixes
1. **Activation ≠ positive outcome** — set polarity from Track-B weight, not the dāśā label.
2. **Don't fuse distinct relationships** — an AD-lord flavour change can be a reset/new relationship.
3. **Map KP house-mix → relationship TYPE** — 5/8/12 = love/secret/long-distance; 2/7/11 = matrimonial/formal.
4. **Always emit an explicit ending/separation window** — not only onset & peak.
5. **"False dawn" rule** — a benefic Sūkṣma under a detachment umbrella (Ketu MD / Rahu→12 AD) is a brief re-opening that fails; rank the umbrella above the trigger for *sign*.
6. **AD change into a 12-dominant lord = likely closure marker.**
7. **"Same partner love→marriage" vs "married someone else despite a continuous timeline"** — decide by romance-bundle vs marriage-bundle **linkage**, not timeline continuity.
8. **Read Shadbala + Iṣṭa/Kaṣṭa + Avasthā per-kāraka and as a contrast**, using the gender-correct spouse-kāraka (Jupiter = husband for a female chart).

Timing methodology is unchanged — only the *reading* of sign, type, segmentation, partner-identity, and strength is tightened.

author: oleg-koval
body:
## What and why

Supply-chain hardening and repo hygiene pass for the `ts-npm-starter` template. Every change is additive or a strict security improvement — no behaviour changes to build, test, or release logic.

## Changes

### GitHub Actions — pin all actions to commit SHAs
All `uses:` references were on floating major-version tags (`@v4`, `@v3`, `@v2`, `@main`). A compromised or force-pushed tag silently runs attacker code in CI. Pinned to exact commit SHAs with the tag as a comment so Dependabot can still update them.

| Action | Was | Now |
|--------|-----|-----|
| `actions/checkout` | `@v4` | `@11bd71901…` (v4.2.2) |
| `actions/setup-node` | `@v4` | `@49933ea52…` (v4.4.0) |
| `coverallsapp/github-action` | `@v2` | `@5cbfd81b6…` (v2.3.7) |
| `actions/upload-pages-artifact` | `@v3` | `@56afc609e…` (v3.0.1) |
| `actions/deploy-pages` | `@v4` | `@d6db90164…` (v4.0.5) |
| `github/codeql-action/{init,autobuild,analyze}` | `@v3` | `@8272c299f…` (v3.36.2) |
| `oleg-koval/pr-automerge-github-action` | `@main` | `@172b14bf1…` (HEAD of main) |

### GitHub Actions — add top-level `permissions: contents: read`
`code-quality.yml` and `automerge.yml` were missing a top-level permissions block, meaning they inherited the repo default (often `contents: write`). Added `permissions: contents: read` at workflow level; job-level overrides that need write access are preserved.

### Dependabot — `.github/dependabot.yml`
Was missing entirely. Adds weekly coverage for both `npm` (grouped) and `github-actions` ecosystems so dependency drift is caught automatically.

### CODEOWNERS — `.github/CODEOWNERS`
Was missing. Routes all review requests to `@oleg-koval`.

### `.node-version`
Was missing. Pins the local dev runtime to Node 22.16.0, matching the CI release job. Tools like `fnm`, `nvm`, `mise`, and VS Code pick this up automatically.

## Not included (left for Oleg)
- OpenSSF Scorecard workflow (would add a new workflow + badge; low risk to skip for a library starter)
- Rotating the Coveralls token to use OIDC instead of `GITHUB_TOKEN` (no security gap today, just a nice-to-have)

author: min-hinthar
body:
## Resend email-events webhook

Completes the Resend integration (after #37's send path). `POST /api/resend/webhook` receives Resend email events (delivered / bounced / complained / …) and acts on them — wired to the `RESEND_WEBHOOK` + `RESEND_SIGNING_SECRET` config.

### Security — signature verification (the load-bearing part)
Resend signs callbacks via **Svix**: `base64(HMAC_SHA256(secret, "{id}.{timestamp}.{body}"))`. The route, **before trusting anything**:
- requires `RESEND_SIGNING_SECRET` (else 500 → Resend redelivers); a secret that **doesn't decode** to a key is a diagnosable **500**, not a silent stream of 401s;
- requires the `svix-id` / `svix-timestamp` / `svix-signature` headers (else 400);
- rejects a timestamp outside **±5 min** (replay guard, 400);
- verifies the HMAC over the **raw** body with a **length-guarded `timingSafeEqual`** (else 401).

No new dependency — `node:crypto`. The pre-PR adversarial reviewer verified the algorithm against the Svix spec and found **no forgery path** (fails closed on a bad/empty/malformed signature; no crash/DoS).

### Behavior (full handler)
- **bounce / complaint** → flagged in server logs (the actionable "a staff invite didn't land" signal) with a **masked recipient** + opaque `email_id` — never the raw address.
- **all verified events** → a **PII-free** PostHog event (type + `email_id` only; no recipient to analytics).
- **Idempotent + fail-safe:** always 200 after a verified signature (a processing hiccup never triggers an endless retry); JSON parse wrapped; PostHog drained via `after()`. Mirrors the Stripe webhook; the middleware matcher already skips `/api`.

### Also
- `siteUrl()` (email links) falls back to `https://qr.mandalaymorningstar.com` (the real prod domain).
- Docs: `ENV.md` gains `RESEND_SIGNING_SECRET` + a webhook-setup step; `HANDOFF.md` activation note. (`RESEND_WEBHOOK` was provisioned but the handler only needs the signing secret — noted in docs.)

### Activation (you)
In the Resend dashboard add a webhook → `https://qr.mandalaymorningstar.com/api/resend/webhook`, paste its Svix signing secret as `RESEND_SIGNING_SECRET`.

### Gate
`pnpm turbo lint typecheck build` ✅ · route registered in the build manifest · pre-PR adversarial review **SHIP WITH FIXES** (signature sound; the one finding — diagnostic 500 on a non-decoding secret — fixed). Verdict posted below.

author: junaiddshaukat
body:
## Summary
A Kafka Serde for `KStreamsPayload` so the envelope can cross a topic boundary. Until now it only flowed in-JVM via `ProcessorContext#forward`; GroupByKey introduces the first real topic (the key-based repartition topic, per the plan agreed with @je-ik), which needs the payload serialized. Split out as its own small PR ahead of GBK.

## Scope
- `KStreamsPayloadSerde<T>`: parameterized by the `Coder<WindowedValue<T>>` for
  the data variant (different topics carry different element types; the watermark
  variant is coder-independent). Wire format: a one-byte discriminator + body —
  data = `[0x00][windowedValueCoder-encoded value]`; watermark =
  `[0x01][long millis][int sourcePartition][int totalSourcePartitions]`.
- Unit tests: round-trip of data, watermark, and terminal MAX watermark, plus an
  unknown-tag failure.

## Out of scope
- Wiring the serde into the GBK repartition / watermark fan-out — that's the
  GroupByKey PR.

## Notes
- Assumes non-null payloads: the topics it's used on (repartition, watermark
  fan-out) are not log-compacted, so no tombstones occur.

## Testing
`./gradlew :runners:kafka-streams:check` green; 4 unit tests.

Closes #39042
Refs #18479
cc @je-ik

author: cagataycali
body:
## What
The reference MoveIt2 ZMQ sidecar (`strands_robots/policies/moveit2/server/zmq_node.py`) had **no test coverage** (0%, 111 lines). It implements the wire protocol `MoveIt2Policy` speaks: a single-threaded REQ/REP msgpack server with `ping` / `reset` / `plan` endpoints. Nothing exercised the argument parser, the `_plan` goal-branch decision tree, the `_build_moveit_py` wiring, or the REP dispatch loop.

## Why
The sidecar deliberately keeps every ROS / `moveit_py` import lazy (inside `_build_moveit_py`, `_plan`, and `main`) so the module imports cleanly on a plain client venv without ROS 2 sourced. That same design makes it fully unit-testable: the heavy deps can be supplied as light fakes. The protocol contract (default port 5556, trajectory rows as `[time_from_start_seconds, q0..qN]`, structured failure responses instead of crashes) is exactly the kind of thing a regression test should pin, since the client depends on it byte-for-byte.

## How
New `tests/policies/moveit2/test_zmq_sidecar.py` supplies the ROS surface (`rclpy`, `geometry_msgs`, `moveit`, `moveit_configs_utils`) as `sys.modules` fakes via `monkeypatch.setitem`, and drives the dispatch loop with **real** `zmq`/`msgpack` against a fake REP socket that replays a fixed request sequence then raises `KeyboardInterrupt` (mirroring a real Ctrl-C). Tests assert observable outputs, not internal state:

- `_parse_args`: defaults (port 5556 matches the client) + full override set.
- `_plan` decision tree: unknown planning group, missing goal, `target_joints`, `target_pose` (PoseStamped field wiring), planner exception caught, empty-result reported, and trajectory row serialisation (nanosec folded into the seconds column).
- `_build_moveit_py`: optional `--robot-description-package` / `--moveit-config-package` wiring through the configs builder.

author: sufforest
body:
The eighth extension point: a sandboxed gate at `POST /login`, run **before** the user lookup and the CPU-bound argon2 verify, for anti-brute-force / credential-stuffing and IP/geo blocking. A block keys on the username and IP, not the auth result, so it never leaks whether the credentials were valid, and a blocked attempt never reaches the DB or the hash.

It is the sibling of `check_registration` — same decision shape, the same privacy-tiered client IP (with its own HMAC subkey so a token is scoped to login), and `kv` works here, so a per-IP attempt counter that blocks after N is a few lines. Only `m.login.password` today; the context carries `login_type` so future types extend without a new point.

- The shared client-IP helpers move out of `register.rs` into `auth/client_ip.rs`, parameterized by HMAC purpose (registration's token is unchanged).
- Same `X-Forwarded-For` trust caveat as `check_registration` (only trustworthy behind a header-overwriting proxy; don't grant hashed/full when directly exposed).

WIT 0.10.0 → 0.11.0; fixtures and the keyword-filter example rebuilt, with a new `login-guest` fixture. Includes an end-to-end test that a plugin blocks a banned username before lookup/verify.

author: mtschoen
body:
## Why

`resolveToolBinary` returned the **bundled** binary whenever present, so aislop ran its own vendored ruff (currently `0.15.4`) instead of the ruff a project pins and gates CI on (e.g. `0.15.15`). ruff's formatter output is versioned by *style edition* (2024.2 → v0.3.0, 2025 → v0.9.0, 2026 → v0.15.0), so two versions can format the same file differently once they cross an edition boundary. aislop's `python-formatting` finding then disagrees with the project's own `ruff format --check` - the exact drift that makes teams disable aislop's format passthrough rather than trust it.

## What

- For **bundled** tools (`ruff`, `golangci-lint`): prefer a system install found on `PATH`, falling back to the vendored binary (then bare name) when absent - preserving the zero-dependency guarantee for users who never installed the tool.
- **Non-bundled** tools (`roslynator`, `jb`) are unchanged: still resolved by bare name so OS `PATH`+`PATHEXT` handles them at spawn.
- Adds `tests/tooling.test.ts` covering prefer-system, fallback, and non-bundled passthrough.

## Verification

- `tests/tooling.test.ts`: 3/3 pass (red→green confirmed against pre-change code).
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean. `biome check` on changed files: clean.
- Full suite: **17 pre-existing failures on `schoen/main`, identical set with and without this change** (zero new failures). The pre-existing failures are unrelated (Windows-env/git-dependent: `agents/worktree`, `cli`, project-wide `security`, etc.).

author: chbrain
body:
## What
Operationalizes the three-tier escalation **languagedetect → franc → NLP** by pushing the franc tier as far as the gate's confidence margin safely allows. Adds `bg` Bulgarian, `sr` Serbian, `tr` Turkish, `uz` Uzbek to `FRANC_MAP` — moving them from NLP-exempt (tier 3) up to franc (tier 2).

## Why these are safe — the margin
The gate only flags when the declared language scores **more than 0.1 below** franc's top. For these four, franc's *top* is often a sibling, but the declared language stays inside the margin, so **correct prose still passes**:

| Lang | franc top | declared score | gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sr` Serbian | `bos` | `srp` 1.00 | passes |
| `bg` Bulgarian | `mkd` | `bul` 0.97 | passes |
| `tr` Turkish | `azb` | `tur` 0.94 | passes |
| `uz` Uzbek | `uzn` | `uzn` 1.00 | passes |

This is a **gross-error-catch** gate for the tight clusters — it flags English-in-a-Serbian-house but won't split Serbian from Bosnian. Weaker than the distinct-language cases, but gating beats dropping to NLP (your stated preference).

## What stays exempt
Only **Czech** (`ces` falls to 0.77 behind Croatian — a true false-fail) and **Azeri** (franc splits it across `azj`/`azb`). They remain declarable via `khai.languages`. The "unregistered language" test now uses Czech.

## Test
A verified native sample per added language pins the routing (the tripwire if `franc-all` ever advances/regresses). **57 tests green.** Governance lane; no new dependency (`franc-all` already present).

author: el3ssar
body:
Closes #188

## Summary

`seed` previously had three meanings across the init subsystem: the topology
builders and the named `random`/`random_binary` initializers drew from NumPy
on CPU (then copied to device), `orthogonal` used a `torch.Generator`, and the
default no-initializer path in `ESNCell` used the **global** torch RNG — which
the initializer `seed` could not reach.

The whole-reservoir `ESNLayer(seed=...)` threading (recurrent matrix,
feedback/input weights, bias, **and** the default `uniform(-1, 1)` draws via a
seeded `torch.Generator`) already landed with the blocker **#135 / #136**. This
PR completes the input/feedback side: the `random`/`random_binary` initializers
now draw with a `torch.Generator` **directly on the target weight's device**
(no CPU build + copy) and accept an `int` *or* a `torch.Generator` seed, so
device-native reproducible draws — CUDA included — are possible.

## Changes

- `InputFeedbackInitializer.seed` widened to `SeedLike` (`int | torch.Generator
  | None`); new protected `_torch_generator_for(device)` builds a device-native
  generator seeded from `self.seed` (a generator is reduced to its
  `initial_seed()` so `seed=k` and `seed=Generator().manual_seed(k)` agree).
- `RandomInputInitializer` / `RandomBinaryInitializer.initialize()` rewritten to
  draw on-device through the helper (uniform / signed-bits), dropping the NumPy
  build-and-copy. Per-device reproducible; `seed=None` tracks `torch.manual_seed`.
- Connectivity mask and the `pseudo_diagonal` / `dendrocycle_input` NumPy draws
  coerce the seed to int (`coerce_seed_to_int`), keeping the package mypy-clean
  under the widened type and reproducible when handed a generator seed.
- Docs: a canonical reproducible-layer recipe + a device-native note added to
  `docs/build/layers/esn-layer.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

author: lucascervera
body:
## What

Introduces a unified **Block Display** system. A *block* (umbrella for a **concept** = instantiable definition, or an **instance** = concrete block) is now rendered through exactly one of three components — **Pill**, **Card**, **Sheet** — chosen by interaction context, replacing the old size axis (`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xs`) and all hand-rolled block markup.

Two orthogonal axes:
- **Display** (engagement level): `Pill` (reference — concepts sidebar, matrix headers), `Card` (browse — hierarchy tree), `Sheet` (work — central panel, always).
- **`kind`** (what it is): `concept` → dashed outline + type icon; `instance` → solid fill + emoji.

## Why

The previous code rendered the same conceptual thing several inconsistent ways (a name was sometimes an `<h3>`, sometimes a giant pill; concept vs instance were visually identical; a `:variant` prop was silently ignored). This made it hard to tell *what part of the model* you were looking at. The new system is one visual language at three zoom levels — concept vs instance readable at a glance, consistent everywhere.

## Key changes

- **New**: `useBlockVisuals` composable (centralizes color/icon/outline-vs-solid), `BlockCard.vue`, `BlockSheet.vue`, `BlockFeed.vue`.
- **Slimmed**: `BlockPill.vue` to a pure reference display.
- **Removed**: `BlockViewer.vue` (replaced by `BlockSheet`), the size axis, the unused `simplified` prop.
- **Central feed**: concept Sheet pinned on top + indented, reorderable instance Sheets; single-active-editor invariant (one local `editingId` ref); explicit pencil-button editing (expanding ≠ editing); concept sheet collapses by type (list = collapsed context, single = expanded content), feed keyed by concept so state resets on navigation.
- **Matrices**: axis source/target render as concept Pills, row/col items as instance Pills (matrices are a relation container, not blocks).
- **Fix**: added `src/vite-env.d.ts` so the production build types `import.meta.env`.

## SDD trail

Planned and verified via SDD; artifacts archived at `openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-21-block-display-system/` (proposal, spec, design, tasks, verification + archive reports).

## Verification

- typecheck clean, 8/8 unit tests pass, **production build passes**.
- Validated live in a browser preview against a real sample model: concept Pills (dashed + type icon), pinned concept Sheet, indented instances, expand≠edit, explicit edit, single-active-editor, matrices-as-pills, collapse-by-type.

## Reviewer notes

- `src/main.ts` includes a dev-only `window.__devLoadModel(path)` gated by `import.meta.env.DEV` (tree-shaken from prod) used for headless preview validation — happy to remove if undesired.
- Foundations (unified `colors.ts`, `conceptVisuals.ts`, `renderMarkdown.ts`, data-driven `MarkerIcons.ts`, stable list-item IDs) are part of this branch too.

## Summary

This is the bounded PR A for the receptor-layer work. It freezes production receptor-evidence inputs for the PhageHostLearn assay phages without adding H1 model-comparison code.

Included:
- sequence-backed PhageHostLearn phage CDS annotations: 8,393 rows across 105 assay phages
- PHROGs/MMseqs receptor-domain evidence: 495 input rows and 495 normalized domain rows
- Phold/Foldseek receptor-like structural evidence: 23 input rows and 23 normalized structural rows

author: kkukielka
body:
## Summary (closes #21)

Ports the React renderer's fix (k11k-labs/better-blocks-react-renderer@e5cc53c) to Astro, with root plugin k11k-labs/strapi-plugin-better-blocks#58.

**Problem:** file-mode download buttons opened PDFs/videos/images inline instead of downloading. The native `download` attribute is ignored for cross-origin assets (Strapi/CDN), so renderable files preview rather than save.

## What's implemented

- **`filePreview` toggle** (`src/types.ts`): file mode only. `true` → opens the file in a new tab (`target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`, no download) for preview — **fully zero-JS**. `false`/omitted → force-download. Passed through to custom `button` renderers via `Button.astro`.
- **Force cross-origin download** (`src/ButtonControl.astro`): download-mode anchors are tagged `data-bb-download` / `data-bb-download-name`, and a **small scoped `<script>`** (the renderer's only client-side JS) fetches the asset as a blob and saves it from a same-origin object URL. Progressive enhancement — without JS the anchor still works via `href` + `download`; a CORS-blocked fetch falls back to native navigation; modified/middle clicks are respected.
- **README** — download-vs-preview section + `filePreview` table row.

## Playground

- Seed gains **Download PDF / Preview PDF / Download DOCX** buttons (mirrors the React seed) backed by real uploaded `sample.pdf` / `sample.docx` assets; `strapi/src/index.ts` refactored to an `uploadAsset` helper that maps each file button to its asset by extension.
- **Strapi plugin bumped `^0.2.0` → `^0.14.0`** (latest) so the admin uses the newest Button editor (which emits `filePreview`); `yarn.lock` regenerated accordingly.
- `CustomButton.astro` override now respects `filePreview`.

## Note on zero-JS

The renderer stays zero-JS for everything except download-mode buttons, which get the tiny progressive-enhancement script. The preview path and all other blocks remain script-free. Mirrors the React behavior; flagged here in case you'd prefer to gate it behind a prop.

## Testing

- 2 new tests (download-mode tagging, `filePreview` new-tab markup) — **91/91 passing**.
- `astro check`: 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 hints; prettier clean; seed JSON validated.
- Changeset added (minor).

Closes #21

body:
## Vấn đề (#1 — critical)

Manifest đặt `documentAccess: "dynamic-page"`. Dưới cờ này, các API **đồng bộ** đã deprecated sẽ **throw exception** (đã xác minh tài liệu chính thức Figma):

- `figma.variables.getLocalVariableCollections()` / `getLocalVariables()` — bị bọc trong `try/catch` trả `null` ⇒ **Phase 2 `variables` luôn rỗng** trên mọi export, im lặng. Toàn bộ "design tokens" của Phase 2 không tạo ra gì.
- `InstanceNode.mainComponent` — **không** có try/catch ⇒ **Phase 3 export chứa bất kỳ INSTANCE nào sẽ throw và fail toàn bộ**.

## Thay đổi

- `variableSnapshot` → async, dùng `getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync()` + `getLocalVariablesAsync()`.
- `componentExtras` → async, dùng `await inst.getMainComponentAsync()`.
- `serializeNode` → async; lặp children **tuần tự** (`for...of` + `await`) để giữ nguyên thứ tự đếm DFS cho `maxNodes`/`maxDepth`.
- `buildExportPayload` await roots + variables.
- Giữ `try/catch` quanh variables chỉ để fallback cho editor không có variables API (FigJam).

## Kiểm thử

- `tsc --noEmit` cho `src` ✅ và cho `plugin/*.ts` (strict) ✅
- `node esbuild.plugin.mjs` build OK → `plugin/dist/code.js`
- Bundle xác nhận chỉ còn `getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync` / `getLocalVariablesAsync` / `getMainComponentAsync`, không còn API sync.

body:
## Description

This PR introduces local-only mode for the Warp OSS build, enabling account-free operation with user-provided API keys for AI inference. The implementation includes:

1. **New `vercel_gateway` module** (`crates/ai/src/vercel_gateway.rs`): A minimal, non-streaming client for OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions APIs. Supports the Vercel AI Gateway, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, and other compatible endpoints. Users configure these as `CustomEndpoint`s in settings.

2. **Local-only mode detection** (`crates/warp_core/src/channel/state.rs`): Added `ChannelState::is_local_only()` to identify when the build is running in fully local, account-free mode (OSS channel).

3. **OSS build configuration** (`app/src/bin/oss.rs`): Enabled three feature flags for the OSS build:
   - `SkipFirebaseAnonymousUser`: Boot directly into terminal without sign-up/log-in
   - `SoloUserByok`: Enable bring-your-own-key for solo users
   - `CustomInferenceEndpoints`: Allow custom endpoint configuration

4. **Settings UI filtering** (`app/src/settings_view/mod.rs`): Hide hosted-only product surfaces (Teams, Referrals, Billing & Usage) in local-only mode since they require a Warp account.

5. **View hierarchy helper** (`crates/warpui_core/src/core/window.rs`): Added `child_view_ids()` method to support GUI view-transfer walks.

The `vercel_gateway` module is intentionally minimal and serves as a scaffold for local-mode AI. Streaming and full tool-calling parity can be layered on top later. All requests bypass Warp's backend entirely—nothing leaves the machine except the request to the user's chosen provider.

## Testing

- Added comprehensive unit tests in `vercel_gateway.rs` covering:
  - URL construction with and without trailing slashes
  - Default Vercel Gateway URL fallback
  - API key validation
  - Response parsing
- Settings filtering logic is straightforward conditional logic
- Feature flag configuration is declarative

CHANGELOG-NEW-FEATURE: Local-only mode for Warp OSS with support for OpenAI-compatible inference endpoints (Vercel AI Gateway, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, etc.) using user-provided API keys.

author: ngtongsheng
body:
## Summary
- `onBack` in `LyricCreatorContext` always blocked navigation with a discard-only "Leave without saving?" dialog whenever the text editor was dirty — there was no way to save and leave.
- Now: when leaving, the dirty draft is rebuilt via the existing `buildLyrics` line-diff. If the edit wouldn't drop any existing line timing (`invalidated.length === 0` — the common case, e.g. no timing yet, or edits that don't touch timed lines), it auto-saves and navigates straight back. If the edit would silently drop existing timing on a previously-timed line, the leave-confirm dialog still fires (a real destructive choice worth asking about).

## Test plan
- [x] Edited lyric text for a song with existing timing, appending an untimed line (no existing timing touched) → clicking back auto-saved and returned to the player with no dialog; reopening the lyric creator showed the edit persisted.
- [x] Deleted a previously-timed line from the text, then clicked back → "Leave without saving?" dialog still appears (destructive-edit guard intact); cancelled, library lyrics.json unchanged.
- [x] `npm run check` passes (pre-existing unrelated lint warning in main.css, not introduced by this change).

Closes #155

author: allamiro
body:
Closes #6.

### Problem
The seed path used two different definitions of "delete this seed":
- the existence-check skip treated **any** all-zero seed as a delete — `is_deleting = seed_bytes == b'\x00' * len(seed_bytes)` (molto2.py:299), whereas
- the padding branch only treated an **exactly-20-byte** all-zero seed as a delete — `if seed == b'\x00' * 20` (molto2.py:313).

So `--seed 0000` skipped the "already has a seed" guard but then fell into the *non-delete* branch and wrote a real `0x80`-padded seed instead of clearing the profile — the opposite of intent.

### Fix
Key the padding branch on the same `is_deleting` flag, so an all-zero seed of any length consistently clears the profile (zero-padded, no `0x80` marker).

### Validation
Standalone test comparing old vs new padding (no device required):

```
seed (hex)             is_del | OLD cleared? NEW cleared?  verdict
00 * 20                  True |         True         True  OK
00 * 16                  True |        False         True  OK  <-- OLD BUG
0000                     True |        False         True  OK  <-- OLD BUG
00                       True |        False         True  OK  <-- OLD BUG
DEADBEEFDEADBEEF        False |        False        False  OK
```

The documented 20-byte delete and all non-zero seeds are unchanged; `py_compile` and `--help` pass.

author: lyaqanyi
body:
## 问题

`Live2DManager.setupFloatingButtonsBase`(`static/avatar-ui-buttons.js`)在**重新调用却不重建锁图标**的路径下(如 showLive2d 重建路径、告别/返回的返回球重建路径),会经 `_removeFloatingButtonsElement` 删掉旧的 `#live2d-lock-icon` DOM —— 但该函数只调用 `el.remove()`,**不会**把 `this._lockIconTicker` 从 `this.pixi_app.ticker` 摘除。

锁图标 ticker 此前只在 `setupHTMLLockIcon`(`static/live2d-ui-buttons.js`)或 `cleanupFloatingButtons`(`static/live2d-model.js`)里才被拆除。于是旧 ticker 变成孤儿,继续每帧 mutate 一个已脱离文档节点的 `left/top`,直到下一次完整 teardown。视觉无感(节点已 detached),但是真实的**每帧 CPU 泄漏**,会跨告别/返回、模型切换循环不断累积。

## 修复

在 `setupFloatingButtonsBase` 删除自身锁图标 DOM **之前**,镜像 `setupHTMLLockIcon` / `cleanupFloatingButtons` 的拆除逻辑,从 `pixi_app.ticker` 摘除 `_lockIconTicker` 并置 `null`:

```js
if (this._lockIconTicker && this.pixi_app && this.pixi_app.ticker) {
    try { this.pixi_app.ticker.remove(this._lockIconTicker); } catch (_) {}
    this._lockIconTicker = null;
}
```

## 验证

- `node --check` 语法通过。
- **无重复移除**:置 `null` 后任何后续拆除路径(`setupHTMLLockIcon` 的 existingLockIcon 分支、`cleanupFloatingButtons`、`app-interpage.js`)都会跳过;PIXI 的 `ticker.remove()` 本身幂等。
- **新锁图标仍注册 ticker**:`setupHTMLLockIcon` 在 base 之后单独运行,无条件重新创建图标并 `ticker.add(tick)`。
- **对其他模型类型安全**:`this._lockIconTicker && this.pixi_app && this.pixi_app.ticker` 守卫,对没有该字段的 VRM/MMD/PNGTuber manager 是空操作。
