author: nubaeon
body:
## What

Fixes the 7 remaining **Category-B** dead static SQL queries flagged by the schema-reference guard (`tests/test_sql_schema_references.py`). Category-A (5 mechanical renames) shipped in #131; these are the core-path **behavior revivals** — each query named a column that doesn't exist, the `OperationalError` was swallowed by a broad `except`, and the feature silently no-op'd for an unknown duration.

Every fix was verified against the **real schema** (built via the production schema builders for `grounded_verifications` / `goals` / `projects` / `reflexes` / `sessions`), not from priors.

| Site | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `calibration_insights._get_recent_verifications` | `calibration_score`, `gaps`, `metadata` | → `overall_calibration_score`, `calibration_gaps`; dropped `metadata` (no such column, key unused downstream); reindexed `created_at` |
| `orchestrator.from_goal` | `scope_breadth/duration/coordination` columns don't exist | read the `scope` JSON blob, parse `breadth/duration/coordination` |
| `docs_commands._detect_project_id` | `project_id` **and** `root_path` | `SELECT id`, drop dead `root_path LIKE` clause, match on `name` |
| `agent_commands` turtle grounding | `vectors_json` column doesn't exist; `reflex_data` has no `vectors` key | read individual vector columns (`know`…`engagement`), build grounding dict |
| `_workflow_preflight` calibration trend | `grounded_verifications` has no `project_id` | JOIN `sessions` on `session_id`, filter `s.project_id` |
| `_workflow_preflight` last-session-ts | `sessions` has no `updated_at` | `MAX(start_time)` (ISO-8601) |
| `goal_commands._prune_test_pollution` | `ai_id` lives on `sessions`, not `goals` | LEFT JOIN `sessions` (NULL-session goals still match objective patterns) |

## Two things session-verification caught (the spec wasn't ground truth)

1. **`agent_commands`** — the deferred spec said read `reflex_data.get('vectors')`. But `reflex_data` stores only `{prompt_summary, uncertainty_notes}` — there is no `vectors` key. The canonical vectors are the individual reflexes columns. The wrong spec would have produced an always-empty grounding, silently.
2. **`docs_commands`** — the guard flagged only `project_id`, but `root_path` was *also* dead. `EXPLAIN` halts at the first bad column, so a violation can mask a sibling behind it. Re-running the guard after each fix surfaces the next.

## Verification

- Guard: **0 known + 0 new violations** (was 7 known); `_KNOWN_VIOLATIONS` allowlist emptied. 523 static queries validated via `EXPLAIN`.
- `agent_commands` query kept **static** (not f-string) so the guard keeps validating it — future vector-column renames fail at test time instead of silently re-killing turtle grounding.
- `tests/test_preflight_feedback_column.py` + `tests/test_import_budget.py` pass; all 6 edited modules import; ruff clean.

author: lupus
body:
## What Two `volume`-surface UX fixes surfaced by the M3-volumes dogfood runs. ### 1. TTY-aware `volume rm` / `volume prune` confirmation Today, without `-f`, these commands print an unanswerable `[y/N]` to a non-terminal, silently default to **No**, and **exit 0** — so `izba volume rm x && …` wrongly proceeds, and the dogfooding Actor read the no-op as a success ("unexpectedly succeeded" candidate). New behavior follows the prevailing CLI convention ([clig.dev](https://clig.dev/): *"only prompt when stdin is a TTY; never **require** a prompt — error and tell the user the flag"*; matches `gh`, `terraform`, `apt`): | Context | Behavior | Exit | |---|---|---| | **TTY**, no `-f` | prompt `[y/N]`, default No | decline → **non-zero** | | **non-TTY**, no `-f` | **no** prompt; error: `refusing to … — re-run with --force` | **non-zero** | | any, `-f/--force` | skip prompt (still does **not** bypass the in-use guard) | normal | This keeps the safety prompt for humans at a terminal (a deliberate, helpful divergence from Docker for *persistent* data — it never affects scripts/CI/agents, which are non-TTY) while killing the silent exit-0 no-op. The decision core (`confirm_with`) takes the TTY flag + input reader injected, so the script-relevant branches are unit-tested without a real terminal. ### 2. Document the `--volume` SIZE format — closes #73 The `g`/`m` suffix requirement was in the spec but absent from the user-facing surface, so users (and the cheap exploration model, 6×) kept trying bare `:1`. Now documented in `create --help`, `volume attach --help`, and the README, and the parse error is self-describing: `size "1" must end in a 'g' or 'm' suffix, e.g. 10g or 512m`. ## Why it came up Found by the spec-anchored LLM dogfooding pipeline running against M3 volumes. The non-TTY exit-0 no-op was the wart behind the "expected a refusal but exited 0" candidate; #73 was the dominant self-inflicted noise source (bare sizes derailing the create-first journeys). A quick UX-convention review (clig.dev + docker/gh/terraform/apt) settled the least-surprising design above. ## Tests / gates All six workspace gates green locally (test / clippy×2 / fmt / musl-static / windows-gnu check+clippy). 5 new `confirm_with`/`is_affirmative` unit tests cover force / non-TTY-errors / tty-yes / tty-no-or-empty. No public `izba-core`/`izba-proto` types changed (CLI-internal helper + doc strings + one error string), so the GUI is unaffected. Closes #73. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes two UX regressions in the `volume` command surface found during M3-volumes dogfooding: a silent exit-0 no-op when `volume rm`/`prune` ran without `--force` in a non-TTY context, and a missing SIZE-format hint that caused bare `:1` specs to fail with an unhelpful error. - Adds a `confirm_with` helper (TTY flag + BufRead reader injected) so the confirm decision is unit-testable; `confirm_destructive` is the thin real-stdin wrapper; `prune` and `rm` now exit non-zero on both explicit decline and non-TTY-without-force, with an actionable error naming `--force`. - Updates all user-facing help strings, the README, and the `parse_size` error message to document the `g`/`m` suffix requirement. - Adds `mutants = "0.0.4"` to suppress cargo-mutants on the KVM-gated daemon-wired functions, and extends the SonarCloud coverage exclusion to `volume.rs`.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge — the changes are additive CLI-layer fixes with no impact on daemon protocol, core types, or disk state. The TTY-aware confirm logic is cleanly separated into a pure, injected-dependency function with five unit tests covering every branch. The exit-code correction (0→1 on decline) is straightforward and consistent with how main.rs maps Ok(code) to the process exit. No public izba-core or izba-proto types are touched, so the GUI and daemon wire protocol are unaffected. Documentation and help-string updates are accurate and match the implementation. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | crates/izba-cli/src/commands/volume.rs | Core change: replaces the old `confirm` helper with a testable `confirm_with` (injected TTY flag + BufRead) + a thin `confirm_destructive` real-stdin wrapper; `prune`/`rm` now exit 1 on decline and error (non-zero) on non-TTY-without-force; 5 unit tests cover all branches cleanly. | | crates/izba-cli/src/main.rs | Doc-string only: `--volume` help now documents the `g`/`m` suffix requirement with examples. No logic change. | | crates/izba-core/src/volume.rs | One-line improvement to the `parse_size` error message: adds "a … suffix, e.g. 10g or 512m" so the failure is self-describing. | | crates/izba-cli/Cargo.toml | Adds `mutants = "0.0.4"` to `[dependencies]` (required placement — `#[mutants::skip]` must be visible during normal compilation, not only test compilation). | | sonar-project.properties | Adds `crates/izba-cli/src/commands/volume.rs` to `sonar.coverage.exclusions` with updated rationale comment; the untestable daemon-glue paths are covered by KVM e2e, and the confirm logic is mutation-tested separately. | | README.md | Adds a short paragraph documenting the SIZE suffix requirement and the new TTY-aware confirmation behavior for `rm`/`prune`. |

author: cjthorpe
body:
Two root causes:

1. useAuth did not check JWT expiry before returning isAuthenticated:true. An expired token in localStorage bypassed the silent-refresh path, causing all protected API calls (including /api/agent-logins) to 401. Fixed by decoding the exp claim client-side and triggering a refresh when the token is expired or within 60 s of expiry.

2. useAgentLogins, useIntegrations, and lib/integrations fell back to http://localhost:3000 instead of port 3001 where the API actually listens.  Also consolidated authHeaders() in useAgentLogins to use the shared getAuthHeaders() from lib/auth.

Existing guards blocked agents from modifying `provisionCommand`, `teardownCommand`, `cleanupCommand`. But host-executed commands could also exist in:

author: ppanchal5698
body:
### 💡 What
The `remarkPlugins` array and `components` rendering object were extracted from inside the `Markdown` component's render function into the module scope.

### 🎯 Why
When these objects are defined inline, they are created with a new memory reference on every single render. ReactMarkdown sees these new references and unmounts/remounts the DOM nodes. For a component used heavily in streaming chat responses, this causes significant and continuous unmounting/remounting which impacts performance and can cause cursor/scroll jumping issues during fast generation. Extracting them creates stable references and eliminates the bottleneck.

### 📊 Impact
Reduces DOM unmounting/remounting for the Markdown component to zero during normal re-renders. Greatly improves rendering performance specifically during fast streaming chat updates where this component re-renders multiple times per second.

### 🔬 Measurement
Verified via Playwright trace and manual visual inspection during a streamed response. The chat window rendering is visibly smoother and doesn't recreate nodes repeatedly while the response is streaming. Validated safe by type checking and building.

author: hikaruegashira
body:
PR #273 removed the started-state poll in the ref-drift verify step, expecting flyctl deploy --strategy immediate to block until machines are healthy. It doesn't — the next run failed because the verify step ran while machines were still 'replacing' and the new deployment-<ts> ref wasn't yet on the machine list.

Restore the poll. Acceptable steady-state timing now comes from depot.dev (fly's remote builder) cache hits, which made the build itself 32s in the failed run — when the verify poll completes normally we expect total ~125s (build 30-90s + poll ~70s + /ready ~20s). The 350s case was the cold-cache first deploy after PR #272.

author: kai-cloudflare
body:
## Summary

The [Spectrum Limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#private-network-load-balancing) page states that the Spectrum proxy protocol setting is unsupported when using Spectrum as an on-ramp and **Cloudflare WAN** as an off-ramp. This is also the case when the off-ramp is **Cloudflare Tunnel**: the proxy protocol header (v1 and v2) is not delivered to the private origin, so the origin does not receive the original client IP.

This PR generalizes the note so it applies regardless of the off-ramp and explicitly includes Cloudflare Tunnel.

## Change

Before:
> When using Spectrum as an on-ramp and Cloudflare WAN as an off-ramp the proxy protocol setting in Spectrum is not supported.

After:
> When using Spectrum as an on-ramp into Private Network Load Balancing, the proxy protocol setting in Spectrum is not supported. This applies regardless of the off-ramp used to reach your private origin, including Cloudflare WAN and Cloudflare Tunnel.

## Verification

Verified empirically with a public Spectrum TCP application whose origin is a Load Balancer using Private Network Load Balancing (LTM) with a private-IP origin routed over Cloudflare Tunnel. With proxy protocol set to v1, v2, and off, the origin received the raw client bytes with no proxy protocol header in all cases.

author: quidow
body:
## Summary

Stage 1 of reducing availability state-flips: expose a read-only **allocatability projection** on the device read API so operators and the frontend have one legible answer to *"can this device take a session right now, and if not, why,"* instead of inferring it from `operational_state` + `is_reserved` + intents.

Two new fields on `DeviceRead` (inherited by `DeviceDetail`):
- `allocatable: bool`
- `unavailable_reason: UnavailableReason | null`

The projection mirrors the real allocation gate (`grid.allocation._eligible_devices`): a device is allocatable iff `operational_state == available` and it is not reserved. Operational state dominates; an available-but-reserved device reports `reserved`.

**Zero behavior change** — additive, non-breaking (both fields have defaults), no Alembic migration (derived fields, not columns).

## What changed

1. `feat(backend)`: pure `app/devices/services/allocatability.py` (`unavailable_reason` / `is_allocatable`) + `UnavailableReason` enum.
2. `feat(backend)`: the two fields on `DeviceRead`, populated in the presenter's single `serialize_device` site (covers list + detail).
3. `feat(frontend)`: regenerated `openapi.ts` + ergonomic `UnavailableReason` re-export.

## Reason values

Ships the currently-producible subset: `busy`, `verifying`, `maintenance`, `offline`, `reserved`. Later stages extend the enum (`cooldown` / `draining` / `paused`) as the soft-gate lands; `allocatable` intentionally does not yet model the transient node transition-token window (deferred).

## Test plan

- Backend full suite: **3009 passed**.
- New unit tests for the pure projection; new device-API tests asserting derived values end-to-end (`offline -> "offline"`, `reserved -> "reserved"`, `available+free -> allocatable:true / reason:null`).
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit`, `lint`, `types:check` all green; `openapi.ts` diff is purely additive.

## Follow-up

Small consistency PR suggested: add `@pytest.mark.db` to both device-detail tests (the new one and the pre-existing `test_device_read_exposes_is_reserved`) so the `-m "not db"` lane stays honest.

author: tangozwo-max
body:
## Why

The essay pipeline was defined **three different ways** that disagreed (`gui/src/lib/types.ts`, `gui/src/lib/team.ts`, the `phase-result` route), with **no single source of truth**, **no handover documents**, and **no resume artifact** — so every new AI chat started from scratch, and the app's status dots / workflow pages were already broken for `curriculum` / `fqa` / `final`. This PR establishes the structure **and** aligns the app to it.

## 1. Structure layer (single source of truth)

- **`STRUCTURE.md`** — master guide: 3 phases → workflows, status model, folder layout, position / resume / go-back-a-phase.
- **`AGENTS.md`** (root) — tells any new AI chat to load the canonical map first, so sessions resume.
- **`structure/workflow-map.json`** — canonical phase/workflow ids with `aliases` reconciling the old schemes.
- **`structure/handover-template.md`** + **`structure/project-state.template.json`** — handover format + resume/status schema.
- **`01 projects/_template/`** — full project scaffold (`00 Input` … `08 Final`, `_handover/`, `project-state.json`, `PROJECT.md` dashboard).
- **`01 projects/README.md`** — how to position and resume a project.

## 2. Handover & resume model

- Each workflow writes `<folder>/result.md` → that **is** the handover into the next workflow.
- At each phase boundary, write `_handover/<n>-<phase>.md` (the document set passed forward) and advance `currentPhase`/`currentWorkflow`.
- `project-state.json` (`currentPhase` + `currentWorkflow`) is the resume pointer; `PROJECT.md` mirrors it for humans.
- Phases can be re-entered ("go back and redo"), recorded under *Revisions* in the handover file.

## 3. Publishing (decided)

`/01 projects/` is now **published** so handover docs / dashboards / the research wiki are readable online — but **PDFs and other heavy binaries are kept local** via `.gitignore` (they're referenced by path, not committed).

## 4. App alignment (single source of truth in code)

- New **`gui/src/lib/workflow-map.ts`** — in-app canonical pipeline (mirrors the JSON); `types.ts`, `team.ts`, `workflow-config.ts`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `WorkflowPage.tsx`, and the `phase-result` route all derive from it via canonical ids + `canonicalId()` alias resolution.
- Fixes the real bug: `Sidebar`'s `SIDEBAR_TO_STATE` keys never matched `team.ts` ids, so status dots were blank for `curriculum`/`fqa`/`final`.

author: garethpaul
body:
## Summary

Harden UpDown's repository verification boundary so caller-controlled GNU Make state cannot redirect trusted checks, while keeping Swift, project assets, prompt selection, and CoreMotion behavior unchanged.

## Baseline

`master` at `016a442bf720b1bd396ddf1e361467d92fb05ff1` passed nine portable static contract groups locally and from an external directory. Its seven exact-head hosted checks were green and all three GitHub security alert queues were empty. The Makefile protected only `ROOT`, leaving interpreter expressions, recipe shell state, startup files, and non-executing or error-ignoring modes caller-controlled.

## Improvements

### Tests

- Adds an adversarial Make authority harness covering 35 public-target/root/shell combinations, hostile literal executable paths, command and environment Make syntax, duplicate Makefile state, startup boundaries, caller `MAKEFLAGS`, and ten unsafe execution modes.

### CI

- Runs the full `/usr/bin/make check` gate in both Ubuntu and macOS jobs, matching the documented local command and preventing executable-path redirection.

### Security

- Freezes literal Python and shell authority, rejects untrusted startup files and Makefile lists, derives the canonical repository root, and fails closed for dry-run, touch, question, and ignore-error modes.

### Static Analysis

- Extends portable contracts to enforce the strengthened Make and workflow boundary.

### Documentation

- Records the authority model, scope boundary, changelog entry, and updated verification behavior.

## Validation

- `timeout 240 /usr/bin/make -C /tmp/updown-master-exact.XMYv6C check` — passed; Xcode tests/build skipped truthfully because `xcodebuild` is unavailable.
- External-directory `timeout 240 /usr/bin/make --no-print-directory -f /tmp/updown-master-exact.XMYv6C/Makefile check` — passed with the same truthful platform skips.
- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/check_ios_contracts.py` — passed.
- `bash -n scripts/test_ios.sh` and `/bin/sh -n scripts/test-makefile-root.sh` — passed.
- `git diff --check` and `git fsck --strict --no-dangling` — passed.
- Gitleaks 8.30.1 filesystem scan — no leaks found.

## Risk

- The Makefile is intentionally stricter and rejects caller startup files, Make expression values for `PYTHON`, and non-executing/error-ignoring modes.
- The full hosted macOS job now performs both XCTest and an unsigned simulator build; its existing 15-minute timeout remains the operational bound.
- Physical-device CoreMotion behavior is unchanged and remains outside local Linux validation.

## Follow-Ups

- Verify the physical-device motion checklist on representative iPhone and iPad hardware.
- Monitor the macOS job duration after adding the explicit build gate and adjust only if hosted evidence shows the existing timeout is insufficient.

body:
## Summary

Adds v0.33 VerifyOS-Governed WORLD Disposition above the v0.32 observation and feedback layer.

## Implemented

- exact v0.32 feedback and evidence binding
- externally issued finite, single-use verification protocol
- pre-adjudication criterion, success/failure and falsification conditions
- exact VerifyOS request with host-license and assessor-policy binding
- independent challenge and corroboration receipt
- strict PASSED / FAILED / INDETERMINATE semantics
- `ADOPT_CANDIDATE`, `REJECT_CANDIDATE`, `DEFER_CANDIDATE`, and `REOBSERVE_CANDIDATE`
- passed v0.32 REOBSERVE feedback cannot be promoted to adoption
- one protocol → one request → one receipt → one disposition candidate
- strict validation of every existing official-ledger row before append
- future-only learning and preserved counterevidence/uncertainty

## Authority boundary

```text
verification != truth
verification != causal attribution
passed verification != WORLD adoption
adopt candidate != WORLD commit
reject candidate != destructive deletion
WORLD disposition != plan activation or ActOS invocation
WORLD fragment update != constitutional root rewrite
```

## Validation state

The dedicated workflow contains the representative scenario, 22 unit tests, v0.32-v0.29 regressions, the targeted Lean module, and the full formal root. Pull-request workflow runs were created for the latest head, but the visible v0.32, VerifyOS v0.2 and formal validation runs remained runner-queued at merge time; no job failure was reported. The local fallback could not clone GitHub because the isolated executor had no external DNS. Static review confirmed protocol-window preservation, exact source bindings, independent-assessor identity, verdict conditions, route derivation, strict-ledger validation, replay guards, and Lean conjunction/proof ordering.

author: michaltargiel91
body:
💡 **What:** Refactored `poly_nms` in `ppocr/utils/poly_nms.py` to pre-compute Shapely `Polygon` objects in an $O(N)$ loop before the main $O(N^2)$ NMS logic. Replaced the expensive Shapely `union` geometric operations with a simple mathematical formula (Area A + Area B - Intersection Area). Uses the *unbuffered* area to calculate union to strictly maintain backward compatibility with original algorithm logic.

🎯 **Why:** The previous implementation reconstructed `Polygon` objects repeatedly and called expensive geometric intersections inside an $O(N^2)$ inner loop, causing severe CPU bottlenecks during inference post-processing. Additionally, naive fixes to geometry errors by buffering inside `poly_union` would erroneously alter areas and drop polygons. 

📊 **Impact:** Reduces `poly_nms` execution time for 200 boxes from ~6.5 seconds down to ~0.33 seconds (a ~20x speedup), significantly reducing inference latency.

🔬 **Measurement:** Verified locally via mock test script simulating 200 randomly generated bounding boxes, confirming identical result counts (192 kept polygons) and precision between the original and optimized versions.

author: groupthinking
body:
## Summary

The web `build` CI job is **red on `main`** (and therefore on every open PR). This PR fixes the first of **two** root causes blocking the build.

### Bug A — fixed here: missing OpenTelemetry peer deps
`next build` dies immediately while loading `apps/web/next.config.js`:

```
Error: Cannot find module '@opentelemetry/instrumentation'
  require stack: .../@sentry/node-core/build/cjs/otel/instrument.js → @sentry/nextjs → next.config.js
```

`@sentry/node-core` (transitively required by `@sentry/nextjs`) declares
`@opentelemetry/{core, exporter-trace-otlp-http, instrumentation, sdk-trace-base}`
as **peerDependencies**. CI installs with `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`, which
does **not** install peer deps, so they were never hoisted to top-level
`node_modules` where `@sentry/node-core` resolves them (only nested copies under
`@sentry/node` and `packages/observability` existed).

**Fix:** declare the four peers as direct deps of `apps/web`, pinned to the
versions already resolved transitively in the lockfile, so they hoist to
top-level `node_modules`.

**Verified locally:** `npm run build:web` now loads `next.config.js` and proceeds
past Sentry init — the `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` error is gone.

### Bug B — NOT fixed here, needs a decision ⚠️
Once Bug A is cleared, the build hits a **second pre-existing failure on `main`**:

```
Error: It looks like you're trying to use `tailwindcss` directly as a PostCSS
plugin. The PostCSS plugin has moved to a separate package... install
`@tailwindcss/postcss` ...
```

`apps/web/package.json` pins `tailwindcss: ^4.3.1`, but the entire frontend is
authored for **Tailwind v3**: `postcss.config.js` uses `tailwindcss: {}`,
`globals.css` uses `@tailwind base/components/utilities`, and there's a v3-style
`tailwind.config.js` with an extensive custom theme. The v4 pin appears to be an
unreviewed/mis-applied dependabot bump (cf. open PR #342).

Two options — **maintainer call**:
1. **Pin back to v3** (`tailwindcss@^3.4.19`) — smallest, lowest-risk change;
   restores the codebase's intended state. (npm fought an in-place downgrade due
   to a stale lockfile node; needs a clean reinstall.)
2. **Migrate to v4** — `@tailwindcss/postcss`, `@import "tailwindcss"` + `@config`,
   and review visual regressions across the design system.

I did not push a fix for Bug B because the direction is a judgment call with
real visual-regression risk.

## Notes
- This branch is `main` + the #347 `@slack/web-api` bump + this OTel fix. The
  lockfile churn includes the slack bump deps and some benign hoist/dedup; no
  framework packages (`next`, `react`, `@sentry/nextjs`, `typescript`,
  `tailwindcss`) changed version.
- Draft until Bug B is decided — the build won't be fully green until then.

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #276. Live testing showed the Coach's regex router still required the magic word "task" for many natural priority questions — "What are my career priorities?" fell through to `light` mode (no task context, generic deflection) while "What are my health task and work task priorities?" already worked. Separately, `compact_task` follow-up replies (e.g. "turn that into 3 steps") sometimes got cut off mid-sentence.

## Changes

- **`coachContextMode.js`** — generalized the `BROAD_TASK_QUERY_RE` literal `what are my priorities` alternative into a structural pattern `what are my[\w\s'-]{0,40}priorit(?:y|ies)` so any inserted category/horizon words (career, work, health, personal, this month, quarter, 6 month, etc.) still route to `full_task`. No hardcoded category list, no person/employer-specific names — purely structural, so it works for a clean-slate new user with any category they type.
- **`coachContextMode.test.js`** — new test block covering all the previously-failing phrasings, plus the already-passing "what should I focus on this month" / "which work/career/health task should I do first" variants (those already routed correctly via existing regexes — added as regression coverage).
- **`coachSystemPrompt.js`** (`buildCompactTaskPrompt`) — added explicit FORMAT RULES: numbered-step requests (N ≤ 5) get exactly N complete numbered lines with no preamble and no mid-sentence cutoffs; N > 5 gets the first 5 complete steps plus an offer for the rest; date/time questions get exactly one complete sentence from `Current Time`.
- **`coachSystemPrompt.test.js`** — asserts the new FORMAT RULES text is present in the `compact_task` prompt.
- **`CoachTab.jsx`** — `compact_task` `maxTokens` raised from 220 to 280 (one line) to give the now-more-explicit format rules room to complete a 3-step reply without truncation.

## Out of scope (untouched)

Providers, Groq/NVIDIA/Gemini fallback, Firebase/auth/sync, check-in/reminder scheduling, task metadata inference, copy buttons, task links, UI redesign, audio/focus timer.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/utils/coachContextMode.test.js src/utils/coachSystemPrompt.test.js` — 35/35 passing
- [x] `npx vitest run` (full suite) — 878/878 passing

body:
## What

The standalone pages **/charts, /risk, /concentration, /data-quality, /ops** had pre-existing horizontal page overflow at mobile width (390px), flagged by m14-mobile-nav. Each shares a `min-h-screen` + `<main class="mx-auto max-w-5xl px-6">` chrome and held wide content — fixed-width SVG charts, a wide data table, or long label/value rows — inside single-column CSS grids whose default `auto` track sized to the content's intrinsic (over-viewport) width. That width propagated up through `main`, pushing the whole document wider than the viewport (a sideways scrollbar a mobile user would see).

## How

- **Chart SVGs** (`bar`, `line`, `area`, `candlestick`, `donut`, `treemap`) carry `h-auto max-w-full` so they scale down to their container instead of forcing it wider. No-op on desktop (containers are already wide enough).
- The two-column `lg:grid-cols-[1fr_18rem]` layouts on risk / concentration / data-quality use `minmax(0,1fr)` + `min-w-0` grid items, so the auto track can shrink below content size on mobile. The wide data-quality table now scrolls **inside** its `overflow-x-auto` wrapper (clientWidth 292 < scrollWidth 556, container bounded to the viewport) rather than expanding the page.
- The ops cockpit's status-column cards (`flex min-w-0 flex-col`) and milestone rows (`min-w-0 truncate` label + `shrink-0` value) let long titles clip instead of stretching the row.

Product stays read-only; no Decimal/number-boundary changes.

## How tested

- `bun run typecheck` ✅ · `bun run lint` ✅ · `bun run test` ✅ (3394 unit tests) · `bun run build` ✅
- Full chromium e2e suite ✅ **391 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed** (no regressions on the ~26 pages that reuse the chart primitives).
- New oracle `e2e/mobile-overflow.spec.ts` (+ `mobile-overflow-trace.spec.ts`): asserts `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` at 390×844 on all five routes, that the data-quality table stays a bounded internal scroller, and that desktop (1280×800) is unaffected.
- Updated the chromium-darwin `charts-gallery` pixel baseline for the few-px vertical shift introduced by `h-auto` (CI/linux skips it — no platform baseline there).

## Visual QA evidence (read back with vision)

Paths under `e2e/evidence/m15-mobile-overflow/`:
- Mobile (390×844): `charts-mobile.png`, `risk-mobile.png`, `concentration-mobile.png`, `data-quality-mobile.png`, `ops-mobile.png`
- Desktop (1280×800): `charts-desktop.png`, `risk-desktop.png`, `concentration-desktop.png`, `data-quality-desktop.png`, `ops-desktop.png`
- Trace: `trace-mobile.zip`

**Vision verdict:** All five mobile pages render fully within the 390px viewport — no sideways scroll, no clipped or blank regions, readable. Charts (line/area/bar/signed/donut/treemap/candlestick) scale down cleanly; the data-quality per-holding table scrolls horizontally **within its card** while the page does not; ops unit titles truncate with ellipsis and keep their right-aligned status badges; risk/concentration bars, donuts and legends fit. Desktop screenshots are unchanged from the prior layout (two-column grids intact, full-size charts).

author: eeee2345
body:
Rebases this branch onto current main and fixes the CI break (its tests depended on scripts/author-rule-llm.ts / check-collector-freshness.ts / format-poc-backlog-issue.ts, deleted from the public repo after this PR was opened on 2026-06-21; those orphaned tests were already removed from main by #210, so the rebase alone resolves it). Also drops the wild-scan-diff.ts / wild-scan-refresh.yml files that were bundled into the original branch — that's a separate, unrelated feature out of scope here.

## What this does

ATR has three layers: ATD is the WHAT (technique knowledge base, like ATT&CK/CWE), the rules are the HOW (detection, like Sigma). The daily collector caught frontline agent CVEs and promote-cve turned the generalizable ones into rules, but nothing fed ATD. `scripts/atd/ingest-cve-to-atd.ts` gives each agent-relevant CVE one of three outcomes:

- **ENRICH** — if the CVE's CWE matches an existing technique, add the CVE as real-world evidence on that technique. Automatic, schema-validated, low risk.
- **DRAFT** (new in this update) — if a CWE has no covering technique but is corroborated by 2+ independent CVEs, Claude drafts a full candidate technique entry (title/description/tactic/abstraction/detection_surface/OWASP-ASI/MITRE-ATLAS) via a direct `@anthropic-ai/sdk` call (same `callClaude`/`extractBalancedJson` pattern as `scripts/fn-mine-llm.ts`), schema-validated with one corrective retry before dropping. Lands in `data/atd-ingest/new-technique-drafts-<date>.json` for human review — never auto-merged. A CWE already covered by a prior draft is skipped so an unresolved cluster doesn't spawn a duplicate PR every day.
- **RAW** — everything else (no CWE, or a CWE seen only once) stays a flat list for human triage.

`.github/workflows/atd-ingest.yml` runs daily after the collector + promote-cve, with `workflow_dispatch` inputs (`source`, `cap`, `dry_run`), `set -eo pipefail`, and opens a draft PR (`atd,needs-human-review`) only when something actually changed on disk — a no-op day opens nothing.

## Verified

Typecheck clean, actionlint clean, baseline `validate-atd` PASS (80 techniques). Dry-run against the real current `proposals/` backlog (4,876 proposals, 1,256 agent-relevant CVEs): 579 real ENRICH opportunities across 24 existing techniques, plus 29 CWE clusters with >= 2 CVEs each that are genuinely uncovered by any existing technique (e.g. CWE-346 unauthenticated cross-origin MCP tool invocation, CWE-1336 Jinja2 SSTI in Haystack, CWE-88 kubectl flag injection via an MCP Kubernetes server) — real material for `--draft-techniques`. The schema-validation + corrective-retry path was smoke-tested against the real ajv validator with a fake LLM response.

Left as draft. Nothing here auto-merges or auto-mints a technique into the catalog.

author: dereuromark
body:
Follow-up to the safe-by-default security work: fixes the inline-nesting DoS
(MED-4 from the audit) that was deliberately kept out of the XSS PRs.

A nested-link bomb `[[[…](#)](#)…` recurses through `parseInlines` and rescans
balanced brackets at each level - ~O(n^2). n=2000 took ~1s; n=8000 several
seconds.

Adds an inline-recursion depth cap (`MAX_INLINE_DEPTH = 100`, mirroring the
existing block-nesting cap): beyond it the remaining text is emitted as a
literal text node instead of recursing further, bounding the cost to ~linear
(n=8000 now ~0.36s). `parseInlines` becomes a thin depth-guard wrapper over
`parseInlinesImpl`. No real document nests inline 100 levels deep; full suite +
corpus unaffected (2659 tests).

author: filmil
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `vivado_program_flash` rule that programs a bitstream **permanently**
— writing it into the device's non-volatile SPI/QSPI configuration flash so the
FPGA loads the design automatically on power-up. The existing
`vivado_program_device` rule only programs the **volatile** FPGA SRAM, which is
lost on the next power cycle.

## Design

A single executable rule with two phases:

1. **Build the flash image (no hardware).** A hermetic build action runs
   Vivado's `write_cfgmem` to convert the `.bit` into a flash image
   (`.mcs`/`.bin`) for the configured flash part. `bazel build //x:prog`
   produces the image as a cacheable artifact. Mirrors the Docker build-action
   pattern in `internal/vivado_extract.bzl`.
2. **Program the flash (needs the board).** A generated `bazel run` wrapper
   connects to a hardware server and writes the image via Vivado's
   `create_hw_cfgmem` / `program_hw_cfgmem`. Mirrors
   `internal/vivado_program_device.bzl` + the `proggen` generator.

```starlark
vivado_program_flash(
    name = "blinky_flash",
    deps = [":blinky_pnr"],                 # provides VivadoBitstreamProvider
    flash_part = "mt25ql256-spi-x1_x2_x4",  # board-specific cfgmem part
    size = 32,                              # flash capacity in MB
    interface = "SPIx4",                    # default
)
```

```
bazel build //build/tests/vivado:blinky_flash        # -> blinky_flash.mcs (no board)
bazel run   //build/tests/vivado:blinky_flash -- \
    --hostport localhost:3122 --device '*/xilinx_tcf/Digilent/<serial>'
```

## Changes

- **New** `internal/vivado_program_flash.bzl` — the rule.
- **New** `build/vivado/bin/proggen/flash_script.tpl.sh` — runtime cfgmem
  programming template.
- Extends the `proggen` generator (reused, not duplicated): new flash fields,
  selects the template by basename, accepts `--mcs-file` as an alternative to
  `--bitfile`. Adds a flash-mode unit test.
- Wires the rule into `rules.bzl`, the `rules` bzl_library, the stardoc/golden
  doc targets, and regenerates reference docs.
- Adds an Alinx A200T (Micron MT25QL256 QSPI) example under
  `build/tests/vivado`.

## Verification

The actual flash write needs the Vivado Docker image and a physical board, so
it cannot run in CI. Everything else was verified locally:

- `bazel test $(bazel query "tests(//...) - tests(//build/tests/...)")` → **26 tests pass** (incl. golden-doc + proggen tests).
- `bazel build --nobuild //build/tests/vivado:blinky_flash` → analyzes clean.
- Rendered the flash template via `proggen`: no unrendered tokens, valid bash
  syntax, and the generated TCL expands correctly (`get_cfgmem_parts {…}`,

author: r0bles
body:
## Description

This PR fixes how branches with multiple slash-separated segments (e.g., `feature/a/b/c`) are displayed in the Git Flow tree view. Previously, only the first two segments were rendered, with the branch name truncated at the first `/` so that only the second segment was visible.

The fix introduces a recursive tree-building approach that correctly groups branches into folder nodes at any depth, ensuring the full branch name is preserved and all Git Flow context menu commands work properly.

## Changes

### `src/ViewBranches.ts`

#### New `FolderNode` class

- Represents intermediate folder nodes in the branch tree hierarchy
- Extends `vscode.TreeItem` with folder icon (`"folder"` theme icon)
- Stores the original gitflow `prefix` (`feature`, `release`, etc.) and current `depth` level
- Sets `contextValue = "folder"` to distinguish from branch nodes in context menus

#### New `buildBranchTree()` method

- Recursively constructs the tree from a flat list of branch names
- Splits each branch path by `/` and processes segment by segment
- When a branch has only one segment remaining, it creates a `Flow` leaf node
- When a branch has multiple segments, it groups them into `FolderNode` parent nodes
- Preserves the correct `contextValue` (`feature_local`, `origin_feature`, etc.) at every nesting level so context menu commands work properly
- Sorts results with folders first, then branches, both alphabetically

#### Refactored `getChildren()` method

- Updated return type to `Thenable<(Flow | FolderNode)[]>`
- When the parent element is a `FolderNode`, filters all branches that match the folder's full path and delegates to `buildBranchTree()` recursively
- When the parent element is a category node (Features, Releases, etc.), collects both local and remote branches and builds the tree

#### Updated `getTreeItem()` method

- Now accepts both `Flow` and `FolderNode` types

#### Fixed `general()` method

- Changed `branch.split("/")[1]` to `branch.substring(branch.indexOf("/") + 1)` so that the full branch name after the prefix is preserved (e.g., `a/b/c` instead of just `a`)

#### Updated `checkoutBranch()` method

- Removed the filter `el.split("/").length < 2` from the quick-pick list, so all branches (including deeply nested ones) appear in the branch selection dialog

## Before vs After

**Before** (branch `feature/auth/login/validation`):

```text
Features/
  └── auth   ← truncated name, not a real branch
```

**After**:

```text
Features/
  └── auth/           (folder)
        └── login/    (folder)
              └── validation   ← correct leaf branch
```

## Testing

- [x] Code compiles without errors
- [x] Branches with 2 segments (e.g., `feature/my-feature`) display correctly
- [x] Branches with 3+ segments (e.g., `feature/a/b/c`) display as nested folders
- [x] Context menu commands (checkout, finish, delete, publish) work on deeply nested branches
- [x] Remote-only branches display correctly at any depth
- [x] Category nodes (Features, Releases, BugFixes, HotFixes, Support) still expand properly
- [x] Root-level branches (without any `/`) remain unaffected

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the code style of this project
- [x] I have tested my changes
- [x] My changes are backward compatible
- [x] Existing context menu commands still work correctly

## Related Issue

Closes #38

body: Closes #412. ## What OS back gesture on Diagnostics was popping two levels (Diagnostics → Main Settings) instead of one (Diagnostics → Security & Privacy → Main Settings). Two `settingsDetailName = null` assignments were erasing the intermediate breadcrumb. ## Fix Two surgical line removals in `MainShell`'s navigation dispatch: 1. **`onOpenDiagnostics`** (was: `sectionName=Diagnostics; settingsDetailName=null`). Stop clearing the detail on the way in — Security & Privacy is the only entry point, so preserving the detail value records the breadcrumb. 2. **`DiagnosticsScreen.onBack`** (was: `sectionName=Settings; settingsDetailName=null`). Leave the detail alone on the way back — it still holds `SecurityPrivacy`, so `SettingsScreen` re-enters that detail directly. The double-back then falls naturally out of `SettingsScreen`'s existing `BackHandler`: on a detail subscreen it pops to Settings home, and from Settings home it routes to chats. ## Why this is two lines, not a navigation refactor Both `sectionName` and `settingsDetailName` are already `rememberSaveable`, so the preserved breadcrumb survives config changes and process death. No new state, no new nav-graph entry — just stop the two over-eager resets. ## Test plan (manual) - Main → Security & Privacy → Diagnostics → **back** → lands on Security & Privacy. - Main → Security & Privacy → Diagnostics → back → back → lands on Main Settings. - Main → Security & Privacy → Diagnostics → back → back → back → lands on Chats. - Same checks via the system back button and the edge-swipe gesture. - Predictive back preview shows Security & Privacy (not Main) as the destination. ## Verification - Confirmed there is only one `onOpenDiagnostics()` call site (`DarkMatterApp.kt:13591`, the Diagnostics row in Security & Privacy). Preserving the detail can't mis-route from any other entry path. - `rememberSaveable` for both nav state values verified (`DarkMatterApp.kt:1044-1045`), so process death restores correctly. - Did not run connected-device tests (AGENTS.md guidance). ## Summary

- Lands SPEC-014 v0.8 Provider Portal as a single-file web bundle at `frontdoor/provider-portal/index.html` — AUTH-3 fail-CLOSED loader, AUTH-1 sign-in (in-memory only), AUTH-2 401/403/404 identical copy + stale-config guard, same-origin proxy fail-loud, all five surfaces (Machine, Setup & Updates, Earn, Monitoring placeholder, Identity).
- Adds `check-bundle.sh` build-time grep guard for AC 8(b) (privileged-key route + identifier isolation) + AC 8(f) (single-machine copy hygiene). Self-protected via Bash string concatenation so external scans with the same patterns produce zero matches on the script itself.
- Phases 1A / 1B / 1C each went through their own codex IMPL audit gate (0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM round-2 LOCK before the next phase began); single PR per the BUILD prompts' unified-branch plan.

## What ships

| Surface | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A — Machine | `/v1/pool/check` (same-origin) + `/providers/{id}/earnings` (same-origin) | A.1 header + A.2 counters + A.3 needs-attention. A.4 deferred (Open Q5/Q10). |
| B — Setup & Updates | SPEC-003 §5 FR-D1 + FR-D2 + §4 FR-C2 + SPEC-013 §6 + GitHub Releases API | B.1 grid + B.1a sizing + B.2 steps + B.3 feed (5-min cache, rate-limit + CORS fail-loud, plain-text body). No autotune banner per SPEC-013 NFR-4. |
| C — Earn | `/providers/{id}/earnings` (reuses Phase 1A cache) | C.1 credit totals + C.2 fiat-not-specified card (no Stripe / no bank-link / no payout-now). C.3/C.4 deferred (Open Q4). |
| D — Monitoring | none | Single placeholder card. **Zero network requests issued by the surface mount.** |
| E — Identity | `state.pool.data` lazy read | Read-only: provider_id / tier / state / coordinator base URL. No rotation, no removal, no notification toggles. |

## Privacy / security invariants enforced

- No `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` / `document.cookie` / `indexedDB` — session is in-memory only; page reload returns to sign-in.
- No remote command execution — every CTA is copy-to-clipboard; no POST/PUT/DELETE; no XHR; no WebSocket; no `sendBeacon`.
- No privileged-key routes referenced anywhere; no `operator_key` ever prompted, parsed, or transmitted.
- 403 and 404 render IDENTICAL "sign-in rejected" copy (SPEC-005 §11.5).
- After two consecutive 401/403/404 on the same surface, sign-in screen adds a stale-config notice ALONGSIDE the identical rejection copy.
- `require_provider_tokens` strict-`true` only; any other value (false, "true", 1, null) renders the SPEC-002 FR-P12 + SPEC-005 §11.5 explanation and makes zero further network calls.
- Release `body` rendered via `document.createTextNode` only — no `innerHTML` of remote data.
- Bundle never reads `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` as application data.

## Commit history on this branch

```
2c9e2dc feat(portal): SPEC-014 Phase 1C implementation + IMPL audit LOCK
0616b98 feat(portal): SPEC-014 Phase 1B implementation + IMPL audit LOCK
826b3cc audit(portal): SPEC-014 Phase 1A round 2 LOCK — both HIGH CLOSED, 0 new
5195418 spec(portal): unify SPEC-014 IMPL phases onto single branch + PR
3cd7787 feat(portal): SPEC-014 Phase 1A implementation (pre-fix; 2 HIGH open)
970d63e spec(portal): SPEC-014 v0.8 provider portal + 3 IMPL build prompts
```

Audit-loop findings closed across the three phases:

- Phase 1A round 1 → 2 HIGH (A.2 non-true flag-false unreachable; C.4 stale-config notice unreachable through retry flow). Round 2 LOCK.
- Phase 1B round 1 → 2 MEDIUM (C.4 unsupported SPEC-003 §6.2 cite on autotune step; H.1 raw hex literals in new CSS). Round 2 LOCK.
- Phase 1C round 1 → 1 MEDIUM (E.5 `check-bundle.sh` self-matched the `operator-key` regex from its own comments + echo messages). Round 2 LOCK.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (no required reviewers per [project memory](https://github.com/Augustas11/macprovider) — gating on whatever workflows exist).

author: toolchainlab
body:
💡 What: Replaced occurrences of `execute(...).scalars().first()` with direct `scalar(...)` executions across authentication endpoints and CLI commands. Also optimized `register_user` to fetch only the ID instead of the full ORM object for existence checks.
🎯 Why: Retrieving a single model instance or an identifier using `.scalars().first()` forces SQLAlchemy to parse and hydrate the full intermediate Result and ORM objects, causing unnecessary overhead for simple single-row or existence checks. Using `scalar(...)` is functionally identical but avoids this overhead.
📊 Impact: Reduces memory allocation and parsing CPU overhead in hot path authentication queries and single-user lookups.
🔬 Measurement: Verify tests run smoothly without regression (`uv run pytest`), and that the updated logic executes natively faster due to fewer intermediate structures generated by SQLAlchemy.

`/harness:harness` build. Adds a **.github-native agentic implementation loop** that auto-delivers a durable backlog (the HUT harness-upgrade targets) one-branch-one-PR into `develop`, gating each change on `make verify` + the repo doctors. The config/CI/docs sibling of `harness:forge-loop` (which targets Rust/cargo).

## Crew (all `model: opus`)
| Agent | Mutates | Job |
|-------|---------|-----|
| `org-change-architect` | no | plan + acceptance criteria + verify recipe |
| `org-change-implementer` | yes | execute on a branch, run the recipe, commit |
| `org-change-guardian` | no | independently run `make verify` + doctors; PASS/FAIL with evidence |
| `harness:evolution-steward` (reused) | proposes | per-cycle retrospective → harness upgrades |
| `harness:continuity-steward` (reused) | checkpoint | resume handoff at the cycle budget |

## Loop (Ralph pattern)
Durable backlog on disk → per cycle: branch → architect → implementer → guardian (gate on `make verify`) → PR into `develop` + arm auto-merge → record → evolution retrospective. Self-paces (3 cycles/session), checkpoints for zero-loss resume. **Guardrails:** never self-approves, never PRs `main`, never downgrades to pass, never edits secrets/clones repos/runs host installs (those → `needs-owner`), never stacks on a red trunk.

author: rmyndharis
body:
## Summary

Two small outbound-fetch hardening fixes.

### Bound SSRF DNS resolution by a deadline
`resolveSafeFetchTarget` resolved a hostname with an **unbounded** `dns.lookup`, so a hanging or very slow resolver could pin a worker indefinitely (the per-request fetch timeout did not cover the DNS phase). The lookup now races a deadline — default **10s**, overridable via `SSRF_DNS_TIMEOUT_MS` — and fails closed with `SsrfBlockedError` on expiry. The in-flight lookup is left to settle with its late result swallowed (no `unhandledRejection`). Because the deadline lives inside `resolveSafeFetchTarget`, it covers **every** caller (webhook delivery, server-side media fetch, and webhook registration) with no call-site changes. Healthy resolvers are unaffected (10s is generous for DNS).

### Case-insensitive remote-media detection (whatsapp-web.js)
The wwebjs adapter treated a media `data` string as a URL only when it had a **lowercase** `http://`/`https://` prefix, so a mixed-case scheme (e.g. `HTTPS://…`) was mistaken for base64 instead of being fetched through the SSRF-guarded `loadRemoteMedia` path — diverging from the Baileys engine. Extracted `isHttpUrl` (case-insensitive `/^https?:\/\//i`) and used it at both send sites, matching Baileys.

## Tests
- `ssrf-guard.spec.ts`: a never-resolving lookup is rejected within the deadline (`SSRF_DNS_TIMEOUT_MS=30`); all existing resolution/blocklist tests still pass.
- `whatsapp-web-js.adapter.spec.ts`: `isHttpUrl` treats mixed-case http(s) as URLs and base64/other as non-URLs.
- Full gate: lint 0 · build OK · 1081 unit · 26 e2e pass.

## Risk
Low. The DNS deadline only triggers on a genuinely hung/slow resolver (fails closed, the safe direction). The media-URL change broadens a too-narrow check; a base64 payload cannot validly begin with the ASCII bytes `http`/`https`, so no realistic base64 is misclassified.

author: jonasnobile
body:
Previously `deploy --remote` required a CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN. Cloudflare's
REST API accepts an OAuth access token as a Bearer token identically to an
API token, so we can authenticate with the credentials `wrangler login`
already stores on disk.

- CloudflareClient now takes a `getToken()` provider instead of a static
  token, fetched per request so a refreshed token is picked up mid-run.
- New src/auth.ts reads wrangler's default.toml (mirroring its config-path
  resolution), returns the access token while valid, and refreshes via the
  OAuth token endpoint when expired — persisting the rotated token back to
  the same file so wrangler stays in sync.
- deploy.ts prefers an explicit --api-token / CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and falls
  back to OAuth; run.ts accepts either for the --remote credential check.

API-token and CI behavior are unchanged. account_id is still required.

## Verification (live, throwaway env)

Ran self-cleaning create→delete probes using real `wrangler login` OAuth creds
against the `nobile` account to settle whether the login scopes cover resources
oblaka provisions (the open question was D1/R2/Vectorize, which have no dedicated
scope in wranglerʼs login set):

| Resource | Create | Cleanup |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | `200` | `200` |
| Queues | `200` | `200` |
| Vectorize | `201` | `200` |
| R2 | `403` (product not enabled on this account) | — |

- D1 and Vectorize are authorized under OAuth despite having no dedicated scope —
  Cloudflare authorizes them via account membership.
- The R2 `403` was a *product-not-enabled* message, not an auth rejection, so it is
  not conclusive; indirect evidence (a product-level error rather than a 9109-style
  auth error) suggests the token is scope-accepted. Not retested on an R2-enabled
  account.
- `GET /accounts` → `200` confirms the token-provider path end-to-end; cleanup left
  0 leftover resources.

author: guneygaar
body:
## What

At cutover, `loadComments` attributed every migrated comment's `author_user_id` to the operator, so the original v1 author was lost on the v2 row. The v1 read-only DB still holds the real author per comment. This is a one-time, idempotent backfill that copies the original author's name and email onto the **migrated comments only**, into `comments.legacy_author_name` + `comments.legacy_author_email`.

It does **not** change the `author_user_id` FK (it stays the operator). **Posts and `post_versions` are intentionally out of scope: their blank authors have nothing recoverable in v1**, so there is no analogous backfill for them.

## How

- New `packages/etl/src/backfill-comment-authors.ts` adds a `backfill-comment-authors` subcommand (mode `dry-run` default / `apply`), wired **only** via a dispatch branch in `index.ts` (dispatched before the migration CLI parse so its own `--mode` flag never reaches `parseCli`).
- Generates a `uuid_v7` trace id at entry and logs it.
- Reuses the v1 source + v2 target connections and the safety guards (`sameDatabase`, `targetRefMatches`) from `config.ts`; resolves the target workspace **by name** from existing config/env. No hardcoded connection strings, project ids, or workspace uuid.
- Reads v1 once, paged (1000), joining `post_comments` → `posts` → `profiles`.
- Pure, unit-tested derivations: `legacyName` (profile_name then `btrim(author)`, truncate 120, empty → null), `legacyEmail` (`lower(btrim(author))` when a standard email, else null, max 320), and `expectedBody` via the existing `commentBody(scrub=false)` so it equals the stored v2 body exactly.
- Builds the active GBL member email set in **one** query; a row whose author email is already a live member (e.g. the operator) is skipped.
- Matches each remaining row to its v2 comment by `workspace_id` + post + `date_trunc('milliseconds', created_at)` + exact `body` + `legacy_author_name IS NULL`, via a **TEMP staging table + one set-based UPDATE**. Counts 0 / >1 matches in both directions (would-fill, skipped-member, no-match, ambiguous).
- New `workflow_dispatch`-only `.github/workflows/backfill-comment-authors.yml` with a single `mode` input, reusing etl-run's secrets/env block and Node 22 + pnpm setup.
- Pure-function unit tests ride the existing etl CI (no new CI workflow).

## Explicit disclosures

- **Separate read/write pools:** the v1 pool is opened read-only (`default_transaction_read_only=on`); the v2 pool is the write pool. Both are opened at entry and closed in `finally`.
- **Single apply transaction:** in `apply`, the temp staging populate + the one set-based `UPDATE` are wrapped in a single `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`. `dry-run` runs the same staging inside a transaction that is rolled back, so it writes nothing.
- **Idempotency guard:** the `legacy_author_name IS NULL` match condition means a previously filled comment is no longer a candidate, so a second `apply` fills 0.
- **Ambiguity safety:** if any staging row matches >1 comment, or any comment is claimed by >1 staging row, `apply` rolls back the whole transaction and exits non-zero with the ambiguous keys logged. Never guesses.
- **Posts/`post_versions` intentionally out of scope:** nothing recoverable in v1.
- **No schema change:** `legacy_author_name` / `legacy_author_email` already exist on the v2 `comments` table (verified against the live DB; recording them into `schema.md`/generated types is a separate, out-of-scope PR). No DDL, no `supabase db push`. The v1 source layer stays SELECT-only; nothing touches v1.

## Verification

- `tsc -p tests/etl/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean
- etl suite green (104 tests) + new file (15 tests)
- `eslint` + `prettier --check` clean on touched files
- offline `--dry-run` self-check unchanged; subcommand dispatch + arg validation confirmed

## QA Investigation Fix: 23f3bc40df2d

**Butler:** lifestyle
**Error:** RuntimeError
**Call site:** <unknown>:<unknown>
**Fingerprint:** `23f3bc40df2d09dc52fa9579930faaf8084d051881d2555e40f92fd921cfcbdf`
**Attempt ID:** `dbc5723f-95df-4c69-90e6-113766b48b66`
**Discovery source:** session_records
**Occurrences:** 1
**First seen:** 2026-06-21T12:17:44.629354+00:00
**Last seen:** 2026-06-21T12:17:49.517352+00:00

### Root Cause
OpenCode can return provider API failures as JSON on stdout, with the actionable message nested under `[REDACTED-HOST]`. The adapter treated that nested shape as an unrecognized payload, so it surfaced the raw JSON blob instead of the compact provider error.

The failover classifier also did not recognize provider balance or credit exhaustion as a pre-tool-call systemic rejection. With no captured tool calls, that kind of runtime failure should be eligible for same-tier failover, but it was classified as an unknown runtime error and persisted as a failed session.

### Fix Summary
The OpenCode error-detail parser now descends into `data` payloads, allowing nested provider errors such as `[REDACTED-HOST]` to become a concise `error_detail`.

The failover classifier now treats insufficient balance, insufficient credits, and credit balance exhaustion as quota/billing rejection markers in the existing pre-work rate-limit category. That lets the spawner fail over to another same-tier candidate when no side-effecting tool calls were captured.

### Test Coverage
Added OpenCode adapter coverage for nested `[REDACTED-HOST]` extraction and invocation metadata, and classifier coverage for provider balance/credit exhaustion messages. Focused adapter/classifier suites pass; full pytest was attempted but the environment lacks Docker and the deployment-form smoke test timed out while downloading dependencies.

`/sources` is **scope-token gated**, so the source list + add-source + sync require the **operator principal** (the user-id bearer is rejected — confirmed 401). **Upload** is per-workspace (any member), so the dropzone stays available even without operator access (a calm note explains the rest).

body:
## Summary

Three changes bundled — CI/infra hardening that pairs naturally with the analytics work that just shipped (#223), plus the Cafe24 tabbed product editor your boss flagged in the latest reference review.

### 1. CI hardening — `next build` in PR checks
PR #223's runtime bundler bug (geoip-country reading its own package.json) slipped through because PR checks only ran `tsc + eslint`, and the failure only surfaces in `next build`'s "Collecting page data" phase. Added a `next build` step using the same Supabase secrets as the post-merge workflow. Catches this entire class of "static analysis OK but runtime resolution fails" bug pre-merge.

### 2. Infra hardening — `ANALYTICS_IP_SALT` wired through terraform
- New terraform variable `analytics_ip_salt` (sensitive, default `""`).
- Plumbed into the EC2 user-data env-file (`/etc/kokkok/env`).
- `/api/track`'s `hashIp()` now reads a real per-deployment salt instead of falling back to the Supabase URL.
- **Set the value in `infrastructure/secrets.auto.tfvars`** (untracked):
  ```
  analytics_ip_salt = "fd9e415218ba02131e304978c85a995ad59b9769ba6c07237786c942b6eb7fe5"
  ```
  (or roll your own — `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"`)
- Rotating the salt invalidates every existing `analytics.ip_hash` row — the canonical "reset repeat-visitor tracking" operation.

### 3. Cafe24-style tabbed ProductDetailModal
Cafe24's product page is a horizontal tab strip. Ours was one long scrolling form. Restructured to 4 tabs covering the data we actually have:
- **기본정보** → image + name / summary / ingredient / category
- **판매정보** → price + originalPrice + naver url + cart/buy buttons
- **상세정보** → detail components editor
- **SEO설정** → existing ProductSeoSettings section

**Tab chrome** matches Cafe24's exact signature:
- White bg with thin bottom border
- Active tab: blue text + 2px blue border-bottom (`#1565c0` matching the sidebar active state)
- Inactive: gray text
- `role="tablist"` + `aria-selected` for keyboard a11y

**Footer pinned** below the scrollable form so save buttons stay reachable regardless of which tab's content is tallest. Save button color picked up `#1565c0` for visual consistency with the sidebar.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a PR with a deliberate import error → PR checks should fail at the `next build` step
- [ ] After rebuild with salt set: `curl /api/track` records `ip_hash` derived from the new salt (different from Supabase-URL fallback)
- [ ] /admin/products → click any product → modal shows 4 horizontal tabs at the top, blue active state on the current tab
- [ ] Switch from 기본정보 to 판매정보 → name field's input is preserved on switch back
- [ ] Save button at the bottom triggers the form submit regardless of which tab is active

## Summary
- Adds 2 real \`@OnEvent\` subscribers to the Trigger.dev webhook router shipped in #1537
- \`TriggerRunStatusSubscriber\` flips \`work_generation_history\` rows by \`triggerRunId\` match on \`run.{succeeded,failed,cancelled}\` (no migration — existing column)
- \`TriggerRunFailureSentryBreadcrumbSubscriber\` routes \`run.failed\` + \`deployment.failed\` to Sentry with \`runId\` / \`tenantId\` / error attrs; falls back to Nest \`Logger\` when SentryService isn't bound (offline/test).

## Why these two
- **Persistence** is the most actionable: closes the loop on records stuck in \`generating\` after Trigger.dev completed the run.
- **Sentry breadcrumb** gives bounded + cheap operator visibility into Trigger.dev failures without polluting the exceptions stream.

## Decisions
- Wrote to existing \`WorkGenerationHistory.status\` (no migration).
- Used \`SentryService.error\` rather than \`addBreadcrumb\` because EventEmitter2 handlers run outside the request hub.
- Both subscribers wrap handler bodies in try/catch + log to honour the router contract (never throw → no poisoning of other subscribers).
- Idempotency: persistence short-circuits when the row is already terminal; Sentry side is naturally idempotent.

## Tests
- 17 new (9 + 8): happy paths per terminal status, idempotency, missing record, payload missing run.id, repo throws, channel purity, Sentry-absent fallback.
- Full \`apps/api\` suite: 2974/2974 passing.
- \`type-check\` clean.

author: ikrysanov
body:
## [0.5.2] - 2026-06-21

### Added
- `PytestOperator(parallel=..., dist=...)` -- run a suite in parallel **on the
  worker** via ``pytest-xdist``. ``parallel`` is the worker count (an int, or
  ``"auto"``/``"logical"`` for xdist's CPU/logical-core keywords) and maps to
  ``-n``; ``dist`` selects the scheduler mode (``--dist``: ``load``,
  ``loadscope``, ``loadfile``, ``loadgroup``, ``worksteal``, ``each``, ``no``)
  and requires ``parallel``. The flags are applied to the first full run only --
  the in-process ``rerun_failed`` rounds stay serial, where worker startup would
  cost more than it saves -- and are skipped in ``dry_run``. If ``pytest_args``
  already drives ``-n``/``--numprocesses`` the operator defers to it entirely
  (and skips ``dist``), so parallelism is never configured from both sides.
  Validated at construction (bad worker count -> ``TypeError``/``ValueError``;
  unknown ``dist`` mode or ``dist`` without ``parallel`` -> ``ValueError``).
  Needs the new ``[xdist]`` extra (``pip install
  'airflow-pytest-operator[xdist]'``) on the worker; defaults ``None`` (serial,
  unchanged behaviour).
- `PytestOperator(markers=..., keyword=...)` -- ergonomic, discoverable sugar
  for pytest's ``-m`` / ``-k`` selectors (e.g. ``markers="smoke and not slow"``,
  ``keyword="login or logout"``). Both are templated, are spliced into the first
  full run (and narrow ``dry_run`` collection), defer to an explicit ``-m``/``-k``
  in ``pytest_args``, and are skipped when they render empty. Equivalent to
  putting the flags in ``pytest_args``, but they read clearly in the DAG.
  Defaults ``None``.
- Sharding across workers via dynamic task mapping (the second, cross-worker axis
  of parallelism, orthogonal to ``parallel``/xdist). Two public, pure helpers:
  ``parse_collect_only_output(stdout)`` pulls node-ids out of
  ``pytest --collect-only -q`` output, and ``partition_node_ids(node_ids,
  num_shards)`` splits them into up to ``num_shards`` balanced, contiguous,
  never-empty groups. A ``collect -> partition -> .expand(test_path=groups)`` DAG
  runs one mapped ``PytestOperator`` per shard; each shard can still set
  ``parallel`` to xdist within its worker, and ``failed_only`` scopes per shard
  via the ``map_index`` in the Variable key. See ``examples/sharded_mapped.py``.

### Changed
- Internal: the operator's option vocabulary (the accepted ``dist`` modes, retry
  strategies, collect-only aliases, etc.) and the ``has_flag`` arg helper moved
  to ``operators/_constants.py`` to keep ``pytest_operator.py`` focused on
  orchestration. No public API or behaviour change.
- Internal: pytest configuration moved from ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` in
  ``pyproject.toml`` to a top-level ``pytest.ini`` (single source). Allure report
  generation is opt-in via ``ALLURE_DIR`` (handled in ``tests/conftest.py``), so
  the bare-pytest CI job stays green. The large ``test_operator.py`` /
  ``test_subprocess_runner.py`` suites were split into per-feature modules under
  ``tests/operator/`` and ``tests/runner/`` with shared fakes in a ``_*_helpers``
  module; same tests, no behaviour change.
- Dev: added ``.pre-commit-config.yaml`` mirroring CI -- ruff (lint + format) and
  file hygiene on commit, ``mypy`` and a fast unit subset on push. Uses the
  project's own pinned tools (``language: system``) so pre-commit, CI, and the
  dev venv never drift.

### Fixed
- `PytestOperator(env=...)` now rejects non-string keys/values at construction
  with a clear ``TypeError`` (naming the offending key), instead of failing
  deep in ``subprocess``/``os.fsencode`` with a cryptic
  ``expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not bool`` at execute time.
- ``dist`` is no longer emitted twice when ``pytest_args`` already contains
  ``--dist`` (without ``-n``): the operator now defers to the user's explicit
  ``--dist`` rather than appending a second one that xdist would silently win.

author: yuxuetr

## Summary

P-A2.4 (step 1 of 2): extract the shared **workflow-assembly** crate so `agentflow-server` can assemble/schedule workflows without depending on the CLI binary crate — the first move toward burning the tracked `server → cli` dependency edge.

The YAML workflow **config schema** (`config::v2::{FlowDefinitionV2, NodeDefinitionV2}`, `config::schema`) and the **executor** that compiles it into an `agentflow-core` `Flow` (`executor::build_flow_from_yaml` + the node factories) moved from `agentflow-cli` into a new `agentflow-config` crate.

## Strangler-fig — consumers unchanged

- `agentflow-cli` re-exports `agentflow_config::{config, executor}` under their original paths and forwards its `plugin` / `rag` / `mcp` feature flags, so every CLI consumer (and internal `crate::config` / `crate::executor` reference) compiles unchanged.
- `agentflow-server` now imports `build_flow_from_yaml` (`runs.rs`) and the V2 schema types (`scheduler::distributed`) from `agentflow-config`, enabling the same capability features the CLI's defaults provided.
- The new crate mirrors the CLI's feature flags (plus an optional `agentflow-tracing` dep the plugin path needs for traceparent propagation).

## Honest scope — edge not burned *yet*

This repoints **2 of 3** server→cli usages. The third — the doctor diagnostics `build_report` (server's `/diagnostics` endpoint) — is deferred to step 2 because the doctor command's `execute` couples to the CLI's `json_envelope`, so the report builder needs a careful split from its command handler. The `server → cli` allowlist entry therefore stays for now and `check-arch` still tracks it; it burns when step 2 lands.

## Verification

`cargo build --workspace --all-targets` clean · feature combos (`cli --no-default-features` / `--features mcp` / `--all-features` / `agentflow-config --features mcp,rag,plugin`) all build · **no test loss** — the moved tests run in `agentflow-config` (21 with all features) + cli 159 + server 180 green · `clippy -D warnings` clean · `fmt` clean · `check-arch` OK · `check-changelog` PASS. CI feature matrix gains direct `agentflow-config` checks.

author: delivstat
body:
## What

Slice 2 of context compression: promote it from an **env-only** knob (slice 1, #361) to a **declarative `context_compression:` block** in `workspace.yaml` — topology-as-data — with env vars still overriding per deployment.

```yaml
# workspace.yaml
context_compression:
  backend: columnar   # off (default) | columnar
  min_bytes: 2000     # payloads smaller than this are left untouched
```

Design: `design/details/context-compression.md` (status → slice 2 built).

## How

**Schema (full dual-surface change):**
- `packages/schema/schemas/workspace.schema.json` — new `context_compression` `$defs` (`backend` enum `off|columnar`, `min_bytes` integer ≥ 0) + property ref.
- Synced the **bundled `_schemas/` copy** (the Python validator prefers it in dev/test).
- Regenerated pydantic (`ContextCompression` model) + TS types — committed, idempotent (no codegen drift).
- Fixtures: `full.yaml` exercises the block; two invalid fixtures (`context-compression-bad-backend`, `context-compression-negative-min-bytes`); `reference/workspace.yaml` example.

**Runtime:**
- `build_compressor(cfg)` + `resolve_min_bytes(cfg)` resolve **env → workspace block → default** (off / 2000). Env stays the per-deployment override; the block makes intent declarative and ejectable.
- `WorkspaceRuntime.run` reads `context_compression` from the parsed workspace, sets the active compressor + min-bytes per run, clears both in `finally`.
- `_effective_min_bytes()` prefers the per-run value, falling back to env/default so the standalone gate keeps working.

**Docs gap fixed (pre-existing):** `schema-change-discipline.md` never mentioned syncing the bundled `_schemas/` copy — but the Python validator prefers `_schemas/` in dev/test, so an un-synced copy silently validates against the *old* shape. Added it as step 2 of the checklist.

## Precedence

| Knob | env | workspace block | default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| backend | `SWARMKIT_CONTEXT_COMPRESSION` | `context_compression.backend` | `off` |
| min bytes | `SWARMKIT_CONTEXT_COMPRESSION_MIN_BYTES` | `context_compression.min_bytes` | `2000` |

## Tests

`packages/runtime/tests/test_compression.py` extended (38 tests total): workspace-block resolution, env-overrides-block both directions (env columnar over block off, env off over block columnar), `resolve_min_bytes` precedence, and the active-min-bytes gate. Schema fixtures validated (valid passes; both invalids rejected on the right field).

- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check`: clean
- `mypy packages/runtime packages/schema/python`: Success, 0 errors
- `pytest` (runtime + schema): **1159 passed**
- TS: `@swarmkit/schema` 119 tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean
- Codegen idempotent (no drift)

## Deferred (slice 3+)

Per-surface lossy/reversible policy, lossy backends + reversible `*_retrieve`, OTel spans for compression, doc-retrieval lossless lever.

Bumps **swarmkit-schema → 1.4.0**, **swarmkit-runtime → 1.7.0**.

body:
Polish the agent detail page tables for a consistent, less-cluttered UI (the 5 tables: native memory, unmanaged skills, direct MCP servers, plugins, conversations) plus the redundant "recall" heading.

## Shared building blocks
- **DataTable**: new server-pagination mode (page on demand via `limit`/`offset` + `total`) and a controlled-search option; type interfaces split to `DataTable.types.ts` (re-exported) to stay under the file-size cap.
- **RowActions**: a primary button + a `⋯` overflow menu (Popover) so crowded rows stop sprawling. File open/reveal actions live in `useFileActionItems` (`lib/fileActionItems.ts`) so they render inline (`FileActions`) or as menu items.

## Per table
| Table | Search | Bulk actions | Row buttons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native memory | ✅ added | Import to Coffer | Import + ⋯ (editor/Finder) |
| Unmanaged skills | existing | Adopt (eligible only) + Delete | inline |
| Direct MCP servers | existing | Adopt (default keychain refs) + Remove | inline |
| Plugins | existing | Enable/Disable + Uninstall | inline |
| Conversations | server-side | Distill to memory | Distill + ⋯ (editor/Finder) |

- Destructive bulk actions each own a confirm dialog (encapsulated in the bulk-actions component).
- **Conversations** rewritten onto the shared DataTable: page-based pagination that loads on demand (was load-more). Project/time filters dropped for parity; the message-count / start / last-activity columns stay **sortable** (server-side sort+order, default last-activity desc). Rows are keyed by `source_path` (one session_id can span several transcript files — subagent sidechains — so it is not unique per row).
- Only conversations uses server pagination (large/unbounded, backend already supports limit/offset). Small bounded resource lists stay client-side by design.

Merges latest `main` (incl. #185 drop-open-folder-button, reconciled in `FileActions`).

## Not a code change
Empty conversation title / last-activity in the UI was a **stale running daemon** (Python doesn't hot-reload modules), not a bug — restarting the dev daemon populates them.

## Test plan
- `make verify` green (lint + unit/integration/contract/acceptance; 281 scenarios).
- Frontend: 800+ existing + new tests pass (DataTable server-pagination & controlled search, RowActions, conversations rewrite incl. sort + source_path keying, unmanaged-skills bulk adopt/delete).

author: bluevulpine
body:
## Problem

The `dragonfly-operator` (v1.6.x) provisions a PodDisruptionBudget per Dragonfly cluster, but its hand-maintained `ClusterRole` (`kubernetes/apps/database/dragonfly/app/rbac.yaml`) lacked `policy/poddisruptionbudgets` access.

Without list/watch, the PDB informer cache never syncs and crashloops the operator (observed **1400+ restarts** on a replica). The operator silently stops reconciling: CR spec image bumps were applied to the `Dragonfly` CR but **never rolled the StatefulSet**, leaving the data pods stuck on `v1.36.0` while git had advanced through `v1.38.1` → `v1.39.0`.

Observed operator log:
```
Failed to watch *v1.PodDisruptionBudget: poddisruptionbudgets.policy is forbidden:
User "system:serviceaccount:database:dragonfly-operator" cannot list resource
"poddisruptionbudgets" in API group "policy" at the cluster scope
```

## Fix

Add the `policy/poddisruptionbudgets` rule, mirroring the [upstream operator role](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly-operator/blob/v1.6.1/manifests/dragonfly-operator.yaml) verb set. Same class of fix as the earlier `configmaps` addition.

author: veho-domi
body:
## B1 — the Study Path (guided unlock progression)

The guided **learn** spine: a per-unit node map at `/learn/[slug]` — teach, drill in graduated steps, then gate the unit behind a checkpoint, with unlock-on-completion and per-node stars. Builds on Smart Review (A3) + streaks/outbox (A4); the game layer (P2) later reuses the same progression.

> **Stacked PR.** Base is `feat/streaks-outbox` ([domigo-v2#24](https://github.com/VEHO-DOMI/domigo-v2/pull/24), A4) because B1 re-edits `home/page.tsx` + `middleware.ts`. Merge order: A3 (#23) → A4 (#24) → this. GitHub auto-retargets as each merges.

### What it delivers
- **Derived node graph** — pure `buildUnitNodes(vocab, grammar)` emits, per unit, `vocab-intro` (teaching) → `vocab-practice-{1,2,3}` → `grammar-intro` → `grammar-practice-{1,2,3}` → `checkpoint`, generating only the difficulties that have items. Node ids are the stable DB/API contract.
- **Sparse progress model** — additive `domigo_v2.study_path_progress` (`0002`): a row exists **iff** a node is completed; locked/available/stars are **derived** by pure `withProgress`. `recordNodeCompletion` keeps the **best** stars (`GREATEST`).
- **Teaching nodes** — `loadWordbank`/`loadUnitStructures` (new content-loader exports) feed `VocabIntroView`/`GrammarIntroView` (new in task-ui) — **student-safe**: German rule text + bilingual examples, never the teacher-facing English grammar names.
- **Graded nodes** reuse `task-ui` + the existing **`/api/attempts` outbox** with `mode:"study:<nodeId>"`, so every answer feeds the **Leitner review queue + streak + XP** automatically (Smart Review *is* the path's spaced re-practice). A thin **`/api/study-path`** records node completion — it **re-derives stars server-side** from the tier tally and **validates the node id against the graph** (a client can't fabricate completions).
- **Checkpoint** — a deterministic ~10-item cumulative sample from the unit's own items, **hints off** (new `hideHint` prop), as the unit's gate.
- **Server-enforced unlock** — a locked-node URL **307-redirects** to the map (hidden links are cosmetic; the route is the gate). Home gains a Study Path card; `/learn` index shows per-unit progress badges.

### Verification
Gate green: `pnpm -r run typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm -r run test && pnpm content validate && pnpm build`. **14 new `studypath` unit tests** (graph / stars / unlock / checkpoint determinism).

Live dev-DB E2E (throwaway `PathKid`, cleaned up):
- `0002` applied to the dev branch — `public` **13 → 13** (additive confirmed).
- login → `/learn` renders → `/learn/g1-u01` map shows **vocab-intro available, the rest locked**.
- complete vocab-intro → the map advances (**vocab-intro ✓, vocab-practice-1 now available**).
- **unlock gate:** `GET /learn/g1-u01/checkpoint` while locked → **307 → `/learn/g1-u01`**.
- two attempts with `mode=study:vocab-practice-1` → land in **`practice_attempts` + `review_queue`** (Smart Review fed) and return a streak.
- node completion @ 100% → **stars=3**; re-run @ 50% → **stays 3** (keep-best).
- all seeded rows removed; `public` back to baseline.

### Scope / decisions
Granular nodes (practice split by difficulty); checkpoint sampled from the unit (no separate Check-up corpus yet). **Deferred:** a game-style/Phaser map (this is a clean functional node list), variety-on-replay checkpoints, a shared `<Stepper>` refactor, teacher view of path progress.

Left unmerged for review.

author: bartegu
body:
Hi! I ran into an issue where the card failed to initialize on newer Home Assistant versions using the Sections layout, either hanging indefinitely in the background or throwing a "No config found" warning. 

After digging into the code, I found two main causes. First, the configuration lookup only scanned `view.cards` one level deep, completely missing cards placed inside the new native Sections layout (`view.sections`) or deeply nested grid/stack structures. Second, if the dashboard config wasn't immediately loaded, the original polling loop had no exit condition, trapping the script in an infinite loop.

To fix this, I refactored the config discovery into a clean recursive search that handles both legacy layouts and modern sections at any nesting depth. I also cleaned up the DOM selector and added a 5-second timeout safeguard to the polling logic to prevent infinite background loops.
