author: meldxkviel
body:
## What & why

Instagram carousel posts were sent as a media-group **album** (photos only) or collapsed to a single item. This makes a multi-item Instagram post (photos **and/or videos**) arrive as a real **swipeable Telegram carousel** — the new `<tg-slideshow>` rich-message block from **Bot API 10.1** (`sendRichMessage`), exactly the feature requested.

No `aiogram` upgrade needed — **3.29 already ships the Bot API 10.1 types** (`InputRichMessage`, `SendRichMessage`, `RichBlockSlideshow`, …).

## How it works

Rich-message media accepts **only public http(s) URLs** — `InputRichMessage` carries just an HTML string, so `file_id`/`attach://` aren't possible. Each slide therefore references the original **Instagram CDN URL** (the same kind Telegram already fetches for link previews):

```html
<tg-slideshow>``<img src="…1.jpg"/><video src="…2.mp4"/>``<figcaption>caption</figcaption></tg-slideshow>
```

Ordered slides (`DownloadResult.carousel_slides`) come from two paths:
- **photo carousels** — the CDN URL of each image `_try_instagram_photo` downloads
- **carousels with video** — harvested from the yt-dlp playlist `info["entries"]` inside `_download_sync` (no extra network calls). `_entry_to_slide` / `_best_entry_media_url` pick a progressive MP4 per video slide and the largest image per photo slide.

The handler builds the HTML (`_build_slideshow_html`) and sends it via `_send_rich_carousel`.

## Safety / fallback

If the rich send fails for **any** reason (Bot API server without rich support, a URL Telegram can't fetch), the handler falls back to the **downloaded local media** — album/single photo for photo posts, single video otherwise. **Worst case equals the previous behavior.** `carousel_slides` is cached/restored alongside `file_path`/`photo_paths`, and the post caption is preserved from the playlist title (captured before the playlist collapses to its first entry).

## Tests

11 new tests in `tests/unit/test_carousel.py` (slide-URL extraction for photo + mixed carousels, the yt-dlp `entry → slide` heuristics, cache round-trip, and the `<tg-slideshow>` HTML builder/escaping). Full suite: **656 passed**, ruff check + format clean.

## Notes / follow-ups

- The rich carousel itself can't be exercised against a live bot here; the API model serialization was verified and the fallback guarantees no regression.
- Video carousels still download the post media for the fallback (pre-existing behavior — no speed regression, but a future optimization could fetch slide URLs without downloading).
- Inline mode (`@bot <url>`) still sends only the first slide (Telegram can't edit an inline placeholder into a rich carousel).

author: aparajon
body:
## Why this matters

A process that embeds SchemaBot as a Go module (its own `serve.Run` caller) may need to run schema changes against a database type this build does not implement natively. The pieces existed — `Service.RegisterEngine` and `LocalConfig.EngineFactories` — but they were unreachable from `serve.Run`: the `Service` is created *inside* `Run`, and the data-plane gRPC/router client factory never set `EngineFactories`. So an embedder could not register an engine, and a custom database type on the gRPC/router path failed with `no engine registered`.

## What it does

Adds `serve.WithEngine(databaseType, factory)` so an embedder can supply an `Engine` without the core depending on its package. `Run` then:

- registers each factory on the `Service` (validated by `RegisterEngine`, failing startup on a bad type or nil factory) so the operator's in-process clients resolve the custom type; and
- threads the same factories into the data-plane `LocalClientFactory` so the gRPC/router path resolves it too.

```
serve.Run(ctx, cfg, WithEngine("customdb", factory))
        ├── svc.RegisterEngine(...)           → operator in-process clients
        └── grpcLocalClientFactory(..., engines) → data-plane gRPC/router clients
```

Both the operator and the data plane share one set of registered engines, so a custom database type resolves identically on either path. The built-in MySQL/Vitess types are unaffected; an unregistered custom type still fails closed.

This is the embeddability seam for supplying an out-of-tree engine; it composes with the existing `WithLogger`/`WithBuildInfo` options.

*This PR was written by Claude (Opus 4.8).*

author: pofallon
body:
## What you saw
```
✗  AWS credentials — aws exited 254
```

## What it means (verified)
- **Valid local-env creds ARE picked up correctly.** The wizard captures `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` / `AWS_REGION` from the environment into the config, and the check passes — confirmed by running the exact check command (`aws sts get-caller-identity` → exit 0) and reproducing the full wizard → check (pass).
- **Exit 254 = AWS *rejected* the credentials** used at that moment (signature/token mismatch or expired), not a pickup failure.

## The bug this fixes
The check threw away the *reason*. The aws CLI prefixes its error with blank lines:
```
\n\naws: [ERROR]: An error occurred (SignatureDoesNotMatch) when calling the GetCallerIdentity operation: ...
```
…and `firstLine` took `split('\n')[0]` — the empty first line — so the detail fell back to the useless `aws exited 254`. An operator couldn't tell an expired key, a wrong secret, or a typo apart.

**Fix:** return the first **non-empty** line, so the detail now reads e.g. `An error occurred (SignatureDoesNotMatch) ...` or `The security token included in the request is invalid` (ExpiredToken).

## Changes
- `install/checks.ts` — `firstLine` returns the first non-empty trimmed line.
- `__tests__/checks.test.ts` (new) — covers pass, blank-line-prefixed error (real reason surfaced), truly-empty-stderr fallback, and aws-not-found → warn.

## Test
`bun --cwd packages/cli test` → 101 pass · typecheck · lint ✅
Verified live: a deliberately-wrong secret now reports `An error occurred (SignatureDoesNotMatch) ...` instead of `aws exited 254`.

The `changes` job used `dorny/paths-filter` with a `['**/*', '!**/*.md', …]` list. The action's `some`-glob

author: romaost
body:
**Description:**
This PR adds a driver for Panasonic Aquarea heat pumps connected via [Heishamon](https://github.com/Egyjs/HeishaMon), a popular ESP32-based MQTT bridge that replaces the original CZ-TAW1 Wi-Fi module.

**What it does**
Subscribes to Heishamon's MQTT topics and emits live metrics: outside temperature, inlet/outlet temperature, target temperature and Zone 1 heat curve offset
Supports heat curve offset control via set_heat_curve_offset action (range -3..+3 °C, configurable)
Returns to safe offset (0) on driver_default_mode() and driver_cleanup() so the pump falls back to its own heat curve if 42W stops

**Tested on**
Heat pump: Panasonic Aquarea WH-SXC09H3E8 (H-series)
Heishamon: Large board, firmware v4.1.6 on ESP32
Broker: Mosquitto (core-mosquitto) on Home Assistant Green
42W: v0.121.0

Configuration example
drivers:
  - name: heishamon
    lua: drivers/heishamon.lua
    capabilities:
      mqtt:
        host: core-mosquitto
        port: 1883
        username: mqtt-user
        password: your-password
    config:
      base_topic: panasonic_heat_pump
      min_offset: -3
      max_offset: 3
      safe_offset: 0

**Notes**
Heishamon supports H, J, K, L and M-series Aquarea pumps – this driver should work with all of them
The driver uses host.emit("battery", { w = 0, soc = 1.0 }) as a heartbeat to keep last_success updated – pending proper heatpump emit type in a future 42W release (see issue #520)
Three-level offset control (-3/0/+3) based on price + battery SoC is currently handled in HA automations; flexload integration can be added when 42W supports discrete setpoint levels

body:
Closes #5288

Recognize alternative error-handling derive libraries (snafu, miette, derive_more, error-stack) as satisfying the rule's intent; crates using them are no longer pushed toward thiserror. Library crates hand-rolling error types with no error-derive library still flagged.

## Detection (structural, root cause)

- Per-file source: bail when the file imports/derives any recognized error library (`use snafu::…`, `#[derive(Snafu)]`) — `ERROR_DERIVE_IMPORT_ROOTS` (Rust path-segment spelling).
- Crate manifest: new `CargoManifest::uses_error_derive_crate` (mirrors the existing `async_runtime` / `is_xml_parser_crate_name` patterns) bails when the nearest `Cargo.toml` declares one as a dependency — covering a derive that lives in a sibling file.

## Error-derive set

`thiserror`, `snafu`, `miette`, `derive_more`/`derive-more`, `error-stack` (both `-`/`_` spellings). Application aggregators (`anyhow`/`eyre`) are intentionally excluded.

## Tests

- snafu source / miette source not flagged; crate depending on snafu not flagged.
- hand-rolled `impl Display`+`impl Error` with no error-derive library still flagged (len == 1).

body:
## Summary
Adds support for proxying a target on a non-default port. Previously the proxy always reached the target on the protocol's default port (80/443) with no way to specify, e.g., port 5443.

## Changes
- **`worker.js`** — after setting the target host, apply an optional `port` override:
  ```js
  url.protocol = target.protocol;
  url.host = target.host;
  if (target.port) {
      url.port = target.port;
  }
  ```
  When `port` is omitted, behavior is unchanged (protocol default port is used).
- **`reverse_demo.js`** — documented the new optional `port` field.

## Usage
```js
"myproxy.example.org": {
    "protocol": "https",
    "host": "backend.example.com",
    "port": 5443,
    ...
}
```

## Testing
Verified via a Node \`URL\` test that setting \`url.port\` produces \`https://backend.example.com:5443/...\`, and that omitting \`port\` yields the default-port URL (no behavior change).

author: mariosigkiempor
body:
## Summary

Implements Slice 3 of the roadmap: completes the `Response` reading surface and establishes the return-based error model. HTTP error statuses (4xx/5xx) are no longer thrown — they resolve as successful round-trips. Callers obtain failures as values via `response.toResult()`, which returns `Result<Response, RequestError>`. The core throws only the network `FatalRequestError`.

## Key Changes

- **`RequestError` class** (`src/errors/RequestError.ts`): A single error class (not a hierarchy) carrying a `kind` discriminant (`'notFound'`, `'unauthorized'`, `'serverError'`, etc.) in place of SaloonPHP's status-class tree. Implements `createRequestError(response)` factory that maps exact statuses (401, 404, 500, etc.) to their kind, with fallbacks to `'clientError'` / `'serverError'` / `'requestError'`. Default message mirrors PHP: `` `${statusText} (${status}) Response: ${bodyExcerpt}` `` with body truncated to 2000 chars.

- **Response reading surface** (`src/contracts/Response.ts`, `src/http/response.ts`):
  - `json<T>(): Result<T, SyntaxError>` — whole-body parse as `Result` (malformed JSON → `err`, never throws)
  - `json<T>(key: string, defaultValue?: T): T` — dot-path getter (forgiving; missing key or malformed body → `defaultValue`)
  - `object<T>(): Result<T, SyntaxError>` — alias of whole-body `json()` (SaloonPHP parity)
  - `header(name: string): string | undefined` — single header, case-insensitive
  - Status predicates: `ok()`, `successful()`, `redirect()`, `clientError()`, `serverError()`, `failed()`
  - `onError(cb: (response) => void): Response` — calls callback when failed, returns `this` for chaining
  - `toResult(): Result<Response, RequestError>` — the headline: obtain failure as a value, never throwing

- **Predicate helpers** (`src/errors/predicates.ts`): Extended with `isRequestError`, `isClientError`, `isServerError`, and per-status predicates (`isNotFoundError`, `isUnauthorizedError`, `isForbiddenError`, `isMethodNotAllowedError`, `isRequestTimeoutError`, `isUnprocessableEntityError`, `isTooManyRequestsError`, `isInternalServerError`, `isServiceUnavailableError`, `isGatewayTimeoutError`). All discriminate via the `kind` field (O(1), no subclass per status).

- **Return-based JSON parsing**: `json()` and `object()` return `Result<T, SyntaxError>` so malformed JSON is a value, not a throw. Upholds the core invariant: **the only error the core throws is the network `FatalRequestError`**.

- **Tests**: Comprehensive coverage in `tests/errors/requestError.test.ts`, `tests/errors/predicates.test.ts`, and `tests/http/response.test.ts` (live server). Includes status mapping, message formatting, body truncation, predicate narrowing, and the full reading surface.

- **Exports**: Updated `src/index.ts` and `src/errors/index.ts` to expose `RequestError`, `createRequestError`, `RequestErrorKind`, and all predicate helpers.

- **Test utilities**: Added `tests/support/expectOk.ts` helper to keep body-reading tests terse (asserts `Result` is `Ok` and returns value).

## Implementation Notes

- The plan document was reworked to reflect the return-based design (PR #4 direction): the old throw-based status-class hierarchy is dropped in favor of a single `RequestError` with a `kind` discriminant.
- JSON parsing is lazy and cached as a `Result` to avoid re-parsing on multiple reads.
- The dot-path `json(key, default?)

body:
Chapter 11 (HI & Galactic Rotation) was the last research chapter running purely on synthetic data. It now applies the **same tangent-point method** to a **real** Galactic HI spectrum — validating the synthetic exercise against real bytes.

## What's here
- **`jansky.data`** — registers `lab-hi-l12`: a small (**366 KB**) real $(b, v)$ slice of the Leiden/Argentine/Bonn all-sky HI survey ([Kalberla et al. 2005](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361:20041864)) at Galactic longitude $l = 12°$, served from the VizieR Harvard mirror; calibrated brightness temperature in K.
- **`notebooks/11`** — new "A real HI spectrum: the LAB survey at l=12°" section (additive, +3 cells): reads the $b=0$ sightline, finds the **terminal velocity** ($+154$ km/s), and feeds it through $R = R_0\sin l$, $v_\mathrm{rot} = v_\mathrm{term} + V_0\sin l$ for a real rotation-curve point — **$v_\mathrm{rot} \approx 199$ km/s at $R \approx 1.7$ kpc**. Guarded with an offline fallback tuned to the same terminal velocity so it runs (and lands the same point) offline.
- **`references.md`** — adds the LAB-survey paper.

## Verified
- Real run: source `LAB survey (real)`, peak $T_B = 134$ K, terminal $v = +154$ km/s → $R = 1.70$ kpc, $v_\mathrm{rot} = 199$ km/s. Offline fallback → $v_\mathrm{rot} = 200$ km/s.
- New dataset URL + Kalberla DOI verified **200**. `ruff` + `mypy` clean; **167** tests pass; `nbmake` green online **and** offline; `mkdocs --strict` + doc-link test green. Additive: every original Ch 11 cell source preserved.

author: am-zest
body:
## Summary

First of two PRs for full session persistence (`TODO.md`). This is the **native foundation + Layer 1**: restore each pane's running command across restarts, with zero external dependencies. A follow-up PR adds the **zmx** layer for true live-process reattach.

Opt-in via a new **Settings → Session Persistence** toggle (**default off**), so existing behavior is unchanged.

## What it does

- When enabled, the workspace snapshot records each pane's **live foreground command** (full argv) and **non-default shell** at save time - the same capture the layout-file system already uses (`ProcessInspector.runningCommand` / `runningShell`). An idle prompt records no command.
- On relaunch, panes restore with those values and the command **re-launches** (via the existing `initial_input` path), alongside the already-restored splits and cwd.
- Adds a **stable per-pane `sessionID`** to `Pane` and the snapshot. It's unused at runtime today, but it's the foundation for the next PR: it survives restarts (unlike `Pane.id`) and will be the zmx session name for live reattach.

## Limitation (by design, addressed in PR2)

The command is **re-run fresh** - live process state, in-memory buffers, and scrollback are **not** preserved (a re-launched `nvim`/`claude` starts over). Keeping a process actually alive across a quit requires a daemon that owns it; that's the upcoming zmx layer. Nothing survives a reboot either way (no macOS process checkpoint/restore).

## Changes

- `Model/SplitNode.swift` - `Pane.sessionID` (stable, persisted), threaded through `init`.
- `Persistence/WorkspacePersistence.swift` - `PaneSnapshot` gains optional `sessionID`/`command`/`shell`; `snapshotNode` captures them (gated on the preference); `restoreNode` rebuilds panes with them.
- `App/Preferences.swift` - `sessionPersistenceEnabled` (default false).
- `Settings/SettingsView.swift` - the toggle + an honest description.
- `MactermTests/Persistence/WorkspaceSerializerTests.swift` - restore carries the fields; fresh `sessionID` when absent; legacy-JSON decode (back-compat); Codable round-trip.

## Compatibility

Old snapshots decode fine (the new fields are optional / absent keys → nil; a fresh `sessionID` is generated on restore). No schema-version bump needed.

body:
### Motivation
- The release packaging scripts default to copying binaries from `.vida/cargo-target/release` while the fresh `cargo build --release` invocation did not force Cargo to write into that directory, which allows stale or attacker-planted binaries to be packaged instead of freshly built outputs.
- The change ensures the build and packaging paths use the same resolved Cargo target root to restore release provenance and reduce supply-chain risk.

### Description
- Updated `scripts/build-release.sh` to call Cargo with `--target-dir "$CARGO_TARGET_ROOT"` so the fresh build writes into the same target root packaging reads from. 
- Updated `scripts/build-release.ps1` to call Cargo with `--target-dir $cargoTargetRoot` to mirror the PowerShell packaging path.
- Committed the scoped fix on the current branch (`fix: align release build target directory`) and prepared a PR containing only these two script edits.

### Testing
- `bash -n scripts/build-release.sh` was run and succeeded with no syntax errors. 
- Static check (`rg`) confirmed the release build invocations now include `--target-dir` in both scripts. 
- Dynamic focused proof using a `fake-cargo` wrapper (`CARGO="$TMP/fake-cargo" env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR -u VIDA_RELEASE_BIN_DIR bash scripts/build-release.sh v0.9.7`) verified Cargo was invoked with `--target-dir /workspace/vida-stack/.vida/cargo-target` and the packaged binaries were produced from that fresh target directory (archive created). 
- PowerShell parse check was attempted but skipped because `pwsh` is unavailable in this environment. 
- Attempt to create the TaskFlow TODO via `cargo run -p vida -- task create ...` was blocked by the local Rust toolchain/MSRV mismatch and `vida` not being available on `PATH`, so TaskFlow automation could not be exercised here.

## 概要
lore の主要エンティティに**一意の識別子（ID）**を導入し、各テンプレートに `id` プロパティを追加しました。

## ID 体系
`PREFIX-NNN`（3桁連番・一意・不変・欠番は再利用しない）
| 種別 | プレフィックス | ゲーム側の対応（参考） |
|---|---|---|
| 人物 | **PER** | `AdmiralData` / `Person.id` |
| 勢力 | **FAC** | `FactionData` |
| 会戦 | **BAT** | `ScenarioData` |
| 星系 | **SYS** | `StarSystem.id` |
| 旗艦 | **SHP** | `ShipNameRegistry` / `signatureShipName` |

## 変更点
- **テンプレートに `id` 追加**：人物・勢力・会戦・星系。
- **旗艦フォルダ新設**：`旗艦/_テンプレート.md`（SHP-NNN）＋実例 `旗艦/グリニッジ.md`（SHP-001・ミレイアの専用旗艦）。
- **既存ノートに採番**：ミレイア=PER-001／碧晶公国=FAC-001／自由港同位体=FAC-002／黎明評議会=FAC-003／鉄環兵団=FAC-004／灯心自由市ファロス=FAC-005。
- **`ID一覧.md`（採番台帳）新設**：プレフィックス規約・既発番・次番カウンタを一元管理（重複防止）。
- **README**：フォルダ構成（旗艦/・ID一覧.md）・ID規約・ゲームデータ対応表（星系/旗艦行）を追記。総覧ハブから ID一覧 へリンク。

## 補足
- lore 内の安定識別子であり、ゲームの手続き生成による数値ID（`StarSystem.id`/`Person.id`）とは別物。突き合わせは名前/IDで行い二重管理しない、と明記。
- ドキュメントのみの変更でコード・テストは非変更。

author: birthright50
body:
Missing skill attributes were added based on combined analysis of PTS 5.8 and 4.6 `skill_base.xml` and `skill_charge.xml`.

For intermediate calculation and validation purposes, a CSV dataset was created to consolidate and structure the comparison between PTS versions.
[skill_flags.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29180292/skill_flags.csv)

1) `apply_magical_critical` - same as the previous `applymcrit`, defaults to `false` when absent.

The flag decides **who may roll** the magical critical, not who may crit. The critical is rolled once per cast and target, and the following effect positions share the result.

| effect type | flag | behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| the six instant magical types (`SpellATK_Instant`, `SpellATKDrain_Instant`, `DelayedSpellATK_Instant`, `SignetBurst_Instant`, `ProcATK_Instant`) | read | **set**: reuses the critical of an earlier position, or rolls one and stores it for the later ones. **unset**: skipped entirely — no roll, no damage multiplier, and an already stored critical is ignored |
| periodic `SpellATK` / `SpellATKDrain` / `Poison` / `Bleed` | ignored | always reuses or rolls |
| `NoReduceSpellATK_Instant` | ignored | displays a critical that was already rolled, but never multiplies its own damage |
| `DispelBuffCounterATK` | ignored | never crits and never decides the critical of other positions |

With `E1 = SpellATK_Instant`, `E2 = SpellATK` (dot): flag unset - E1 cannot crit and E2 rolls its own; flag set - E1 rolls and E2 is locked to E1's result. Both verified on retail with `EL_ManaReverse_G6` (3555), whose launched dot crits although the flag is unset.

Details that follow from the shared roll:

* only the boolean is shared, each position applies its own `critadddmg`
* the result is stored before the resist check, so a resisted position still decides for the later ones
* a position dropped by its `conditions`/`preeffect` breaks the chain and the next one rolls again
* a dot crits on all of its ticks or on none.

#### `critprobmod` had to be completed for this

The flag only decides whether to roll - the chance itself comes from `critprobmod`, which was incomplete:

* **added `critprobmod1`.** The modifier is `critprobmod2 + critprobmod1 * skillLvl`.
* **fixed `critprobmod2` on 483 effects.** A missing `critical_prob_mod2` had been imported as 0, which means "never crits". The default is 100. 376 effects get their criticals back (112 `SpellATK_Instant`, 93 `NoReduceSpellATK_Instant`, 49 `SignetBurst`, 27 `SkillATK_Instant`, 22 `DelayedSpellATK_Instant`, 21 `FPATK_Instant`, 15 `Bleed`, …), the remaining 107 are explicit zeros that were missing.

That default is version dependent, and both were checked on retail: on 4.6 an effect without `critical_prob_mod2` never crits, on 5.8 it does. We follow the newer behaviour because 4.8 is the skill rework https://aionpowerbook.com/powerbook/New_World_Update_-_Skill_Changes, and our skill data lines up with 5.8 rather than 4.6.

2) `apply_casting_time_bonus `- removed the redundant hardcoded checks for effect type, avatar etc., since casting is governed solely by this flag. Also removed the check that cast speed bonuses only apply to magical skills - cast speed affects physical skills as well, for example https://aioncodex.com/48/skill/819/

For chargeable skills the bonus type comes from `charge_time_bonus_type` in `skill_charge.xml` instead of the caster's class (that check is gone):

   - `PHYSICAL` - attack speed always applies, this flag plays no role
   - `MAGICAL`- cast speed applies, but only when this flag is set
   - absent - the charge time is fixed.

      Charge skills only receive **half** of the speed bonus, so their caps are half of the normal ones: -37.5% for `MAGICAL` (half of the 75% casting time cap) and -25% / +50% for `PHYSICAL` (half of the 50% / 100% attack speed cap).

   `StatCapUtil` limited the attack speed bonus symmetrically to half the base value, giving a range of `[base * 0.5, base * 1.5]`. The attack delay is now clamped to `[500, 10000]` first and to `[base * 0.5, base * 2]` afterwards. The fast side is unchanged, slow effects can now double the attack delay instead of increasing it by half. This is also what gives `PHYSICAL` charge skills their +50% upper bound.

3) `apply_heal_boost_bonus` - All possible heal skills were tested for how they are affected by the `apply_heal_boost_bonus `flag. The `DISEASE `abnormal effect applies to all of them.

   `CaseHeal`: deboost does not affect it, healboost does not affect it. The flag plays no role. No changes were made within this PR.

   `Heal_Instant` (percent=false, with flag true): deboost affects, healboost affects.
   `Heal_Instant` (percent=false, without boost flag): deboost affects, healboost does not affect.
   `Heal_Instant` (percent=true, without boost flag): deboost affects, healboost does not affect.
   `Heal_Instant` (percent=true, with flag true): deboost affects, healboost affects.

   `ProcHeal_instant` (percent=false, with flag true): deboost affects, healboost affects.
   `ProcHeal_instant` (percent=false, without boost flag): deboost affects, healboost does not affect.
   `ProcHeal_instant` (percent=true, without boost flag): deboost affects, healboost does not affect.
   `ProcHeal_instant` (percent=true, with flag true): deboost affects, healboost affects.

   `Heal` (percent=false, with flag true): deboost affects, healboost affects.
   `Heal` (percent=false, without boost flag): deboost does not affect, healboost does not affect.
   `Heal` (percent=true, without boost flag): deboost does not affect, healboost does not affect.
   `Heal` (percent=true, with flag true): deboost affects, healboost affects.

   For the `Heal` effect, the base heal amount is calculated at the moment the skill is applied (based on the caster's    healboost), while the actual healing amount changes dynamically depending on the deboost effect.
   Also, the `<= 0` check for periodic healing was removed, since the retail allows it.
   
4) `apply_magical_skill_boost_bonus` - logic using this flag has also been implemented, hardcoded instanceof checks have been removed from magic damage calculations (e.g., for `NoReduceSpellATKInstant`).

author: lupus
body:
## What Distills the spec-anchored **LLM-driven exploratory testing** ("dogfooding") method I ran by hand across this session into a reusable, **git-versioned, in-project skill** so future runs are repeatable and high-signal. Subagent-driven: the orchestrator stays lean and delegates the two strong (Opus) judgement phases. ### Two Opus agents (the core) - **`journey-compiler`** (`.claude/agents/journey-compiler.md`) — Phase 1. Reads the *privileged* anchors (spec/PR/review) and emits spec-covering user journeys + a **fair-test context pack** (README + `--help` only). It launders privileged knowledge out of everything the swarm sees and **predicts discoverability findings** — if a feature isn't usable from the user-visible surface, that's a finding, not a reason to help the swarm. - **`trajectory-skeptic`** (`.claude/agents/trajectory-skeptic.md`) — Phase 3. **Bidirectional** adversarial triage: refutes failing candidates (real | intended | self-inflicted | discoverability) **and audits passing trajectories** for cheating / unverified success / premature-done, using the deterministic reconcile snapshot as independent ground truth (a green is a claim, not a result). ### The skill + scripts - `.claude/skills/llm-dogfooding/SKILL.md` — the 3-phase loop, the **fair-test boundary** (three-way information asymmetry), bidirectional skepticism, and the find→improve→re-find cadence. - `references/methodology.md` — oracle catalog ("LLM proposes, harness disposes"), the candidate + cheating taxonomies, signal/noise maturation, and field gotchas (short socket paths/SUN_LEN, mandatory caps, dispatch discipline, harness-code-in-the-product-repo). - `scripts/` — `gather-context-pack.sh` (assemble the fair-test surface, portable awk), `dispatch-swarm.sh` (validate journeys → push `dogfood-run/*` off main, no PR → trigger `dogfood.yml` → download bundles), `collect-trajectories.py` (flatten negatives **and** positives for the skeptic). **Phase 2 reuses the existing `hack/dogfood/` runner + `dogfood.yml`** — not duplicated. The skill is the orchestration + methodology + the two agents. ## Why these specific shapes Grounded in the real failure modes from this session's runs: slop from unanchored expects, the swarm unable to discover `volume attach` from `--help`, never auditing "green" trajectories for cheating, oracle false-positives on rejection journeys, AF_UNIX `SUN_LEN` blowups, and runaway loops without caps. The **fair-test boundary** and **bidirectional skepticism** are the two ideas that most improve signal over a naive setup. ## Notes - Built via the `superpowers:writing-skills` meta-skill (structure, triggers-only description, references for depth, one canonical example, portable scripts). - Files are force-added past the repo-local `.git/info/exclude` `.claude/` rule (personal `.claude/*` stays locally excluded; these project files are now tracked for everyone). - Validation posture: this is a technique/process skill whose RED baseline was the live session, not synthetic pressure runs — the natural end-to-end validation is the next real feature run, which the skill itself drives. Scripts are syntax-checked + smoke-tested. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR distills the spec-anchored LLM dogfooding method into a reusable, git-versioned skill: two Opus subagents (`journey-compiler` and `trajectory-skeptic`) bookending a CI swarm (Phase 2 reuses `hack/dogfood/`), plus three supporting scripts and a methodology reference. - **`journey-compiler` / `trajectory-skeptic`** — new agent definitions with clear three-way information-boundary rules; the compiler launders privileged knowledge out of swarm inputs, and the skeptic audits both failing *and* passing trajectories bidirectionally. - **`dispatch-swarm.sh`** — Phase 2 glue that validates `journeys.json`, pushes a throwaway branch, triggers `dogfood.yml`, polls for the run ID, and downloads trajectory bundles; contains a real poll-exit bug when the workflow hasn't registered yet (see inline comment). - **`collect-trajectories.py` / `gather-context-pack.sh`** — helpers to flatten bundles for the skeptic and assemble the fair-test context pack from `--help` + README recursively.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 Safe to merge — the bug in dispatch-swarm.sh only manifests when the GitHub Actions workflow hasn't registered yet, causing the script to proceed with a literal "null" run ID rather than retrying the full poll window. The dispatch script's run-ID poll loop exits immediately when jq returns the JSON null literal as the string "null" — that string is non-empty, so the guard `[ -n "$RID" ]` passes and the loop breaks on the very first iteration. Every subsequent command then fails with opaque errors instead of waiting the intended 40-second window. dispatch-swarm.sh — the run-ID poll loop needs an additional `[ "$RID" != "null" ]` guard alongside the existing `[ -n "$RID" ]` check.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | .claude/agents/journey-compiler.md | New Opus agent definition for Phase 1; well-specified mandates, launder rules, and validation steps — no logic issues. | | .claude/agents/trajectory-skeptic.md | New Opus agent for Phase 3 bidirectional triage; Direction A/B classification is clear and well-grounded — no issues. | | .claude/skills/llm-dogfooding/SKILL.md | Skill entry-point with three-phase loop, fair-test boundary table, common-mistakes section, and quick-reference — purely documentation, no defects. | | .claude/skills/llm-dogfooding/references/methodology.md | Depth reference covering oracle catalog, candidate/cheating taxonomies, cost/scale guidance, and field gotchas — documentation only, no code defects. | | .claude/skills/llm-dogfooding/scripts/collect-trajectories.py | Trajectory-flattening script; return-type annotation on load_bundles is wrong (list[tuple] not list[dict]) and both open() calls lack context managers — mypy will error and a mid-dump exception leaves a truncated output file. | | .claude/skills/llm-dogfooding/scripts/dispatch-swarm.sh | Phase 2 swarm-dispatch glue; has a real bug where a not-yet-registered workflow returns JSON null, which becomes the string "null" and prematurely exits the poll loop — all downstream gh commands then fail with opaque errors. | | .claude/skills/llm-dogfooding/scripts/gather-context-pack.sh | Fair-test context-pack assembler; portable awk subcommand parser, bounded recursion, correct || true guards — no significant defects. |

Comments Outside Diff (4)

 1. `.claude/skills/llm-dogfooding/scripts/dispatch-swarm.sh`, line 728-734 ([link](https://github.com/lupus/izba/blob/a9899190843a50650441550e3e46f554f4077fcb/.claude/skills/llm-dogfooding/scripts/dispatch-swarm.sh#L728-L734)) **Early exit with `RID=null` when workflow hasn't registered yet** When `gh run list` returns an empty array (workflow not yet registered), `.[0].databaseId` evaluates to the JSON `null` literal, which `gh --jq` emits as the string `"null"`. That string passes `[ -n "$RID" ]`, so the loop exits immediately with `RID=null`. Every subsequent command — `gh run view null`, `gh run watch null`, `gh run download null` — then fails with a confusing error rather than waiting the full 40-second window. The guard needs to also reject the literal string `"null"`: `[ -n "$RID" ] && [ "$RID" != "null" ] && break`

body:
**- What I did**

Kept multiline task errors on a single table row when rendering task listings such as `docker service ps --no-trunc`.

Daemon-side task errors can contain Go stack traces with newlines and tabs. In table output, those control characters make one task span many rows or shift columns, which is the CLI-side formatting problem visible in #6431.

Addresses #6431.

**- How I did it**

Normalized CRLF, LF, CR, and tab characters to spaces when formatting the task `Error` field for table output.

The change is scoped to table rendering only. Custom non-table formats such as `--format '{{.Error}}'` continue to preserve the original multiline error text.

**- How to verify it**

Ran:

```console
scripts/with-go-mod.sh go test ./cli/command/task -run 'TestTaskContextError(PreservesNewlinesForCustomFormat|ReplacesNewlines)' -count=1
scripts/with-go-mod.sh go test ./cli/command/task ./cli/command/service ./cli/command/node ./cli/command/stack -count=1
scripts/with-go-mod.sh go test ./cmd/docker -run '^$' -count=1
git diff --check
```

Second-agent review:

```text
Reviewer: hermes chat -Q
Result: CLEAN after fixing the first review's blocking tab-normalization finding.
Note: claude -p was attempted first but failed authentication with HTTP 401, so the required fallback reviewer was used.
```

**- A picture of a cute animal (not mandatory but encouraged)**

body:
Closes the gaps left behind by the archived centralized-logging change (#T000964).

## What

### Application logging (closes AC 1)
Migrate the 7 API routes that still used `console.error/warn/info` to use
`locals.requestLogger` so every line carries `requestId`, `method`, `path`
and is captured as structured JSON by Promtail:

- `website/src/pages/api/admin/agent-push/settings.ts` — 2 errors (GET/POST) + also now returns `errorResponse` instead of leaking `err.message` in the body
- `website/src/pages/api/admin/projekte/create.ts` — 2 warns (folder materialization)
- `website/src/pages/api/meeting/save-transcript.ts` — 1 warn + 2 infos
- `website/src/pages/api/admin/coaching/books/index.ts` — 1 warn
- `website/src/pages/api/admin/platform/hardware.ts` — 1 warn
- `website/src/pages/api/admin/platform/software.ts` — 1 warn
- `website/src/pages/api/admin/billing/[id]/send.ts` — 1 warn

After this change `grep -RE 'console\.(error|log|warn|info)' website/src/pages/api` returns nothing.

### Spec SSOT (closes the TODO stub)
The merged spec `openspec/specs/centralized-logging.md` was a TODO stub.
Rewrote it with 9 proper Requirements + 20 Scenarios that describe the
system that actually runs today:
- Pino logger singleton + `createRequestLogger`
- X-Request-ID middleware (incoming header reuse, 12-char nanoid fallback, request.start/end at the right level)
- Standardized `errorResponse(code, requestId, status)` contract
- API surface free of `console.*`
- `PINO_LOG_LEVEL` env-driven
- Traefik JSON access logs
- Promtail JSON pipeline + level label + debug drop
- Keycloak JSON console logging
- 4 Grafana dashboards (log-explorer, api-errors, traefik-access, keycloak-audit)

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run src/lib/logger.test.ts src/middleware/logging.test.ts src/pages/api/_error-contract.test.ts` → 7/7 pass
- `task workspace:validate` → green
- `task freshness:regenerate` → no diff (all artifacts already current)
- `task freshness:check` → green (98→98 baseline, no new S1/S2 violations)
- `task test:code-quality` → 0 fails, 0 errors
- 7 route files all well under 500-line S1 limit (largest: send.ts 243)

## Out of scope / known pre-existing flake

- `src/lib/assistant/actions/portal/shareFile.test.ts` has 5–7 timeouts in the
  full vitest run, both on this branch AND on `main` (reproduced on
  `main` before any changes). The test passes in isolation
  (`pnpm vitest run src/lib/assistant/actions/portal/shareFile.test.ts` → 8/8 in 359ms).
  This is a pre-existing concurrency flake, not introduced by this PR. Will be
  tracked as a separate ticket.

author: juliusolsson05
body:
## Why #320 didn't work

#320 added body truncation to `SubAgentWatcher`, but a fresh `--owners` snapshot showed `SubAgentWatcher` **still retaining ~278MB / 89%** of the main-process heap — unchanged. Investigation (dominator tree + path-to-root + standalone proofs) found **two real bugs**, both missed by the agents and the prior review:

### Bug 1 — `clampString` used `.slice()`, which frees nothing
`value.slice(0, cap)` returns a V8 **SlicedString that retains the entire parent string**. So every "truncated" body kept its full original alive behind the slice — truncation freed *zero* memory. The heap even showed 56MB of Read blobs as `sliced string`.

**Proof:**
```
clamp 2000×200KB via slice   → 194 MB pinned
clamp 2000×200KB via flat-copy → 19 MB
```
**Fix:** round-trip the prefix through a `Buffer` (utf16le, byte-exact) so the result is a fresh flat string and the parent becomes GC-eligible.

### Bug 2 — the bulk lives in `toolUseResult`, which we never truncated
Claude writes the **full** Read/tool output to the **top-level `entry.toolUseResult`** field (`toolUseResult.file.content`, `stdout`/`stderr`) — *in addition* to the `message.content` tool_result block. `truncateEntryBodies` only walked `message.content`/`attachment`/`content`, so the actual megabytes (held by `Object.content` under `toolUseResult.file`) sailed through untouched. That's why only **5** truncation markers existed for ~1,952 un-truncated Read blobs.

**Fix:** replace the hand-maintained field-by-field walk with a single recursive `clampDeep(entry, cap, 12)` over the **whole entry** — catches `toolUseResult`, `message.content` (string OR array), `tool_use.input`, attachments, and any future shape. No more whack-a-mole.

**Proof:** on a realistic entry, `toolUseResult.file.content` clamped 270,000 → 8,238 chars with `type`/`tool_use_id`/`filePath` all intact.

## Safety / invisibility
`clampString` is a no-op for strings under the 8KB cap, so structural fields (type/uuid/role/name/id/tool_use_id/timestamps) are untouched, and `buildSubAgentState` only renders ≤80-char headlines — so clamping at 8KB can never change a rendered value. Durable full bodies stay on disk. Net **−57 lines** (simpler than #320's field list). Typechecks clean.

## Verify after merge + rebuild
```
node --max-old-space-size=12288 scripts/analyze-heapsnapshot.mjs <new-snap> --owners
```
`SubAgentWatcher` should fall from **~278MB → single-digit MB**.

author: iamacoffeepot
body:
The local attestation producer aborted on its qodana step when run from a linked worktree: `attest.sh` ran `qodana scan` in place, but the worktree's `.git` pointer references a gitdir the qodana analysis container can't reach, so qodana mis-scoped the diff and flagged the whole pre-existing backlog as new.

This is the producer counterpart to the preflight fix in #2123. When in a worktree, scan a throwaway self-contained clone of HEAD (real `.git`, full history) under a Docker-shared path; the main checkout still scans in place. The scan directory is passed through the environment, never as a command argument, so the command-run attestor records no machine-identifying path — the same PII discipline as the per-step log redirect. The verifier's `qodana scan` command-match is unaffected.

Surfaced while dogfooding the producer end-to-end from a worktree.

🎯 **What**
Fixed a bug in `DashStyleEditor.cs` where switching the spacing mode to `FixedCount` would incorrectly apply the spacing ratio calculated from the first selected object to *all* selected objects when performing multi-object editing.

💡 **Why**
The original code explicitly had a TODO marking this logic as "wonky" because it directly updated `propSpacing.floatValue`, which Unity Editor inherently applies uniformly to all selected instances. This caused unintended spacing values on shapes with different initial sizes.

✅ **Verification**
Ran editor test suite to ensure no regressions. Verified the fix by wrapping the value modification inside a loop over `targetObjects`, instantiating individual `SerializedObject` instances, and calling `ApplyModifiedProperties()`, ensuring that each object preserves its correct relative ratio based on its own specific `size` and `spacing`.

✨ **Result**
Multi-object editing for dash style spacing now correctly and individually scales spacing to period ratios without overriding distinct values across shapes.

## What

A **Table ⇄ Bubbles** toggle in the screener that renders the token universe as a live "crypto bubbles" field — floating, logo-filled, glass bubbles.

- **Colour** = 24h performance (green up / red down, brighter = bigger move), carried on a coloured glass rim + outer glow.
- **Size** = selectable metric: `24h %` / `6h %` / `1h %` / `Volume` / `Mkt Cap` / `Liquidity`, with a smooth animated tween + re-pack on switch.

- **One bubble per token** — the screener is pair-based, so a token had many pairs (WPLS ×15, WBTC ×13, …); the view dedupes by base token and over-fetches pages to reach the requested distinct-token count.
- **Count selector** 100 / 250 / 500 (default 250); the size floor + cap scale with count so the field packs full at every level.

author: usirin
body:
Closes #1040

## What

The vote/report **target kind** (`definition` | `post` | `comment`) — shared by the vote engine, the report engine, and two D1 columns — was independently re-declared 4+ times and stored as untyped `text`. This consolidates it into ONE typed source and closes the corrupt-PK channel.

`apps/web/worker/db/target-kind.ts` (new) exports:
- `TARGET_KINDS` — the one runtime tuple the D1 enums source from
- `TargetKind` — the type
- `TargetKindSchema` — the one `Schema.Literals`

### Why `db/` and not `vote/`
The triage AC suggested hoisting into the vote engine, but the `report/` feature-boundary pin (`report-boundary.unit.test.ts`) **forbids a `report/ → vote/` sibling edge**. The taxonomy is genuinely shared, so it lives in `db/` — below both features, the established neutral home both `vote/` and `report/` (and the schema) already import from. This is also the right semantic home: `target_kind` is a D1 column domain, sitting beside `schema.ts` exactly as `report/resolution.ts` anchors `status`/`resolution` (db ← feature there; here db owns it outright).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] One exported `TargetKind` + one `Schema.Literals` (`TargetKindSchema`). `VoteTargetKind` **and** `ReportTargetKind` deleted; both engines + every consumer import the shared type.
- [x] The two `text("target_kind")` columns switch to `text(…, {enum: [...TARGET_KINDS]})`, matching `user.role` / `content_report.status` — a typo can no longer write a corrupt PK.
- [x] No behavior change for valid kinds; adding a votable entity (e.g. `imge`) is now a one-site edit.

## Sites re-routed to the single source
- `vote/errors.ts` (`VoteTargetKind` type + inline `Schema.Literals`) → `TargetKindSchema`
- `report/errors.ts` (`ReportTargetKind` type + inline `Schema.Literals`) → `TargetKindSchema`
- `report/mutations.ts` — 3 inline `Schema.Literals` (submit/resolve/restore inputs) → `TargetKindSchema`
- `report/{Report,views,shapers}.ts` — `ReportTargetKind` type refs → shared `TargetKind`
- `vote/Vote.ts` — `VoteTargetKind` type refs (incl. `./Vote` re-export) → shared `TargetKind`
- `vote/Vote.unit.test.ts` — inline `["definition","post","comment"]` loop → iterates `TARGET_KINDS`
- `db/drizzle/schema.ts` — both `target_kind` columns + import of `TARGET_KINDS`

## Behavior-change status
**None for valid kinds.** drizzle's sqlite `text(…, {enum})` is a TypeScript-only narrowing — it emits **no** CHECK constraint (the `status`/`role` enums have none in any migration; 0007 documents the set in a `--` comment only). The annotation is **forward-only with no migration**; stored + wire values are unchanged.

## Verification
- `pnpm -w typecheck` — clean (all 24 tasks, incl. `preview-seed`/`fts-backfill` which also import the schema)
- `pnpm vitest run --project unit` — **446 passed** (incl. the `report-boundary` pin, now satisfied: `report/` imports no sibling feature)

## Scope
Did **not** touch the DefinitionCard vote test or `useVoteToggle` (#1044's lane). No control-plane files. Builds on the merged #1039 (myVote boolean) + #1042 (report resolution) types without undoing them.

author: joshskkim
body:
## Problem
The API image build failed with an opaque `process "/bin/sh -c SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=... mvn ... -q -DskipTests package" ... exit code: 1`. Root cause: the `sentry-source-context` Maven profile activates whenever `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is set (the CD image build), and its `uploadSourceBundle` goal **fails the whole `package`** when the upload errors. `-q` hid the real Sentry message.

Reproduced with a bogus token: `Invalid org token (http status: 401)` / `Unrecognized auth token format` → `BUILD FAILURE`. A symbolication source-upload should never block shipping the image.

## Fix (`api/Dockerfile`)
- Drop `-q` so the real Sentry error is visible in the build log.
- Best-effort upload: if `package` fails with the profile active, retry once with it explicitly off (`-P !sentry-source-context`), so a jar is always produced and the image always builds.

## Verification (buildx)
- **No token** → `package` succeeds on the first try, profile inactive, nothing uploaded.
- **Bogus token** → upload 401 surfaced in the log, fallback rebuilds without the profile, image ships (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

## Note
This makes the build resilient, but uploads still wont happen until the real `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` secret is a valid **org auth token** (`sntrys_…`) for org `joshua-kim-m4` — the 401 suggests the current secret is malformed or the wrong token type.

## Feature 006: pg_stat_io screen (flagship of 0.11.0)

New TUI screen for `pg_stat_io` (PostgreSQL 16+) in `pgcenter top` — unified IO breakdown by
`backend_type × object × context`, shown as per-interval rates.

### What's new
- **Two sub-screens** (no horizontal scroll in pgcenter, so split like `pg_stat_statements`):
  - `j` — count screen (operations + KiB throughput); repeat `j` toggles to timings.

author: jay-githubs
body:
## Problem

`owui-feedback-sync` (round-trip) polls for a thumbs-up that syncs into ThaiRAG's feedback log. But the feature is **off by default** (`THAIRAG__OWUI_FEEDBACK_SYNC__ENABLED=false`, intentionally — low value at current scale) and it's a **deploy-time env** the spec can't toggle. So nothing ever syncs → the poll times out → hard fail. (It previously failed even earlier on the embedding-404 ingest, now fixed.)

## Fix

Gate the round-trip on `RUN_FEEDBACK_SYNC=1` so it **skips by default**. The companion `owui-feedback-sync-disabled` spec already verifies the default (off) state and **passes**. Same approach as the Ollama/stress specs: don't fail a deployment for a feature it intentionally has off.

Verified: with the feature off, the round-trip skips and the disabled spec passes; with `RUN_FEEDBACK_SYNC=1` on a sync-enabled deploy it runs as before.

## Summary

Auto-generated slugs (`Case._generate_unique_slug`) look like `{court}-{title-fragment}-{md5}` and appear in public `jawafdehi.org/case/<slug>` URLs. This proposes human-readable replacements.

body:
Evaluating a submodel used to recurse through the shared `_evaluate!!(::Model, ::AbstractVarInfo)` method. Each submodel level constructs a contextualized `Model{..., Ctx}` whose `Ctx` parameter gains another context layer. In nested submodels, Julia's recursion limiter (`limit_type_size`) sees the same `_evaluate!!(::Model, ...)` method recurring with a more complex `Model{..., Ctx}` call signature, widens the `Model` argument to abstract `Model`, and inference can no longer resolve `model.f` precisely. The model return type then collapses to `Any`, evaluation falls back to runtime dispatch, and primal/gradient evaluation slows down.

Submodel evaluation now calls the generated model function directly instead of going through `_evaluate!!(::Model, ...)`. This removes the recursive `_evaluate!!(::Model, ...)` call edge while leaving the recursive `_evaluate!!(::Submodel, ...)` edge intact; the remaining submodel edge is not widened by the limiter. As a result, inference stays type stable for nested submodels.

Adds type-stability (`@inferred`) and allocation (`iszero(allocs)`) regression tests at both the evaluation and `LogDensityFunction` levels, covering several nesting depths under `UnlinkAll`/`LinkAll`. The tests were verified to fail on the unfixed code. Also bumps the version to 0.42.1 and adds a HISTORY.md entry.

See https://github.com/TuringLang/Turing.jl/issues/2844

Above is written by Claude/Codex, lightly touched by me.

## Summary

body:
## Problem

The typing animation restarted from the first descriptor on every page refresh.

## Fix

On mount, pick the starting descriptor from `Date.now()`:

```ts
setDescriptorIndex(
  Math.floor(Date.now() / DESCRIPTOR_DISPLAY_DURATION_MS) % descriptors.length,
);
```

Since the selection advances with the clock, a refresh resumes at a time-appropriate descriptor instead of restarting at the first one. The existing per-character typing/deleting state machine is **unchanged** — only the descriptor *selection* is time-based.

Seeding happens in an effect (client-only), so the initial render still matches the server (no hydration mismatch).

## Verification
- `npm run build` compiles and TypeScript passes.

### Motivation

- Preserve raw historical/chart/candle files while ensuring derived decision outputs are not trusted when generated by an older patch version.  
- Detect and remove stale generated outputs, force full recalculation where needed, and make replay coverage, calibration, and live-gate decisions depend on fresh expanded history.  
- Provide an audit of what was reused, removed, or regenerated and surface mixed-version warnings in the viewer so operators can safely decide about live trading.  

### Description

- Add post-patch constants and file categories including `NEXT_PATCH_GENERATION_VERSION`, expected replay coverage thresholds, `RAW_RUNTIME_FILES_TO_PRESERVE`, `DERIVED_RUNTIME_FILES_TO_REGENERATE_WHEN_STALE`, and `POST_PATCH_AUDIT_CSV_PATH`.  
- Implement sidecar metadata helpers `write_generated_file_meta`, `read_generated_file_meta`, and `generated_file_is_current`, plus `replay_history_needs_expansion`, `_csv_product_time_coverage`, `derived_outputs_are_stale`, and `remove_stale_derived_outputs_if_needed` to detect and clean stale derived outputs.  
- Wire cleanup into `TradingBot.__init__` so stale derived outputs are removed before seeding calibration, and add flags to force historical replay / startup recalculation when coverage is insufficient.  
- Make historical replay expansion append/merge (preserve existing rows, fetch gaps, dedupe, sort) and mark expanded/compacted replay caches with generation metadata.  
- Block seeding cached `calibration.csv` unless its metadata is current and validate rows with `calibration_row_is_live_safe`; require fresh replay coverage before regenerating calibration on startup.  
- Harden product live-gate checks so stale live-gate files block buys, require spread/liquidity checks (special stricter rule for `SHIB-USD`), and ensure product live-gate is regenerated after fresh calibration; mark regenerated files with sidecar metadata.  
- Add `write_post_patch_audit` to record previous-runtime import, stale cleanup, replay coverage, live-gate summary, and final readiness into `post_patch_audit.csv` and ensure it is written after calculation status is written.  
- Update viewer to compute and display mixed-version warnings, generation version, stale/current generated files, replay coverage days, approved products, and clear readiness blockers; render a top warning when derived outputs are stale or replay coverage is insufficient.  

### Testing

- Compiled both modules with `python3 -m py_compile bot.py viewer.py`, which completed successfully.  
- Ran `git diff --check` and it returned no check errors.

body:
Extends the revision diff (#30) from **visuals-only** to the **artifact body**, and covers **decisions** — the other big revisable artifact, which previously showed only the reason banner with no diff.

## What's diffed now

| Type | Body list | Matched by |
|---|---|---|
| **plan** | Steps | description (steps have no stable id) |
| **spec** | Requirements | `id` |
| **decision** | Options | `id` |

One generic `key + detail` list diff drives all three: same `key` across versions = matched; differing `detail` (the rest of the item) = **changed**; otherwise **added** / **removed**. It renders with the same `＋ / ~ / −` language as the file_map diff, and shows an honest **"no changes"** when a section is untouched — so *"only the diagram changed, the steps are the same"* reads at a glance.

So a revised plan now shows step changes **and** visual changes; a revised decision shows its options added/removed/changed.

Implements all 10 fixes (F1–F10) from the decision-engine evaluation
(`docs/decision-engine-evaluation.md`). Four themed commits, each with node tests.

## Headline results (exhaustive sweeps)
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Build-grid plans exceeding MRV (2,520 plans) | **869 (34.5%)** | **0** |
| Worst over-MRV (back) | **57.5 vs MRV 25** | **0 over** |
| "Band Pull-Apart" prescribed to band-less users | yes | **0** |

## What changed
**A · quick wins** — equipment-filter the activation primer (F2, swaps Band Pull-Apart → Scapular Wall Slide); trim the primer on ≤30-min sessions (F6); honest session titles, mixed sessions read "Full body" (F3); kill vestigial "aerobic engine" copy (F7); fix the stale cyclist dev preset (F10).

**C · peaking & specificity** — the event **taper now keeps intensity (RPE 8) and only cuts volume** instead of behaving like a deload (F4; Bosquet 2007, Travis & Mujika 2020); in-season deloads/tapers respect the season scalar. **Sport sessions lead with sport-specific work** — swimmer opens on a pull, sprinter on Power Clean/plyos — and sprint chest volume drops ~12 → 6 sets (F8).

**D · adaptive deloads** — deloads now track real fatigue: `deloadRecommendation()` **forces** a deload on sustained-high ACWR or low readiness + poor recovery, and **defers** a planned deload when fresh. Lives entirely in the runtime layer (`adaptedPhases`); the pure generator is untouched (F9).

## Verification
- `npm run dev` clean; verified live in the preview (primer swap, 20-min trimmed primer, swim leads on a pull, forced adaptive deload flips the current week with a reason).

## Summary

Adds an explicit acyclicity premise to the module wf rule, mirroring how module-level dependency acyclicity is already handled. Previously, cyclic inheritance was rejected only implicitly (via non-termination of `fields_M`), which made `fields_M` ill-defined and caused the checker to crash with `RecursionError`.

### Spec
- §2.2 (Class contexts) names the inheritance graph `G_{Λ_M}` with edge `(C, B)` iff `Λ_M(C) = (\vec{x}, B)`.
- Fig 6 (Module structure) module rule gains the premise `G_{Λ_M} acyclic`, alongside the existing imports-resolved and class-name-uniqueness premises.
- `fields_M` is now a well-defined least solution to its equations rather than relying on non-termination for ill-formedness.

### Implementation
- `src/reasons.py`: new `CyclicInheritance(cycle)` reason.
- `src/check_module.py`: `build_class_context` builds the inheritance graph and runs `has_cycle`; raises `IllFormedModule(node, CyclicInheritance(...))`. `has_cycle` moves here so `check_program` can share it.
- `src/check_program.py`: drops the local `has_cycle`, imports from `check_module`.

### Tests
- New `test/module-level/ill-formed/semantic/cyclic_inheritance.py` plus `.error.expected` (`cyclic inheritance`) and `.exception.expected` (`NameError` — Python rejects at runtime via the same shape).

author: presidentanderson
body:
Refs #476.

## What
Adds `docs/plans/issue-476.md` — a PLAN-mode deliverable (epic / human-gated, **security + compliance**, **no feature built**) for the mobile *Secure offline access — encrypted local cache* epic, which resolves the "deliberate exception" tension in **#74** (no browser-stored litigation data for signed-in users).

- Decomposes the six epic children ([A]/[H]) into ordered, gate-tagged sub-tasks, reusing the `issue-541.md` / `issue-478.md` gate taxonomy and adding the security gates this epic needs: **[H-LEGAL]** (Loi 25 / privilege / #74 exception), **[H-SEC]** (crypto boundary + key custody), **[H-EXT]** (native shell + biometric/secure-storage), **[H-RLS]** (tenant isolation).
- Names the two hard prerequisites that block everything: (1) the #74 exception is **unsigned** — per the epic's first child the security stance must be approved and recorded on #74 *before any caching code lands*; (2) there is **no native runtime** in the repo (no `capacitor.config.ts` / `ios/` / `android/`), so the Secure-Enclave/Keystore key, biometric prompt, and `secure-storage` plugin are all blocked on the Capacitor foundation tracked in `issue-541.md` (#471/#473/#476) — not duplicated here.
- Grounds the contract in real code paths: the #74 invariant already enforced in `lib/store/evidence-files.ts` `uploadEvidence()`, the localStorage-for-anonymous-only model in `lib/store/cases.ts`, the edition registry `lib/editions.ts`, and the legal-hold guard `supabase/migrations/0060_legal_hold_delete_guard.sql`.
- Specifies **one safe first slice**: a pure, web-testable `lib/mobile/offline-cache-policy.ts` core + invariant tests with **zero** persistence, crypto, or native dependency — it makes the #74 invariant executable as tests and writes no cache, so it advances the epic without spending a human gate.

## Why
An encrypted on-device cache is a deliberate carve-out from a founder-level invariant (#74: "NO litigation data may live in the browser" for signed-in users, aligned with Loi 25 + solicitor-client privilege). That exception cannot be granted by an agent edit, and the encryption itself needs a native runtime that does not exist yet. This doc makes the hold-line legible, sequences the work behind its real legal and native prerequisites, and gives the safe pure-logic slice a typed contract the gated native layer must obey.

## Notes
- Markdown only — no code, migrations, RLS, `lib/version.ts`, gate flags, or attestations touched. No `.ts` files changed, so no new type errors. Next free migration number documented as `0067` for any future slice (none needed for slice 0).
- The `[A]` code slices target the `juge.ca` litigation-OS repo where #476 lives; this PR carries the plan deliverable.

## Summary

Adds wrappers for the official Alpha Vantage gold/silver endpoints in `Commodities`, aligned with the existing commodity method style (`get_wti()`, `get_copper()`, etc.):

Historical series:

- `get_gold(interval="monthly", symbol="GOLD")` -> `GOLD_SILVER_HISTORY`
- `get_silver(interval="monthly", symbol="SILVER")` -> `GOLD_SILVER_HISTORY`

Realtime spot prices:

- `get_gold_spot(symbol="GOLD")` -> `GOLD_SILVER_SPOT`
- `get_silver_spot(symbol="SILVER")` -> `GOLD_SILVER_SPOT`

The official docs accept:

- Gold: `GOLD` / `XAU`
- Silver: `SILVER` / `XAG`

Historical intervals are documented as:

- `daily`
- `weekly`
- `monthly`

This PR overlaps with #387 on the historical endpoint (`GOLD_SILVER_HISTORY`). I updated this PR to follow the same package-style API direction as #387 (`get_gold()` / `get_silver()`), while also adding:

- realtime spot endpoint support (`get_gold_spot()` / `get_silver_spot()`)

The official API supports these endpoints, but they were not exposed through the Python wrapper. Using `ForeignExchange` / `FX_DAILY` is not a substitute for XAG/USD or XAU/USD, because gold/silver are handled by the dedicated `GOLD_SILVER_*` endpoints.

body:
Adds a new guide page at `site/content/docs/guides/bun-to-nub.mdx` covering migration from the Bun runtime to Node + nub.

Per the request, the page is **created but not added to the sidebar nav** (no `meta.json` changes) until the maintainer wants it listed.

Content is grounded in real nub behavior verified against the codebase:

- Runtime / TS execution (`nub <file>`, the file-runner vs `nub run` distinction, `--node` escape hatch).
- Node version selection (nub runs your Node; tier banding; pin a realistic floor).
- Package manager + lockfile (pnpm-grammar CLI, multi-PM lockfile compat, peer-deps NOT auto-installed).
- Scripts: `/regex/` selection (the native multi-script form, concurrent by default / `--sequential`), `run a b` is NOT multi-script, `npm-run-all2` for explicit run-p/run-s lists.

- `Bun.$` → tinyexec; `Bun.sql` → postgres.js / pg (Prisma-aware); `Bun.file`/`Bun.spawn`/`Bun.YAML`/`import.meta` replacements.
- Dependabot (`npm` ecosystem + a `nub install` lockfile-regen step).

body:
Fixes from the first real test run on macOS 26.5 (thanks for the diagnostic output).

### What was wrong
- **Menu bar never appeared.** `menubar.py` crashed on import with `objc.BadPrototypeError` — my pure-Python helper methods (`_add`/`_rebuild`) on the `NSObject` subclass were being interpreted as Objective-C selectors with the wrong arity, so the LaunchAgent just crash-looped (`launchctl` showed last-exit = 1).
- **Nothing pinned to Finder Favourites.** `mysides` wasn't installed, so setup fell back to the manual-drag path.

### Fixes
- **`menubar.py`** — helpers are now `add_item`/`rebuild` marked `@objc.python_method` (hidden from the Obj-C runtime); menu actions are passed as `bytes` selectors; the custom-icon `Icon\r` file is filtered out of the dropdown; paths are `str()`-coerced before `open`.
- **`install.command`** — puts Homebrew on `PATH` (a double-clicked `.command` often doesn't have `/opt/homebrew/bin`), then **auto-installs `mysides` via brew** so the sidebar actually gets pinned. Finishes by printing the **`doctor`** report instead of vague "look for it" text.
- **`working-folders.sh`** — filters the `Icon\r` custom-icon file out of `list`/`count`/`remove`; **relaunches Finder after pinning** so the sidebar refreshes immediately; adds a **`doctor`** command (and menu entry **d**) that reports macOS version, shelf, icon, app, menu-bar agent status, PyObjC, mysides and the pin state — so future debugging is one command.

### Validated here
`bash -n` on all scripts, `menubar.py` byte-compiles, the embedded icon-render Python compiles, and the `Icon\r` filter + `doctor` were exercised with stubs. The PyObjC menu-bar runtime itself still needs your Mac to confirm — but the specific crash above is fixed.

Re-run `install.command` after merge; it's idempotent and will reload the (now non-crashing) menu bar agent and install mysides.

## What

Restructures the seeded org so every department has a **Leadership** team — the department manager plus that department's team managers (and a little staff). Managers report there, so each team's score now reflects its individual contributors only, and no rollup unit is exposed by a lone manager's own response. The CIO abstains, so the company root has no recoverable lone response.

Also tunes response rates back to ~70–80% and updates the README's seeded edge-cases section to match.

## Why

Closes the differencing gap where a department/company rollup minus its visible teams could recover a lone manager's individual response (and over-suppressed in some cases). Modeling managers as a Leadership cohort removes that leak cleanly and gives departments a fuller team comparison.

## Details

- New `*_leadership` org units (Engineering / Revenue / Customer Operations) — manager-less peer groups; managers moved into them.
- ~6 supporting people added so leadership cohorts reach ~5 and a couple of teams keep a ~70% rate.
- `RESPONSE_TARGETS` retuned for IC-only teams; leadership cohorts get their own score profile.

## Privacy showcases preserved

- AI Lab / SMB Sales / CX Research Pod still hidden (<4).
- Revenue: Enterprise Sales suppressed to protect SMB Sales.
- Customer Operations: the smallest visible sibling (the Leadership team) is suppressed to protect the CX Research Pod; Core Support and Customer Success stay visible.

## Notes for reviewer

- Branched from the current `main` (which removed `.claude`); no `.claude` re-added.
- Verified: every department + the CIO view renders, charts draw, response rates land ~72–74%, and the suppression structure is unchanged by the rate tweak.

author: kninetimmy
body:
First **M5 (environmental layers)** slice. Polls a USGS earthquake **GeoJSON feed** and projects each quake onto the map as a schema-v2 `GeoFeatureRecord(earthquake)` — opening the milestone with the simplest source (public-domain, no key, polling).

### What's here
- **`adapters/usgs.py`** — pure `Feature → GeoFeatureRecord` normalizer carrying magnitude / depth / time / review-status / significance / felt / tsunami / PAGER alert (USGS-FR-003); 2-D point geometry with **depth in attributes** (never a mislabeled altitude); an **earthquake-only type guard** so a quarry blast isn't plotted as a quake (honest labeling, §37). `UsgsGeoJsonProvider` does an https-only, size-capped fetch (injectable for tests). `usgs_records()` polls no faster than the feed cadence (USGS-FR-002), filters to the **AOI disk + a min-magnitude floor**, **dedupes by event id** (USGS-FR-004) with the seen-set pruned to the in-AOI set each poll so it can't grow unbounded over a soak, and **degrades** (keeping the last good quakes on the map) on a fetch failure rather than crashing (§17.4/§37). `run_usgs()` pumps the bus with jittered backoff.
- **`adapters/usgs_fake_feeder.py`** — canned roster placed at the configured AOI center, so the no-hardware demo renders quakes wherever the station points (PRD §6/§34).
- **`config.py`** — `usgs` toggle + feed/poll/timeout/AOI/min-magnitude settings + env parsing.
- **`backend/main.py`** — launch `run_usgs` when `cfg.usgs`.

### Honesty / scope
USGS earthquake feeds are public-domain (no key); aether only *fetches* within the feed cadence and is **not authoritative** — records carry USGS attribution and a caveat. Magnitude/distance **alert thresholds** (USGS-FR-005) defer to the later environmental-alerts slice. No frontend change: features render generically and the `earthquake` presentation is already registered, so quakes appear as dots with an "Earthquakes" layer toggle.

### Verification (no-hardware gate)
- **10 unit tests** — normalizer field mapping, type/AOI/magnitude filtering, cross-poll dedupe, degraded-on-failure isolation, provider selection.
- **1 integration test** — full adapter→bus→state→ws path: in-AOI quakes arrive as `feature_upsert` with attribution; the far quake and quarry blast are filtered out end to end.
- Gate green: `ruff + mypy + 594 pytest`, "All checks passed."

## What

Extends the S1 per-position drilldown (Numista coins, #461 / PR #468) to the **Binance** holding, so each day's movement in `/historico` is attributable to specific tokens (e.g. "BTC −18 €, ETH −2 €"). This is the price-driven half of PRD #459 (ADR 0035) — coins are frozen, Binance varies live (ADR 0021).

Closes #462.

## How

The S1 machinery (child relation `snapshot_position_holdings`, the `Σ positions == holding` reconciliation invariant, `derivePositionDeltas`, and the zero-JS second-level drilldown rendering) is already source-agnostic. Only two things are new:

- **`tokenPositionSnapshotInput`** (domain) — the live-valued mirror of `coinPositionSnapshotInput`. Freezes one snapshot row per token, keyed by the stable `symbol:wallet` `externalId` (ADR 0021), labelled by symbol, valued live as `balance × price`. An unpriceable token freezes value 0 (never dropped). A token has no metal/thumbnail, so both freeze `null` and the existing drilldown renders its metal-glyph fallback.
- **`load-dashboard`** — builds the `positionDetails` breakdown from Binance sources too, mapping each token to the asset materialized on its rung (market / term-locked, #248) so the contribution lands under the holding it actually rolls up into.

The rendering layer (`historico-table.tsx`) is unchanged — it already renders any `PositionDelta` generically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Snapshot capture freezes one row per token for the Binance holding, keyed by `symbol:wallet`, summing to the holding (`Σ == holding` per scope).
- [x] `/historico` second-level expander shows per-token movers with a symbol label and signed € contribution; price-driven movement is attributed per token (shared S1 renderer).
- [x] A token that zeroes out / disappears stays in the snapshots it was part of (frozen rows, ADR 0008).
- [x] No secrets in token rows; demo gate + scope split inherited at the holding level.
- [x] Domain tests for token capture + reconciliation; rendering covered by the shared S1 drilldown.

## Test plan

- [x] `tokenPositionSnapshotInput` unit tests (priced + value-at-0) — `connected-source.test.ts`
- [x] Integration tests through `loadDashboard` → frozen rows: market breakdown summing to the holding, value-at-0 token kept, and market + term-locked rungs each freezing their own breakdown — `load-dashboard.test.ts`
- [x] Full gauntlet green before commit: `tsc` (domain/db/web), full vitest suite (turbo, all packages), `next` production build, `prettier --check`, `eslint`.

author: ggmoosie
body:
Reworks the raid **building generator** so structures translate cleanly from the
intended design instead of reading as broken open boxes. Everything is contained
in `js/world.js` (the world/building module); weapons/inventory/UI/player files
are untouched, and the collision/AI/loot/minimap/vault contracts are preserved.

## What changed

### 1. Alignment / gaps / overhangs / roof peaks
- **Pitched roof rebuilt** (`addPitchedRoof`): the two slope panels now meet
  **exactly at the ridge** (each panel's ends land on the ridge line + the eave
  by construction), a ridge cap joins them, and the gable ends are proper
  **triangles** (a small custom `BufferGeometry`) flush to the eaves. The old
  gable was a full-height rectangular **block** that poked above the slopes — the
  source of the "roof peaks that don't line up / overhang" complaint.
- **No more double roof**: each building now gets exactly **one** cap — a solid
  ceiling slab at the wall top, then **either** a pitched roof whose eaves rest on
  that slab **or** a flat parapet. The old code always laid a flat roof slab *and*
  floated a pitched roof 0.25u above it (a visible double/floating roof).

### 2. Doors — orientation + casing
- Door leaf is now sized to the doorway **gap width** so a **closed** door fully
  seals its opening. The old fixed-2u leaf left a 0.3u slit on each side of the
  2.6u gap (read as a gap bug). Collider spans the full gap.
- Door **axis matches its wall** (S/N walls → X-running leaf; W/E walls →
  Z-running leaf), and a **jamb + lintel casing** is drawn around every doorway.

### 3. Windows
- `addWindows` reworked into clearly readable **framed openings** (reflective
  glazing + sill/lintel + side mullions + a muntin bar) on every solid outer wall.

### 4. Stairs + walkable second floor
- New **floor colliders** (`addBox opt.floor`): walkable surfaces that
  `groundTopAt()` seats the player on, but `moveActor`/`spotClear`/`vaultProbe`
  never treat as walls (so they don't shove anyone or wall off the ground floor).
- **Stairs** are now a real **walkable ramp** of floor-collider treads (each rise
  ≤ the player's auto step-up tolerance) — the player physically climbs them.
- The **second floor** is a real **walkable slab** laid *around* a stair-well hole
  (flush with the top tread), ringed by a guard parapet. The player ascends and
  walks on it; stepping off the edge falls (handled by existing player gravity).

### 5. Safe spawn
- `findSafeSpawn` now sweeps the arena **perimeter** and picks the clear edge spot
  **farthest from every live enemy** (facing centre), instead of starting
  dead-centre and dropping the player into the enemy cluster. Falls back to inner
  rings only if the whole perimeter is blocked.

## Verification
- `node --check` passes on **all** `js/*.js`.
- No exported symbols moved/renamed, so `CODEMAP.md` is unchanged.
- No browser run here — **needs a human playtest** (see below).

## Needs a playtest
- Climbing the stairs and walking the second floor in a few generated buildings
  (the staircase sits in a back corner; confirm an interior partition wall doesn't
  cross the run on some seeds — partitions have doorway gaps but weren't repositioned).
- Roof seams on both pitched (small) and flat (large) buildings.
- Door open/close passability on all four facings.
- Spawning a few raids to confirm the player lands on the edge, away from fire.

body:
Implements **[P2.6] — Model: baseline + tracking + calibration** (Deep Dive #2 §4.1–4.2, §4b.5). The LightGBM baseline under the four §4.2 disciplines, behind the model package's own interfaces.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Baseline trains and is evaluated **only under purged CV** — `BaselineTrainer` runs `PurgedKFold`, pools out-of-fold predictions (every event predicted by a model that never saw it); all metrics computed on the pooled OOS.
- [x] Importances use **permutation/MDA, not MDI** — `permutation_importance` computed *within* the CV on each held-out fold; `feature_importances_` is never read.
- [x] Probabilities **calibrated** — isotonic (hand-rolled PAVA) fit on the leak-free pooled OOS predictions; calibrated Brier ≤ raw Brier (the isotonic guarantee).
- [x] Runs **logged to MLflow** — `ExperimentTracker` interface with an in-memory default + a lazy, confined `MLflowExperimentTracker` (operator-installed, like ArcticDB, since mlflow pins pandas<3); proven against a faithful fake module.
- [x] **Tested** — 58 new tests, **100% coverage** on all 8 new modules; 786 total pass.

## What's here
- `research/models/`: `baseline.py` (trainer + `LightGBMBaseline`, which implements the live `core.interfaces.Model`), `calibration.py` (PAVA isotonic), `importance.py` (MDA), `scoring.py` (accuracy/log-loss/Brier/AUC, no sklearn), `tracking.py` (`ExperimentTracker` + in-memory + MLflow adapter), `tuning.py` (`HyperparameterTuner`, purged-CV grid search, each candidate logged as a trial).
- `core/config.py` + `config/default.yaml`: `ModelConfig` (capacity/regularization + purged-CV + calibration/importance + seed + `model_version`); `max_depth > 0` / `num_leaves > 1` encode the §4.2 "modest capacity" discipline in the schema.
- `pyproject.toml`: adds `lightgbm` (native API; no pandas pin). **mlflow is intentionally not a declared dependency** (it would downgrade pandas 3→2 — Part II environment policy).
- Also fixes a one-character Part V "Gate status" mirror drift (`Gate 1 ☐ → ☑`).

## Verification
ruff · black · mypy strict (183 files) · 12 pre-commit hooks · `uv lock --check` clean (pandas stays 3.0.3) · **786 tests pass (58 new)**, 100% coverage on new modules. A `test_models_confinement.py` (AST scan) fails CI on any `lightgbm`/`mlflow` import outside `research/models/`.

author: kane50613
body:
Adds top-level `renderSvg` and `renderAnimation` to `takumi-js`, alongside `render`.

## JS
`render` already wrapped the renderer's `render` method with input transform (JSX/HTML/node), emoji extraction, and resource fetching. The two new functions reuse the same pipeline:

- **`renderSvg(element, options)`** → vector SVG document string. Same input + resources as `render`, but emits real `<svg>` (`<rect>`, `<path>`, gradients, glyph outlines, embedded images) instead of a raster bitmap.
- **`renderAnimation({ scenes, ... })`** → encoded animation (WebP/APNG/GIF). Each scene's content is any `RenderInput` (JSX/HTML/node); scenes are transformed and their `<style>` extracted automatically, and image resources are fetched once across all scenes.

The shared steps (renderer resolution, content/emoji resolution, image collection) are factored out of `render` so all three entry points share them — no duplicated pipeline. New exports: `renderSvg`, `renderAnimation`, and types `RenderSvgOptions`, `RenderAnimationOptions`, `RenderAnimationScene`, `RenderInput`.

## Docs
- **Home page** (`index.mdx`): note vector-SVG output via `renderSvg()`.
- **Keyframe animation** (`keyframe-animation.mdx`): the stylesheet example now drives the top-level `renderAnimation()` (no manual `Renderer` / `fromJsx`).
- **v2 upgrade guide** (`upgrade/v2.mdx`): a `renderSvg` section for users coming from [satori](https://github.com/vercel/satori)'s SVG output — `render()` for PNG/WebP, `renderSvg()` for vector.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` (takumi-js): clean. The union-renderer (`napi | wasm`) method calls and the `Managed<...>` option types check out under `strict`.

Changeset: `takumi-js` minor.
