author: exapde
body:
# Summary

This PR adds physics-parameter sweep support to Exasim while preserving the existing single-case workflow. Users can now define multiple `physicsparam` cases in MATLAB, Python, Julia, exported standalone apps, and `pdeapp.txt`/text2code inputs. Exasim runs each case with one concrete `physicsparam` vector and writes deterministic per-case outputs such as `dataout/paramcase_0001/`, `dataout/paramcase_0002/`, etc.

It also adds frontend-side execution mode dispatch so generated executables can be launched in legacy solve mode or postprocess mode from MATLAB/Python/Julia frontends.

# Motivation

Before this branch, Exasim workflows accepted one `physicsparam` vector per simulation. Exploring Reynolds number, angle of attack, material constants, or other model parameters required manually editing inputs and rerunning the frontend or generated app for each case.

This branch makes parameter studies a first-class workflow:

- Frontend users can define sweeps directly in `pde.physicsparamsweep`.
- Exported standalone apps can run sweeps without MATLAB, Python, or Julia at runtime.
- `pdeapp.txt` users can define `physicsparamcases` and run the generated standalone executable once.
- Each case stores the exact parameters used, making runs reproducible and easier to compare.

# Major Changes

- Adds `physicsparamsweep` support to MATLAB, Python, and Julia frontends.
- Adds standalone runtime sweep execution through `datain/physicsparamcases.bin`.
- Extends C++ preprocessing and text2code parsers to accept `physicsparamcases` in `pdeapp.txt`.
- Adds deterministic per-case output directories and reproducibility metadata.
- Adds frontend execution mode dispatch for solve/postprocess executable launches.
- Adds documentation and examples for frontend, exportapp, and text2code sweep workflows.
- Adds a Python frontend unit test for sweep normalization and exported binary file layout.

# Implementation Details

## Frontend-driven sweeps

The MATLAB, Python, and Julia `exasim` frontend paths now normalize optional sweep inputs before preprocessing. Supported user-facing forms include:

- a numeric matrix with one row per case;
- a list/cell/vector form for scalar or explicit samples;
- a structured grid form that expands Cartesian products of parameter values.

For frontend-driven sweeps, Exasim preprocesses and generates code once, then sequentially rewrites the runtime `app.bin` physics parameter data for each case using `writeapp`. Mesh, master, and domain decomposition data are reused across cases. Each case is executed with the same generated executable and fetched from its own output directory.

## Standalone runtime sweeps

The C++ runtime now detects `datain/physicsparamcases.bin` during input parsing. The file format is shared by exportapp and text2code:

- `ncases` as a double;
- `nparam` as a double;
- all parameter values in case-major row order.

At runtime, `ExasimSolver` validates that `nparam` matches the `physicsparam` length in `app.bin`. For each case it:

- selects the active parameter vector;
- overrides `app.physicsparam` before reading the model data;
- rebuilds the model instance for that case;
- recomputes missing generated initial-condition fields using the active parameters;
- writes outputs to `dataout/paramcase_XXXX/out*`;
- writes `physicsparam.txt`, `physicsparam_metadata.txt`, and a top-level `physicsparam_sweep_manifest.txt`.

Existing `sol.bin` fields are still trusted. If `udg`, `odg`, or `wdg` exist in `sol.bin`, they are read as before. If an initial field is missing, the generated `initu`, `initudg`, `initodg`, or `initwdg` path computes it using the currently active case parameters.

## Exported apps

MATLAB, Python, and Julia `exportapp` now write `datain/physicsparamcases.bin` when `physicsparamsweep` is defined. This allows the exported C++ app to run the entire sweep without a frontend installed.

## Text2code and C++ preprocessing

Both the backend preprocessing parser and text2code parser now recognize `physicsparamcases`. They accept nested-row syntax and semicolon-separated row syntax, validate rectangular dimensions, and write the shared binary sweep file next to `app.bin`.

## Execution mode dispatch

The frontend `runcode` implementations now initialize `executionmode = 0` by default. Mode `0` preserves the legacy solve command form for backward compatibility. Mode `1` appends the `postprocess` command argument. Unsupported execution modes fail early with clear errors.

# Compatibility

- Existing single-case examples and applications do not need any changes.
- If no `physicsparamsweep` or `physicsparamcases.bin` is present, runtime behavior remains the legacy single-case solve path.
- Existing `physicsparam` vectors remain valid and keep the same ordering and precision semantics.
- The legacy solve executable command is preserved for `executionmode = 0`.
- Frontend sweeps are additive; the standalone runtime sweep does not replace the frontend sweep loop.
- The standalone runtime sweep is currently solve-mode only and single-model only.
- Cases run sequentially; the implementation is structured so future parallel execution across cases can be added later.

# Testing and Validation

Validation performed for this branch includes:

- `git diff --check origin/master...Kitesurf-Coupling` passed.
- `bash tests/check-hygiene.sh` passed.
- `python3 tests/frontends/python/test_physicsparamsweep.py` passed.
- Rebuilt Exasim, text2code, and the local installed package during feature validation.
- Rebuilt `apps/builtinlibrary/exasimapp` during feature validation.
- Ran the standalone NACA0012 steady text2code sweep with 4 MPI ranks.
- Ran the MATLAB NACA2D frontend sweep.
- Ran the MATLAB NACA2D exportapp sweep and verified exported standalone metadata.
- Ran the MATLAB Eppler exportapp sweep for six cases over `Re = [2000, 5000, 8000]` and angle of attack `[4, 8]` degrees.
- Verified per-case `paramcase_XXXX` output directories, sweep manifests, and stored `physicsparam.txt` files for the sweep examples.

# Notes for Reviewers

- The most important backend review area is `ExasimSolver` sweep lifecycle management: model destruction/rebuild per case, output stream handling, and metadata writing.
- The C++ runtime sweep intentionally rebuilds model state for each case to avoid stale host/device data. This is more conservative than mutating an initialized solver in place and should reduce GPU/MPI correctness risk.
- Initial-condition behavior is intentional: existing fields in `sol.bin` are trusted, while missing fields are recomputed with the active case `physicsparam`.
- The binary sweep file uses doubles for the header and payload to match existing Exasim binary input conventions; runtime values are converted to `dstype` when loaded.
- GPU correctness depends on the existing model construction path copying the updated `app.physicsparam` to device data for each rebuilt case. The sweep avoids in-place parameter mutation of an already initialized GPU model.
- Standalone sweeps currently reject multi-model/coupled runs and postprocess mode. Those are explicit limitations rather than silent partial support.
- The branch is currently one commit behind `origin/master`, so GitHub may report it as out of date with the base branch.

author: tomacox74
body:
## Summary
Mitata release runs were failing after publish because the workflow treated NuGet indexing as the only readiness signal. In the failing release, the package index reported `jroc` as available, but `dotnet tool install --global jroc --version <release>` still returned a 404 moments later.

### Fix
- Replace the one-shot `dotnet tool install/update` step with the same retry pattern used by the other release workflows.
- Clear the NuGet HTTP cache between attempts so the runner does not keep a stale miss.
- Keep retrying until the published `jroc` tool is actually installable, then proceed with the benchmark run.

### Why this is safe

- The retry logic matches the existing smoke/release workflow pattern for package-index propagation delays.

author: iliedanila
body:
## What & why

**Phase 3** ([spec §5](docs/arcscope-precise-tier-spec.md)) retires the product's longest-standing caveat: `find_refs` couldn't follow **member access** (`obj.method()`). It now escalates to the precise tier (TypeScript `LanguageService.findReferences`) for **methods**, resolving call sites **compiler-exact**.

Functions / classes / consts / types stay on the **fast tree-sitter path** (already complete for imported symbols); non-TS files fall back to tree-sitter. So the hot path stays fast, and the gap that mattered — methods — is closed.

## Live on knowledge-graph

`find_refs getDocumentSnapshot` (a DI repository method, invoked only via `this.x.getDocumentSnapshot()`):

```
TREE-SITTER:  No import-resolved references to `getDocumentSnapshot` ...   ← the old caveat
PRECISE:      2 references ... compiler-exact, incl. member access (precision: typescript):
  apps/.../comment-roster.service.ts:86   [call]  documents.getDocumentSnapshot(documentId).pipe(   -> firestore-document.repository.ts:183
  apps/.../document-fork.service.ts:50    [call]  this.documentService.getDocumentSnapshot(...)      -> firestore-document.repository.ts:183
```

From **nothing** to every member-access call site, each resolved to the concrete implementation.

## How

- **`precise-refs.ts`** — `findReferences` from the symbol's definition position; classifies each ref (call/new/access/type); drops the definitions themselves; dedupes each call site (a member call can dispatch to multiple impls — keeps the real implementation, searched in file order). `precisionTier: 'typescript'`.
- **`find_refs`** routes to precise for methods (ProgramStore threaded in), invalidates the Program on index change (no stale refs), and the member-access message now **points at the precise tier** instead of "deferred, not in v1".
- Tool description + INSTRUCTIONS updated; `RefRecord` tier widened to include `typescript`.

## Verification

- **81 tests** (+3: member-access resolution, honest degrade without a precise tier, non-method stays tree-sitter; one existing caveat test updated). `tsc` + build clean.
- Live validation above (correct refs on the real DI-heavy repo).
- Proportionate review call: reuses the adversarially-reviewed precise tier ([#19](https://github.com/iliedanila/arcscope/pull/19)); the one genuinely-new piece (`findReferences` usage + classification) is validated by the live demo and the member-access test. Tree-sitter `find_def`/`find_refs` for non-methods is unchanged.

## Where this lands the arc

The precise tier now reaches the **most-used nav tool**: `find_refs` is compiler-exact for methods, `call_graph`/`flow` resolve dispatch, and flow concepts persist it. The member-dispatch gap that ran through the whole product is closed end to end.

author: anud18
body:
## Problem

Generating a payment roster (造冊) for a **multi-college matrix-mode** scholarship without picking a specific ranking only included the **latest-finalized college's** allocated students. In production: a doctoral scholarship with 4 colleges / 9 allocated students produced a roster with only the 電機院 (2 students). The full name list existed only via the 獎學金分發 → 生成造冊 path (`generate_rosters_from_distribution`); the `/generate` (single-config/period) path was broken.

**Root cause:** `RosterService._get_eligible_applications` (matrix mode, no `ranking_id`) selected **one** `CollegeRanking` via `.order_by(finalized_at.desc()).first()`. Under matrix distribution each college has its own `CollegeRanking`, so `.first()` silently dropped every other college's 正取者.

A second, divergent copy of the bug lived in the `preview_roster_students` endpoint (it self-detected a single ranking via `created_at.desc()`, missing `academic_year`/`is_finalized` filters), so the preview could disagree with the generated roster.

## Fix

1. **`_get_eligible_applications`** — when `ranking_id is None`, aggregate **all** `is_finalized + distribution_executed` rankings for `(scholarship_type_id, academic_year)` and select every `is_allocated` `CollegeRankingItem` via `.in_(ranking_ids)`. Produces **one** roster across all colleges with mixed sub_type (decision **B1**, existing `STD_UP_MIXLISTA` template). An explicit `ranking_id` still scopes to that single ranking.
2. **`preview_roster_students`** — removed its self-contained single-ranking auto-detect so the preview delegates ranking resolution to the same service selector → **preview == generate**.
3. The per-application sub_type/amount derivation in `_create_roster_item` already resolves each student's `allocated_sub_type` per-application when `roster.ranking_id` is NULL — so the aggregated single roster itemizes each row correctly. **Unchanged.**

Net production change: **+29 / −36** lines across `roster_service.py` and `payment_rosters.py`.

## Behavior matrix

| Trigger | Executed rankings | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| `/generate`, no ranking_id | 0 | error 「找不到已執行分發的排名」 (unchanged) |
| `/generate`, no ranking_id | 1 | that ranking's 正取 (== current) |
| `/generate`, no ranking_id | ≥2 (multi-college) | **all colleges, one mixed roster** (the fix) |
| `/generate`, explicit ranking_id | any | that ranking only (unchanged) |
| preview-students | ≥2 | matches generation: all colleges |
| 分發面板 生成造冊 | ≥2 | per-sub_type split (unchanged) |

## Deliberately not changed (per approved spec)

- `generate_rosters_from_distribution` (分發面板 path), `RosterCreateRequest` schema, frontend, semester filtering, borrowed-quota per-item snapshots, `backup_info`.
- **No `.distinct()`** despite the spec's suggestion: the legacy `db.query(Application).all()` already dedupes single-entity rows by PK identity (proven by `test_application_allocated_in_two_rankings_counted_once`), and `SELECT DISTINCT` over the `json` `student_data` column errors on Postgres. Relying on identity-dedup is the correct, test-guarded choice.

## Known follow-ups (out of scope)

- Preview's `allocation_map` enrichment query is not `is_finalized`/`distribution_executed`-scoped (display enrichment only; protected by the one-app-one-allocation invariant).
- Pre-existing N+1 in `_create_roster_item` per-application allocation lookup on the NULL-ranking path.
- Three "find this app's allocation" queries could share one helper.

## Tests

New `backend/app/tests/test_roster_matrix_aggregate_all_colleges.py` (11 behavioural tests via the real `generate_roster` chain, only `StudentVerificationService`/`audit_service` patched) and `test_roster_preview_ranking_consistency.py` (2 scoped source-invariant guards):

- multi-college aggregation; un-allocated excluded; explicit ranking_id scoping; single-ranking regression; 0-rankings raises
- per-student sub_type derivation where allocated sub_type **diverges** from the application's own field (exercises the NULL-ranking derivation path)
- gating: non-finalized excluded; non-executed excluded; prior-year excluded
- dedup invariant (same app in two rankings → counted once)
- preview must not self-select a ranking and must pass `ranking_id` through unchanged

**Run** (host, from `backend/`, dummy env + SQLite — the dev container mounts `main`):
```bash
cd backend && DATABASE_URL='sqlite:///:memory:' DATABASE_URL_SYNC='sqlite:///:memory:' \
  SECRET_KEY='test-secret-key-at-least-32-characters-long-xx' \
  MINIO_ACCESS_KEY='test' MINIO_SECRET_KEY='test' ENVIRONMENT='test' \
  python3 -m pytest app/tests/ -k roster --no-cov
```

Result: **13 focused pass; broader `-k roster` 452 pass**; black 26.3.1 + flake8 (B904/B014/F401/E501) clean.

## Manual verification TODO (post-merge / on a worktree-mounted container)

- [ ] Force-regenerate the dev-data monthly roster (period 114-09) → expect items go from 2 → 9 across colleges A/B/C/E.
- [ ] Export the mixed-sub_type roster Excel (`STD_UP_MIXLISTA`) and confirm per-row amount/fields.

author: prezbar
body:
## Summary

Implements the **Next/React visualization layer** (issue #3): a single local-app page that lists every conversation from the core read API in a sortable shadcn table with full cost data, a Refresh button, and expandable per-conversation detail. The app is a **thin server-side consumer** of `src/core` — it calls only the read API (`listConversations`, `getConversation`, `refresh`) and touches no Prisma/SQL.

Built TDD, one vertical slice per worker:
1. **Presentation helpers + shadcn** — pure `formatTokens` / `formatCost` (adaptive 2–4 dp) / `formatGrandTotalCost` (2 dp) / `grandTotal` aggregation (with the `hasUnpriced` flag), TDD'd in node-env vitest; shadcn `table` + `button` installed.
2. **List page** (server component) — renders all 9 columns (Folder, Title, Model(s) dominant + `+N`, Input, Output, Cache-write, Cache-read, Total, Cost), default sort **Cost desc** via search params, grand-total footer summing tokens by type + cost, unpriced row/footer markers, zero-usage rows at $0, and a "Click Refresh to scan" empty state.
3. **All columns sortable server-side** — a pure, tested `sortConversations` comparator in the app zone (see plan note below).
4. **Refresh action + button** — a `"use server"` action wrapping `core.refresh()` with `revalidatePath("/")`; a client button showing a spinner + disabled state while scanning and surfacing the full `RefreshSummary` (parsed/skipped/deleted, malformed-skipped, duration).
5. **Row expansion + detail** — rows expand (click + keyboard, `aria-expanded`) to lazily call a `getConversationDetail` action wrapping `core.getConversation(id)`, rendering per-model cost, sub-agent rollup, and per-Skill breakdowns.

## Validation gate (all sentinels pass)

`pnpm test` → TEST OK (11 files, 93 tests) · `pnpm lint` → LINT OK · `pnpm fallow` → FALLOW OK · `pnpm build` → BUILD OK

## How the plan evolved

- **Sorting (added slice 2b).** Slice 2 found that core's `listConversations({sortBy})` only sorts **top-level scalar keys**, so delegating sort to core would make only Title and Cost sortable — failing AC #2 ("columns are sortable") for the analytically important token columns. Adapted in service of the goal: added a pure, tested **server-side comparator in the app zone** (`src/app/_lib/sort.ts` `sortConversations`) so all 9 columns sort via URL params — no client-side sorting, **no changes to the frozen `src/core` API**. Sorting stays server-side (the user's chosen approach).
- **Core-loading under `cacheComponents: true`.** Importing `@/core/refresh` at module top level crashes `next build` ("Collecting page data") because `src/core/db.ts` evaluates `import.meta.dirname` at import time. Established pattern across all server entry points: `import type` only at top level, then `await connection()` + `const { … } = await import("@/core/refresh")` at request time. This keeps the build green and guarantees core never lands in the client bundle.

## Decisions / assumptions workers made

- **UI testing** is pragmatic and **pure-function only** (node-env vitest; no jsdom/RTL added) — formatting, grand-total aggregation, sort comparator, and refresh/detail shaping helpers are unit-tested; React rendering is not. (Confirmed approach up front.)
- `formatCost`: exact `0` → `$0.00`; `|usd| ≥ 0.01` → 2 dp; `0 < |usd| < 0.01` → 4 dp (so sub-cent costs stay legible). Grand total always 2 dp per spec.
- `+N` badge: `N = distinctCount - 1` (other models beyond the dominant), shown only when `distinctCount > 1`.
- Unpriced shown as a `~` prefix + tooltip on the row Cost cell and the footer total (lower-bound indicator).
- Sub-agent label: empty/root `agentType` → "main". Folder cell shows `project.folder` with full `project.path` on hover.

## Reviews

- **Final fresh-review** (independent, read-only, whole-diff, graded against issue #3): **0 blockers, 0 should-fix, 2 consider — ship.** The core/client boundary was traced (every core import reachable from a `"use client"` file is `import type` only; core touched solely in `"use server"` actions via dynamic import; no SQL in the app), all 9 acceptance criteria verified met, and every field read matches the core contract exactly (no shape/name drift).
- No mid-run slice review was needed (slice 3's "risk flag" was the inherent fact that `refresh()` mutates the DB — contained to request time, never triggered by build/tests).
- **No auto-fixes were applied** (no blocker/should-fix findings) — the 2 `consider` items are left for the human below. (Note: per the review-once-fix-once policy, fixes if any are not re-reviewed.)

### Consider-level items left for review
- `src/app/_components/conversation-row.tsx` — a **failed** detail fetch sets `status: "error"`, but the refetch guard only fires on `status === "idle"`, so collapsing and re-expanding a failed row shows the stale error and never retries (despite the panel saying "Try again"). Low-impact (transient failures only), but worth making `error` retryable. *(reviewer: high confidence)*
- `src/app/_lib/format.ts` — a sub-cent **grand total** rounds to `$0.00` (the explicit 2-dp rule); when also unpriced it reads `~$0.00` ("approximately zero" for a non-zero lower bound). Token counts remain exact. Spec tension rather than a clear defect — could suppress `~` when the total renders `$0.00`. *(reviewer: medium confidence)*

## Out-of-goal discoveries (parked, not acted on)
- `pnpm fallow` in this repo runs only `fallow dupes` (CLAUDE.md describes more checks); a worker noted a clone group below the min-occurrences threshold — not flagged, not acted on.

Closes #3

author: sbesh91
body:
Adds library-agnostic payload validation via the [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) spec across four surfaces. Bring your own validator (Zod, Valibot, ArkType, anything implementing `~standard`); the framework runtime depends only on the types-only `@standard-schema/spec`.

## What you can do

```ts
// shared module (non-.server, so the browser can import it)
export const NewTask = z.object({ title: z.string().min(1), count: z.coerce.number() })

// .server.ts: server-authoritative validation
export const create = defineAction(
  (ctx, payload) => { /* payload: { title: string; count: number } */ },
  { input: NewTask },
)

// component: opt-in client pre-validation, type-linked to the action
<Form action={create} schema={NewTask}>
  <input name="title" />
  <FieldError name="title" />
</Form>

// loaders: validate + coerce URL params
defineLoader(fn, { searchSchema: z.object({ page: z.coerce.number().min(1).default(1) }) })
serverRoute('/task/:id').loader(fn, { paramsSchema: z.object({ id: z.coerce.number() }) })
```

## Design

- **Server is authoritative; client validation is opt-in.** The server always validates at the handler seam (after auth/page middleware, before the handler). Client `<Form schema>` pre-validation is an enhancement and requires a shared (non-`.server`) module.
- **No framework coercion.** Standard Schema validates `Input -> Output`; the schema coerces (`z.coerce.number()`), the framework passes the raw payload as `Input`.
- **Carried payload type is `InferOutput`, uniformly** (handler, `useAction`, `<Form>`), keyed on the existing single `TPayload` param.
- **Failures reuse `deny`.** Action schema failure -> `deny(422)` with normalized issues under a reserved `deny.data` key; read via `getValidationIssues(useActionResult(...))`. Loader failure -> `deny(400)` (search) / `deny(404)` (params) to the error boundary. `useParams()` stays string (coercion is loader-side).

## Surfaces

| Surface | API | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| Action payload | `defineAction(fn, { input })` | `deny(422)` + issues |
| Form fields | `<Form schema>` + `useFieldErrors()` / `<FieldError>` | submit-gate + live-clear |
| Loader search | `defineLoader(fn, { searchSchema })` | 400 -> error boundary |
| Loader params | `defineLoader(fn, { paramsSchema })` | 404 -> error boundary |

## Public API added

`getValidationIssues`, `useFieldErrors`, `FieldError`; types `StandardSchemaV1`, `ValidationIssue`, `InferSchemaInput`, `InferSchemaOutput`, `FieldErrorsMap`; options `input` / `searchSchema` / `paramsSchema` / `<Form schema>`. (`searchSchema`/`paramsSchema`, not `search`/`params`, since `DefineLoaderOpts.params` is the existing cache-key list.)

## Testing

- Unit: `validateWithSchema` + normalization (hand-rolled schema against the raw spec), action enforcement (deny 422, handler not called, coercion observable), Form pre-validation (submit-gate, live-clear), loader enforcement (400/404 + coercion).
- Type-level (`*.test-d.ts`): payload inferred from `input`; `<Form schema>` drift rejection; loader `ctx.location` narrowing.
- End-to-end with real Zod (devDep) through actions + loaders.
- All 7 CI steps green: build, format:check, typecheck, test:types, test:coverage (1615 tests, +26), test:integration, site build.

## Dogfood + docs

- `/demo` task board's create-task action uses `input` + `<Form schema>` + `<FieldError>` with **Valibot** (tree-shakeable, ~1kb, minimal client-bundle impact).
- New guide page `docs/validation`; LLM corpus + AGENTS drift gates updated.

Design + plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-21-standard-schema-validation-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-21-standard-schema-validation.md`.

body:
## Summary

PR 3 of 4. Makes the SP1/ZK lane reproducible with a **cheap, execute-only smoke path** that runs in CI without the SP1 toolchain, while keeping heavy proving and end-to-end differential tests gated behind `RUN_SP1_E2E=1`. Also fixes the repo's only pre-existing `tsc --noEmit` error.

**Stacked on PR #61** (`feat/pq-evidence-artifact-schema`). Base is that branch; review this PR's diff alone. Merge order: #60 → #61 → this.

## What it adds / fixes

- **`scripts/prover-client.ts`** — fixes the pre-existing typecheck error (`encodeProof` was typed `Promise<string>` but returns synchronously) and extracts a pure, deterministic `ProverClient.encodePublicValues` used by **both** the proof path and the smoke lane, so they bind to the exact same guest journal. `tsc --noEmit` is now clean.
- **`scripts/sp1-smoke.ts`** (`npm run sp1:smoke`) — a deterministic journal-encoding check that needs **no SP1 toolchain** (runs in CI), plus an **optional execute-only** step (SP1 `execute`, no proving) when a built `mldsa65-host` binary is present. It never proves.
- **`test/SP1Smoke.test.ts`** (5 tests) — pure-core coverage: deterministic 160-byte journal, decode round-trip, parity with `encodeProof`, input validation.
- **`package.json`** — adds `sp1:smoke` and `typecheck` scripts; version 0.7.0 → 0.8.0.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — adds a **Typecheck** step and an **SP1 smoke** step (execute-only journal check, no toolchain) to `build-test`.
- **`docs/SP1_Smoke_Lane.md`** (+ runbook pointer) — documents the normal CI / smoke / gated-e2e lanes and what each proves vs only executes.

## What the smoke lane proves vs does not

| Claim | Smoke (pure, CI) | Smoke (+execute) | Gated e2e / prove |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Journal encoding well-formed & deterministic | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Rust guest commits same journal for a valid sig | — | ✅ (execute) | ✅ |
| Guest rejects tampered signatures | — | — | ✅ |
| Real Groth16 proof generated & verifies | — | — | ✅ |
| On-chain ML-DSA verification | ❌ (mock path on-chain) | ❌ | ❌ |
| Production custody / mainnet fund flow | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

The smoke lane **never proves** anything and makes **no on-chain verification or production claims**. The active testnet verifier remains the mock path. Research prototype — not audited, testnet/local only, no real yield, not "quantum-proof".

## Verification

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run sp1:smoke` | deterministic JSON summary; `hostExecuted: false` in CI (no toolchain) |
| `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) | **clean (0 errors)** |
| `npx hardhat test` | **391 passing / 10 pending** (gated SP1) |
| `npx hardhat test test/SP1Smoke.test.ts` | 5 passing |
| `npm run format:check` | clean |
| Gated (`RUN_SP1_E2E=1` + built host) | not run here — requires the SP1 toolchain/WSL2 |

author: eng-eslamezzat
body:
## Summary

Adds a configurable `n_init` confirmation grace window to the tracker, fixing short-track fragmentation: today a newly-born (unconfirmed) track is `mark_removed()` immediately if it isn't re-matched on the very next frame, so a target missed by association for a single frame is deleted and re-spawns a new ID. Measured on soccer broadcast footage, **61% of new tracks died after one frame**.

## Changes (2 commits)
1. **`feat: add n_init tracker param`** — new `int n_init` on `TrackerParams` + `BoTSORT::_n_init`, read in `_load_params_from_config`. Plumbing only, no behavior change.
2. **`feat: confirmation grace`** — in the stage-3 unconfirmed-removal loop, only remove a track once it has been unconfirmed for `>= _n_init` frames (`_frame_id - start_frame >= _n_init`). A kept track stays in `_tracked_tracks` (state `Tracked`), predicts forward via its Kalman filter, and stays eligible for re-association. Default `n_init = 3` preserves prior behavior except that it *retains* tracks the old code deleted (never deletes one it kept).

## Why merge this to the fork's `main`
These commits are consumed by the parent OpticXI engine via the submodule pin. They currently live only on this branch; merging to `main` lets the parent re-point its submodule at `main` instead of a feature branch.

## Validation (in the parent engine, opticxi-engine-core #150)
A/B on `ten_min.mp4`: distinct track IDs **1019 → 830 (−18.5%)**, median lifespan **5.9 → 8.8 s**, zero over-merge regression (under-segmented minutes 5 → 1). `n_init` swept {2,3,4}; 3 is the knee. CPU unit tests added on the engine side (`soccer_test_per_class_tracker_bank`): grace keeps the ID across a one-frame miss under `n_init=3` but churns under `n_init=1`.

body:
## Contexto

La vista de revisión/calificación de una entrega (`TeacherSubmissionPreview`) se sentía "amontonada": dos cabeceras apiladas (la barra azul global de 80px + el topbar local) y el chip de PUNTOS partía el número en dos líneas. Esta PR descongestiona el topbar, mueve la navegación e identidad al sidebar y corrige varios detalles de calidad y accesibilidad detectados en el camino. Solo frontend; sin backend, sin cambios de contrato/API.

## Cambios

- **Volver → sidebar** (arriba de "Revisión docente", estilo superficie oscura + focus ring) y **Volver en móvil** dentro de la barra de módulos (el sidebar se oculta en `<md`).
- **Topbar más limpio**: se quita el título (ya está en el sidebar) y se baja `h-16 → h-12`; queda solo la línea de contexto curso·correo (peso semibold, 12px).
- **Chip de PUNTOS** ya no se parte: `whitespace-nowrap` + `tabular-nums` + `shrink-0`.
- **PUNTOS = total del caso**: el denominador suma el valor de **todas** las preguntas (default 10 c/u vía `DEFAULT_QUESTION_MAX_POINTS`, refleja el "Valor de la pregunta" editado), no solo las calificadas.
- **ESTADO enfocado en calificación**: `POR CALIFICAR` / `CALIFICADO` (badge ámbar→verde) vía helper local `getReviewStatus`; **no** toca el formateador compartido del cuadernillo.
- **Botón "Actualizar" compacto** (ícono + etiqueta corta; `aria-label` preservado).
- **Defectos móviles**: las píldoras de módulo muestran el **nombre** (p. ej. "Case Reader") en vez de "m1".
- **Fila ENTREGA** a ancho completo (`col-span-2`) para ver la fecha completa sin recortar.
- **A11y**: contraste de etiquetas del footer (slate-500→slate-400), números tabulares, anillos `focus-visible`.

author: lantum-brendan
body:
Adds a Model Context Protocol server so external AI clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor) can read and act on a user's Trakli data, using the maintained `laravel/mcp` Streamable-HTTP transport.

Auth is a Sanctum bearer token a user issues from Settings > Connected AI clients (paired UI change in trakli/webui). Read tools (wallets, transactions, categories, parties, stats) and write tools (create wallet, record transaction) reuse the REST API's validation and ownership; writes are gated per user, defaulting to allowed and overridable by a gate an operator defines.

Two related fixes ride on the same branch:

- Closes #275: confirming a wallet, category, or party now resumes the assistant against the original request rather than stopping, so it continues with the transaction that needed the new record.
- Closes #284: every agent turn records per-user token usage through the metrics package.

── Summary ─────────────────────────────────

First smart-delta sync without a prior force-scan timestamp was doing a full metadata refresh, which diverged from the Python behavior and made initial sync more expensive than intended. This keeps the first pass in fast ID-only mode unless force is explicit or the weekly force interval is due.

── Changes ─────────────────────────────────

| Type | File | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| Fix | [LibrarySyncService.swift](Packages/Services/Sources/Services/Workflow/LibrarySyncService.swift) | Treat missing lastForceScanDate as fast mode instead of initial force refresh. |
| Test | [LibrarySyncServiceTests.swift](Packages/Services/Tests/ServicesTests/LibrarySyncServiceTests.swift) | Align the missing-timestamp expectation with the Python smart-delta contract. |

```bash
env CLANG_MODULE_CACHE_PATH="$PWD/.build/clang-module-cache" swift test --disable-sandbox --package-path Packages/Services --filter LibrarySyncServiceTests/missingForceScanTimestampStaysInFastMode  # RED before fix, pass after fix

```

── Notes ───────────────────────────────────

Review focus: `shouldRefreshCommonTrackMetadata(force:)` only changes the no-prior-force-scan branch. Explicit force scans and stale weekly scans still fetch common-track metadata and update the force-scan timestamp.

## Summary by Sourcery

Align smart-delta sync behavior so that an initial run without a prior force-scan timestamp stays in fast ID-only mode instead of performing a full metadata refresh.

Bug Fixes:
- Treat missing last force-scan timestamp as non-forced fast mode rather than triggering an initial full metadata refresh.

author: scienceisneato
body:
Migrates this repo's slop-mop CI from the hand-spun install (`slopmop[all]==1.5.0`) to **`ScienceIsNeato/slop-mop-action@v2`** (slop-mop 2.11.0). This is both an action adoption *and* a major slop-mop upgrade.

## What changed
- **Swapped** `pip install slopmop[all]==1.5.0` + `sm scour` → the v2 action.
- **Kept** the project setup: `npm ci`, `.venv` + `requirements.txt`, `npm run build`. The slop-mop gates detect `.venv` and analyze against it — so `dependency-risk` audits the project's **real** deps and type-gates resolve its imports.
- **Dropped** the `pyjwt>=2.13.0` patch — it was forcing a fix for slop-mop's *own* transitive dep (mcp/semgrep → pyjwt). That now lives isolated in the action's pipx venv and is no longer part of this repo's dependency audit.
- **find-duplicate-strings** comes from the manifest (npm) instead of a hardcoded `npm install -g`.

author: thomaspryor
body:
## What

New `scripts/auto-triage-cross-production.js` — conservatively flags `wrongProduction=true` from `data/audit/cross-production-audit.json`, only on items with a concrete reassignment target (`closerTo`) and a non-ambiguous signal (high confidence by default; medium opt-in via `--include-medium`). Dry-run by default; `--apply` writes.

## Why the requested filter didn't apply

The task asked to flag `class==='A' && !outOfScope && !resolved && articleYear < showYear-5` over "1,159 open" items. Those fields don't exist in the audit schema. The real schema is `{file, publishDate, filedUnder, closerTo, urlYear, matchReason, confidence, hasDupeInCorrectDir}`, and the "1,159" is the **`ambiguous`/`low` bucket** — reviews with no parseable date, no URL-year match, no venue match, and `closerTo: null`. The audit deliberately records but does not claim them. Auto-flagging them would corrupt the corpus.

## Result on current data (1,210 audit issues)

- **29** issues have a `closerTo` target; **27** are high-confidence.
- **26** of those 27 already carry the full human-clear set (`wrongProductionManualClear` + `override` + `humanReviewedWrongProduction=false` + `allowEarlyDate` + `allowCrossMarket`) — settled human decisions to keep them. The script refuses to override a human clear.
- The **1** remaining (`titanique-west-end-2024/british-theatre--susan-novak.json` → `titanique-2026`) is a **false positive**: an evergreen britishtheatre.com *tickets page* whose text says "Criterion Theatre / West End" (the WE production's actual venue); its `2026-05-19` re-scrape date tricked the publish-date heuristic into pointing at the Broadway 2026 run.

**Net: 0 reviews auto-flagged.** No data changes to ship — the script is the deliverable.

## Flag shape (when it does fire)

Mirrors the canonical date-based setter in `rebuild-all-reviews.js`: `wrongProduction=true` + `wrongProductionReason='cross-production-audit'` (the `hasManualReason` breadcrumb that survives rebuild auto-clear passes) + `wrongProductionNote`. The prompt's "8 protection fields" are for *clearing* a review, not flagging one.

## Verification

- `node scripts/scoring-delta.js` → 0 newly excluded / included, 0 T1 flips, within tolerance.
- Single candidate hand-verified against `shows.json` venues and full text.

author: iamzulx
body:
Full-codebase security review after Round 1 hardening. Findings and fixes:

**Billing bypass (high)** — `POST /v1/chat/completions` resolved a provider from the model string but never required the model to be in our catalog. Any model on a loaded provider (unlisted, or `is_active=0`) had no pricing row, so cost was `0` — skipping the balance check and deduction entirely (free, unmetered usage). Now the model must exist and be active in `models` before forwarding.

**Rate-limit self-escalation (high)** — `PUT /api/budget` let any user set their own `rate_limit`/`daily_limit`, which the limiter reads straight from the key row, defeating per-tier throttling. Those fields are tier-governed and no longer client-writable; only the self-imposed `monthly_budget` remains editable (validated).

**Privilege escalation via tier (high)** — admin was gated on `tier === "enterprise"`, but enterprise is a purchasable tier and `POST /api/pricing/upgrade` let a user self-upgrade by merely holding the balance. So any user who reached the tier balance got full admin (list/modify all users and balances). Admin is now gated on a dedicated `is_admin` flag (new column + migration, granted out-of-band); self-serve upgrades to enterprise are blocked.

**BYOK secret exposure (high)** — user-supplied provider keys were stored in plaintext (the code even noted "encrypt in production"). They're now encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM; `ENCRYPTION_KEY` is validated in production like `JWT_SECRET`.

**PII leak (medium)** — `GET /api/referral/leaderboard` exposed every referrer's email to any authenticated user. Email dropped.

**Stored XSS (medium)** — the SPA rendered user-controlled values (API key name) into `innerHTML` unescaped. Added an `esc()` helper and applied it.

### Noted, not changed here (flagged as Linear comments)
- `POST /api/midtrans/callback` credits the IDR `gross_amount` directly onto the USD `balance` (~16,000× over-credit) — needs a product FX decision, not a blind code change.
- `src/routes/dashboard.ts` is dead code (not mounted) but authenticates by `?token=<user.id>` with no secret — should be removed or rebuilt on real sessions before mounting.
- `/health` exposes user/model counts unauthenticated.

Verified: typecheck clean (only the pre-existing `seed.ts` rootDir config error remains), DB migration adds `is_admin` defaulting to 0 even for enterprise users, and AES-GCM round-trips.

author: askpt
body:
## Why

`RpcResolver` event-stream tests fail intermittently on `windows-latest` (for example [this run](https://github.com/open-feature/dotnet-sdk-contrib/actions/runs/27900850597)) with:

```
Assert.True() Failure - Expected: True, Actual: False
at RpcResolverTests.HandleEvents_WithNoFlags_CallsFlagdProviderEventHandler
```

## Root cause

The mocked gRPC stream signalled end-of-stream **immediately** once its responses were consumed. `RpcResolver.HandleEvents` only increments its retry counter inside `catch (RpcException)`, so when `MoveNext` returns `false` (rather than throwing) the retry bound is never reached and the inner `await MoveNext()` completes synchronously. The loop then reconnects in an unbounded, never-awaiting **hot CPU spin**.

Because the tests never called `Shutdown()` (unlike `InProcessResolverTests`), each test **leaked a busy-spinning background task**. xUnit runs test classes in parallel, so the accumulated spinners saturated the 2-core Windows runner and the 10s waits timed out. The same loop is a latent production bug: a gracefully closed stream would hot-spin in the field.

## Approach

**Production (`RpcResolver.HandleEvents`)**
- Pass the cancellation token to `MoveNext(token)` so the read is cancellable and shutdown is responsive.
- Catch `OperationCanceledException` for graceful shutdown.
- On a graceful end-of-stream (loop exits while not cancelled), route through the existing `HandleErrorEvent()` retry/backoff path (bounded by `MaxEventStreamRetries`) instead of immediately reconnecting in a tight loop.

**Tests (`RpcResolverTests`)**
- `SetupGrpcStream` now emulates a real long-lived stream: after yielding the configured responses it parks on the supplied cancellation token instead of returning `false` instantly, eliminating the in-test hot-spin.
- Each `HandleEvents_*` test shuts the resolver down in a `finally` and sets `WithMaxEventStreamRetries(1)`, mirroring `InProcessResolverTests`, so no background task leaks between tests.
- Blocking `AutoResetEvent.WaitOne(10_000)` waits are replaced with the existing async `Utils.AssertUntilAsync` helper, so tests no longer block a thread-pool thread or depend on real-time scheduling under CPU pressure. All existing assertions are preserved.

## Notes for reviewers

- The behavior change worth a careful look: a graceful end-of-stream now emits a `ProviderError` and backs off (bounded) rather than silently hot-reconnecting. In practice flagd closes the stream via an `RpcException`, so this path is defensive, but it removes the unbounded spin at the source.

## Verification

- Full Flagd suite green on net8.0 (166) and net9.0 (166); `src` builds on all TFMs including net462.
- `RpcResolverTests` stable across 5 consecutive runs (~390ms each); the net8.0 suite dropped from ~46s to under 1s now that the spin is gone.
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` clean on the changed files.

author: zkysar1
body:
## What

A **sub-agent is a sub-task within the parent's already-started session**, not a new session — but `AgentLoop` fired `SESSION_START` once per *loop*, and every sub-agent gets its own loop. So **every sub-agent re-ran the workspace's SessionStart hooks.**

On a framework with a heavy SessionStart — e.g. a Mind's boot orchestrator (daemon start + recovery-gate + conventions load, a 95s-timeout hook) — this is wasted work per sub-agent. And because the `task` tool runs subtasks **concurrently** (`asyncio.gather`), a parallel best-of-N fan-out fired N boots *simultaneously*, which then **contended on shared resources** (the single daemon, file locks).

The result was the opposite of what parallelism should do:

| Parallel best-of-N research loop | Wall-clock |
|---|---|
| before (per-subagent boots) | **3587s (60 min)** |
| after (sub-agents skip boot) | **664s (11 min)** |

~5.4× faster, and now faster than the sequential baseline — measured on a live Mind probe.

## Fix

- `AgentLoop.__init__` gains `fire_session_start: bool = True`; `_session_started` is initialized to `not fire_session_start`.
- `SubAgentRunner` builds child loops with `fire_session_start=False`.

This **matches Claude Code**, where a sub-agent (Task) does not re-fire SessionStart. `_session_started` is used *only* to gate SESSION_START (the other lifecycle fires are PRE_COMPACT; there's no SESSION_END pairing), so the change is localized and the top-level path is unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_subagent_does_not_refire_session_start` — a real sub-agent with a recording SESSION_START lifecycle hook runs a turn and the hook does **not** fire.
- `uv run poe check` green: **2060 passed**, ruff + format + mypy clean.

author: mvanhorn
body:
## Summary
transcrub advertises a multi-source chronological feed but today only ingests Claude-shaped data (`claude-code`, `claude-json`, `text`). This adds a `chatgpt` loader that reads the official ChatGPT data export (`conversations.json`), so the feed now spans ChatGPT alongside Claude. No viewer changes.

## Why this matters
ChatGPT is the most common transcript people have, and the export is a local file users already possess, so it fits the local-only privacy model exactly. Because the loader emits the same turn schema the other loaders produce, the corpus chips, search, filters, and margin marks all work with zero changes to `coread.html`. This is the loader that makes the "multi-source" framing real for most people.

## How it works
- Walks each conversation's `mapping` graph along the active branch (`current_node` -> root via parent pointers), so regenerated/dead branches are ignored. Falls back to `create_time` order when `current_node` is absent.
- Maps `author.role == "user"` -> a new turn's `prompt`, `assistant` -> `reply`, joins `content.parts`, captures tool names and the `model_slug`, and converts `create_time` epochs to ISO timestamps so they sort with the existing string-date ordering.
- Registered in `LOADERS` as `chatgpt`; documented in the scanner docstring, README source list, and `sources.example.json`.
- Standard library only, no network calls.

## Testing
Ran `scan.py` against a realistic `conversations.json` (a conversation with a regenerated branch) and asserted the output: prompt/reply pairing is correct, the dead/regenerated branch is excluded via the `current_node` walk, the model slug (`gpt-4o`) and a tool node (`python`) are captured, and `create_time` epochs become ISO timestamps. All assertions pass.

65 lines, additive, one new loader plus docs.

author: oudaykhaled
body:
## Problem (proven on-device, iter6 FINAL-PROOF STEP-5 caveat)

The on-device compose-request flow created the request **without a recipient phone**, so the gateway request-store row had `RecipientPhone=null`. The gateway `POST /deliveries/{id}/otp/verify {code:"1234"}` then returned **400 "Recipient phone is missing on the delivery row"**. The OTP mechanism is fine (the 1234 path is proven working on a delivery that HAS a phone); compose just never captured/passed one.

## Root cause — where the phone is actually read

The gateway OTP **issue** (`GET /v1/deliveries/{id}/otp`) and **verify** (`POST /deliveries/{id}/otp/verify`) paths read `delivery.RecipientPhone` where `delivery = await _store.GetAsync(deliveryId)` — i.e. the gateway's **own request-store row** (`IRequestsStore` / `DeliveryRequest.RecipientPhone`), **not** the delivery-service row. That store row is populated from `CreateRequestBody.RecipientPhone` (JSON `recipientPhone`) on `POST /requests`. The mobile create body simply never sent it.

The gateway already plumbs `recipientPhone` fully end-to-end (`CreateRequestBody → CreateRequestInput → store → DeliveryRequest.RecipientPhone`, surfaced on the read DTO), with the `S09RecipientPhonePlumbingTests` keystone regression guard. **No gateway change is needed.**

## Fix (mobile-only)

- `RequestDraft` gains an optional `recipientPhone`.
- `DioRequestSubmissionService` now sends `recipientPhone` in the `POST /requests` body. The compose UI has no recipient-phone field today, so it **defaults to the signed-in client's own phone** (the requester is the default recipient) via a new `RecipientPhoneResolver` → `DioRecipientPhoneResolver`, which reads the `phone` field from `GET /v1/users/me`.
- Precedence: an explicit draft phone wins; otherwise the resolved client phone; otherwise the field is omitted. The lookup is **best-effort** — a resolver miss/fault degrades to omitting the field so the order create is never blocked (the gateway field is optional/additive).
- DI wires the resolver into the live `RequestSubmissionService`.

## Request → delivery phone path

`POST /requests {recipientPhone}` → gateway `CreateRequestBody.RecipientPhone` → `CreateRequestInput.RecipientPhone` → `IRequestsStore` → `DeliveryRequest.RecipientPhone`. The at-door OTP issue/verify reads the phone from **this** store row, so `code:"1234"` now dispatches/validates → 200/Done.

## Gateway follow-up flagged (non-blocking)

The B5 mint body `CreateDeliveryRowUpstream` (`POST /api/v1/deliveries`) does **not** carry `recipient_phone` — it only seeds id/tenant/client/jeeber/tier/pickup. This does **not** affect the gateway OTP-1234 path (which reads the gateway store, not the delivery-service row), so it is out of scope here. But the delivery-service `deliveries.recipient_phone` column stays null. If any future consumer needs the phone on the canonical delivery-service row (e.g. delivery-service-side OTP/SMS), a small gateway+delivery-service change to thread `recipient_phone` through `CreateDeliveryRowUpstream` would be needed. Flagged, not changed.

## Test / analyze

- `flutter analyze` clean on all changed files (zero issues; the 18 repo-wide info lints are all pre-existing, in unrelated files).
- 28 tests pass: 4 new submission-service cases (draft phone wins / default from resolver / omitted when none / resolver-fault degrades) + 6 new resolver cases + the existing submission/route/request-type suites.

PR targets `temp-overall-run-1` (NOT main).

## What

Add a dedicated filter for `docker build` (and `docker buildx`). Previously `docker build` had no dispatch arm and fell through to `passthrough`.

## Why

The bulk of a `docker build` log is base-image layer-fetch progress (`Pulling fs layer` / `Downloading [..]` / `Extracting [..]` / `Pull complete`) and apt download lines (`Get:` / `Fetched`) — pure token noise. The signal is the build structure, errors, and the final image.

## How

Mirrors the `make` filter:
- strip ANSI, process **stdout + stderr** as one stream (BuildKit `--progress=plain` writes to stderr),
- drop layer-fetch / download / intermediate-container noise, collapse blank runs, dedup, head/tail truncate,
- fall back to `passthrough` when the output does not look like a build (nothing dropped and under the line cap).

Normalisation before the noise check:
- `<layer-id>: <status>` → the layer id (short hex) is stripped so `Downloading`/`Pull complete`/etc. match,
- BuildKit `#N <ts> <body>` → the `#N` marker and decimal timestamp are stripped (so `#8 0.5 Get:1 …` is recognised as noise while `#5 [2/5] RUN …` and `#5 DONE` are kept).

**Kept always:** `Step N/M`, BuildKit stage headers, `Successfully built/tagged`, and any line containing `error`/`failed`/`cannot`. The full original is stored for `hush expand` (lossless).

## Output / ratio

Fixture (`tests/fixtures/docker-build/build.stdout`) compresses **3.1 KB -> 742 B (~76%)**. Added a `CASES` entry with a 0.55 floor.

## Test

- New unit tests: drops pull/apt noise & intermediate layer ids while keeping steps and the result; keeps error lines; BuildKit prefix stripping.
- `cargo test` (138 passed) / `fmt` / `clippy -D warnings` / `--no-default-features` build all green.
- Pure & lossless; does not touch the gate/transmission path.

author: mircea-popescu
body:
## What this adds

Two changes so the next OTA both shortens the failure window **and** makes any remaining failure diagnosable.

1. **Request timeout 30s → 10s.** The 10s value was committed on PR #14's branch but #14 merged at an earlier head, so `main` still had 30s. 30 seconds of spinner before the retry button is too long on mobile; 10s still clears genuinely slow mobile networks.

2. **Home error screen shows the actual error text** (name + message, selectable). A timeout reads as `AbortError`; a Supabase/PostgREST/auth failure brings its own message (e.g. `AuthApiError: ...`). If loading still fails after this update, one screenshot pinpoints the exact cause instead of another round of guessing.

## Context

The infinite spinner means the Home `load()` promise never settles — only a fetch with no timeout does that. The 10s timeout guarantees termination; this PR makes the resulting error legible rather than a generic "couldn't load".

## Delivery

OTA only (confirmed working). After merge: `eas update --branch preview`, then launch the app twice (download, then apply). No rebuild.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: richardeko
body:
A phased plan answering the debuggability-of-emergence adoption risk — the one most specific to coordinator-free design, and structurally invisible to the 25-axis audit (it measures node-local legibility, which is strong, and is blind to the emergent stratum, which is blank).

**Load-bearing design decision:** the diagnostic layer is *itself coordinator-free*. Every node already holds the complete gossiped fleet soft-state, so any node computes fleet-level diagnostics **locally** — no central collector (which would reintroduce a coordinator). HLC supplies causal order without a central clock; bounded per-node event rings, collected on demand via **scatter-gather** (a pull fan-out, not a central log), supply the only thing not already in local KV: other nodes' temporal history.

**Six phases:** 0 taxonomy + detection-source classification → 1 emergent-condition tripwires (`/stats`-shaped; *the #56 governor-vs-autojoin detector*) → 2 fleet snapshot (relational, computed from local KV) → 3 causal event ring + fan-out reconstruction (the hard *explain*) → 4 fleet narrative (the SRE-facing payoff) → 5 operator surface + runbook + coop demo.

**Invariants:** no collector · detection-not-prevention · zero-overhead-when-off · false-positives-are-the-product · library-not-platform. **Acceptance gate:** a non-designer Detects→Localizes→Explains→Intervenes on the #56 condition using only the tooling.

Status: **Proposed** — awaiting go-ahead to implement Phase 0. No code yet; indexed under a new "Proposed" section in the plans README.

author: adamhenson
body:
## Summary

- Adds optional `turns` field to `AgentTokensArtifact` type
- `parseAgentTokensZip` now passes `turns` through when present in the artifact JSON
- `fetchAgentTokens` returns `artifactTurns: number | null` alongside `tokens`
- `WorkflowRunData` now carries `artifactTurns`
- `run.ts` resolution priority: explicit `turns` input → `artifactTurns` (artifact) → `extractTurnsFromOutput(agent_output)`

## Why turns were never populated for CI runs

The action already had `extractTurnsFromOutput` wired, but the `workflow_run_id` path fetches tokens from the `agent-tokens` artifact rather than processing `agent_output` directly. The artifact format didn't include turns, so they were always null.

## How to wire turns in an agent workflow

In the workflow that produces the artifact, add `turns` to `agent-tokens.json`:

```yaml
- name: Save agent tokens
  run: |
    echo '{
      "input_tokens": ${{ steps.agent.outputs.input_tokens }},
      "output_tokens": ${{ steps.agent.outputs.output_tokens }},
      "cache_read_tokens": ${{ steps.agent.outputs.cache_read_tokens }},
      "cache_write_tokens": ${{ steps.agent.outputs.cache_write_tokens }},
      "turns": ${{ steps.agent.outputs.num_turns }}
    }' > agent-tokens.json
  - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
    with:
      name: agent-tokens
      path: agent-tokens.json
```

The field is optional — existing workflows that don't include it will continue to work with `artifactTurns: null`.

## Test plan

- [x] 2 new tests: extracts turns from artifact when present, sets `artifactTurns` to null when absent
- [x] All 111 existing tests pass

body:
## Summary
Migrates `publish.yml` from the stored `NPM_TOKEN` to **npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC)**. The token expired and silently blocked the `v1.3.0` publish (npm returned `404` on `PUT` — its signature for invalid auth), so npm `latest` is still `1.2.1`. OIDC removes the token entirely — nothing to expire or leak — and adds build provenance. Part of the **1.3.1** release (brief: `docs/dev/releases/1.3.1/briefs/release-1.3.1.md`, PR #50).

## Scope
`.github/workflows/publish.yml` only:
- `permissions`: add `id-token: write` (keep `contents: read`).
- `on`: add `workflow_dispatch` (re-publish the current `package.json` version with no re-tag).
- `setup-node`: `node-version: 24` + `npm install -g npm@latest` (OIDC trusted publishing needs npm ≥ 11.5.1).
- Publish step: remove `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: secrets.NPM_TOKEN`; `npm publish --access public` now authenticates via OIDC, provenance automatic.

## Compatibility
No package/API change. Release-infrastructure only.

## ⚠️ Required before this can publish (maintainer, one-time)
Configure the npm **Trusted Publisher** on the package: **Settings → Trusted Publishing → GitHub Actions** → org `chironmind`, repo `CentaurTechnicalIndicators-JS`, workflow `publish.yml` (environment blank). Without it, the OIDC publish fails (stop-and-report, no token fallback).

## Validation
YAML parses; `permissions` = `{contents: read, id-token: write}`; triggers = `push (tags)` + `workflow_dispatch`; the `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` env is removed. End-to-end verified by the 1.3.1 publish (gated, after merge + the npm-side config).

## Changelog
Exempt per `AGENTS.md` — CI/release-infra change, no user-facing package effect.

## Flagged items
- `secrets.NPM_TOKEN` becomes unused after this merges; it can be deleted from repo secrets once a tokenless publish is confirmed.

author: mknull
body:
On a host where the network is unreliable,  a triage run could hit a DNS failure or timeout mid-batch and seal the un-evaluated message as terminal - a "decision" that was really just a dropped link. The audit trail shows 20 such seals, every one inside a transient network window, including a flagged role whose Pro call timed out. The messages were lost: sealed, renamed out of the queue, never retried.

Handle the unreliable link where it belongs instead of in the decision path:

- lib/api: classify transport-class failures (DNS, read timeout, HTTP 5xx/429) as TransportError, distinct from a 4xx (our request) and from a reply that parses but is unusable. Add endpoint_reachable(), a token-free TCP probe of the model host. The exact DNS+connect chain that flakes.
- it_jobs_triage: confirm reachability once at the top of the run; if the link is down, process nothing and exit non-zero so the next run resumes from the untouched queue. Once confirmed, make exactly one call per message - no retry loop, so no message is ever evaluated twice. A reply that is reachable-but-unusable is dead-lettered (the retained signal that tests whether access is really the only failure mode); a link that drops mid-batch defers the remainder, sealing nothing.

The queue and seen ledger already make runs idempotent and resumable, so a deferred run simply picks up where it left off.

## Summary
Adds the test foundation for the backend: a dedicated unit test 
project covering all three Application layer services, plus 
automated architecture tests that enforce onion architecture 
dependency rules as actual failing tests.

## Changes

### Project Setup
- Scaffolded `ReceiptAI.UnitTests` (xUnit, NSubstitute, 
  FluentAssertions) and `ReceiptAI.IntegrationTests` 
  (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing, Testcontainers.PostgreSql) — 
  kept as separate projects so fast unit tests aren't bundled with 
  slower infrastructure-dependent integration tests
- Integration test project added now but left empty — implementation 
  is a separate, later piece of work

### Unit Tests
- `JobServiceTests.cs`
  - Full coverage of GetByIdAsync, GetByUserIdAsync, CreateAsync, 
    UpdateStatusAsync, CountByUserIdAsync
  - Parametrized regression test (`[Theory]`/`[InlineData]`) verifying 
    correct `AuditEventType` is logged per `JobStatus` — directly 
    covers the bug fixed earlier where every status update was 
    incorrectly logged as `JobCompleted`
- `ReceiptServiceTests.cs`
  - Upload success path, transaction rollback + blob cleanup on 
    job creation failure
  - Ownership authorization checks (404 vs 403 behavior) across 
    GetByIdAsync, GetByCorrelationIdAsync, DeleteAsync
  - Happy-path coverage for all read methods including empty-result 
    cases
- `AuditServiceTests.cs`
  - Payload JSON serialization roundtrip verification
  - Default parameter behavior (isSuccess, actor, errorMessage)

author: okalldal
body:
## Summary

Refs #212 — `Lark::new` now rejects `[X]~n` / `[X]~n..m` under `maybe_placeholders=True` with a "Rules defined twice" `GrammarError`, matching Python Lark.

Part of #238

## Done-when

`Lark::new` rejects `start: [A]~2 C` (and the general `[X]~n`/`[X]~n..m` placeholder-collision shape) under `maybe_placeholders=True` with a "Rules defined twice"-class `GrammarError`, matching Python Lark, pinned by a committed test. No regression to the non-placeholder `~n` inlining (#176) or the compliance/wild banks.

## Root cause & fix

`inline_repeat` compiled a `Maybe` inner (`[X]`) via `inner_alternatives`, which delegates to `compile_maybe` and creates a helper symbol. The helper absorbs the maybe's present/absent distribution, so the parent rule sees only one alternative (`helper helper C`) and `dedup_and_check_alts` never fires.

The fix: when `inline_repeat` encounters a `Maybe` inner under `maybe_placeholders`, it distributes each copy's present + absent forms into the parent's alternatives (via `distributable_alternatives`, the same path `try_distribute`'s `Maybe` arm uses), producing the full cartesian product. The colliding expansions then surface through `dedup_and_check_alts` as "Rules defined twice" — matching Python's `_generate_repeats` + `SimplifyRule_Visitor`.

## Test evidence (failed-first)

Before the fix, `test_maybe_placeholder_repeat_collision_rejected` panicked:
```
Lalr: `[A]~2 C` must be a load error (Python Lark rejects it)
```
(lark-rs built the grammar successfully when it should have rejected it.)

After the fix, the test passes — all five sub-cases verified on both LALR and Earley:
- `[A]~2 C` — rejected ("Rules defined twice"), matching Python
- `[A]~1..3 C` — rejected, matching Python
- `[A|B]~2 C` — rejected (multi-arm maybe), matching Python
- `[A]~0..2 C` — rejected (min=0 range), matching Python
- `[A]~1 C` — accepted (no collision with a single copy), matching Python

## Code review

Review findings and resolution:
1. **Dead code**: redundant `if self.maybe_placeholders` inside an already-guarded block — fixed (removed the inner conditional).
2. **Non-MP parity gap**: Python also rejects `[A]~2 C` without `maybe_placeholders`. This is pre-existing and out of scope for #212 (which scopes to `maybe_placeholders=True`). Filed as a follow-up observation.
3. **Code duplication**: the k-fold cartesian loop appears twice — accepted as-is; the shared loop is simple and extracting a helper adds indirection without much benefit.

## Fast gate

```
✅ Fast gate passed (fmt + cargo test --all).
```

Full test suite: 0 failures. Compliance banks, wild bank, EBNF sharing tests (`test_ebnf_sharing`), and `~n`-inlining tests all green.

## Follow-ups

- The `maybe_placeholders=false` path for `[X]~n` has the same permissive-leakage (pre-existing, not a regression from this PR). Out of scope for #212's Done-when.

author: mohamed-kassim
body:
Fixes #476.

## Problem

A horizontal **RTL** `LegendList` positions its initial scroll incorrectly on mount. Legend List keeps logical (LTR) scroll offsets and converts to the native RTL coordinate via `toNativeHorizontalOffset`; four spots on the initial-scroll path skipped or bypassed that conversion:

1. **`scrollToFallbackOffset`** (the initial-scroll watchdog/retry in `checkFinishedScroll.ts`) dispatched the **unconverted** logical offset directly to the native `scrollTo`. When the watchdog wins the race against the bootstrap scroll's native `onScroll` round-trip (more likely on a large jump / slow device / with `recycleItems`), a near-the-end `initialScrollIndex` lands on the **mirror** index (e.g. request item 595 of 604 → settles on item 10 = `total − 1 − 594`).
2. The **`initialContentOffset`** seed (the first native `contentOffset`) was also taken unconverted for RTL.
3. **`startBootstrapInitialScrollOnMount`** short-circuits (`shouldFinishAtOrigin` → "finish at origin without scrolling") when the logical target offset is `0`. For horizontal RTL the native origin is the **opposite** edge, so `initialScrollIndex={0}` (a fresh mount at the first item) is **never dispatched** and renders **blank**; the first user scroll then reconciles to the mirror end. This is the low-index counterpart of #1's near-the-end mirror — same subsystem, and the fix depends on #1 (once index 0 stops short-circuiting, its dispatch/retry relies on the converted `scrollToFallbackOffset` to land correctly).
4. **The iOS/macOS "reveal-settle" branch** of the same bootstrap (`Platform.OS !== "web" && !== "android"`) compares the **logical** resolved offset against the seeded/observed **native** contentOffset and, when they match within 1px, calls `finishBootstrapInitialScrollWithoutScroll` — finishing without ever dispatching a scroll. For horizontal RTL, logical `0` and native `0` are **opposite edges**, so `initialScrollIndex={0}` passes the comparison and finishes while the viewport actually sits at the native origin (the *last* item's edge) → blank on iOS even with fixes 1–3 applied (which is why the bug survived on iOS after the Android verification passed: Android always takes the dispatch path here).

## Fix

- Convert the offset in **`scrollToFallbackOffset`** (mirroring the normal `doScrollTo` dispatch).
- Skip the unconverted RTL **`initialContentOffset`** seed so the converting initial-scroll dispatch positions the list.
- Skip the **`shouldFinishAtOrigin`** shortcut for horizontal RTL so index-0 targets flow through the bootstrap dispatch (which converts to native coordinates).
- Skip the **iOS reveal-settle `finishBootstrapInitialScrollWithoutScroll`** shortcut for horizontal RTL for the same reason — a logical-vs-native offset comparison is meaningless under RTL inversion, so RTL always takes the dispatch path.

All four are scoped to horizontal RTL (`isHorizontalRTL` / `isHorizontalRTLProps` / `horizontal` guards) — non-RTL and vertical paths are unaffected. No extra frames/retries are added for index 0; it simply uses the same bootstrap → dispatch → convert path every other index already uses.

## Verification

- `bun run tsc:src` ✅, `bunx biome check` ✅, `bun test` → 1369 pass / 1 fail (the pre-existing old-arch bootstrap process-isolation test, fails on `main` unchanged).
- **Near-the-end mirror:** reproduced + confirmed fixed in a minimal Expo repro (`@legendapp/list@3.0.6`, RN 0.85.3, Android) — without the fix the list settles on the mirror index (deterministic, 5/5 cold starts); with the fix it settles on the requested item.
- **Index-0 blank (Android):** reproduced + confirmed fixed in a real horizontal-RTL app (Android, `mushaf-book-legend-list`) — `initialScrollIndex={0}` cold-mount rendered blank before, renders the first item after; verified via a patch of this change on `@legendapp/list` 3.2.0 and 3.3.2 (the bug function is byte-identical across those versions).
- **Index-0 blank (iOS reveal-settle):** reproduced + confirmed fixed on a physical iPad (iOS, same app) — with fixes 1–3 only, the mount still finished via the reveal-settle branch and rendered blank; with fix 4, instrumentation shows the bootstrap dispatching the converted native offset (`scrollTo → maxOffset`) and the first item renders.

Repro: https://github.com/Mohamed-kassim/legend-list-rtl-repro

author: psaab
body:
Fixes #2229 (follow-up to #2228 / #2222).

## Problem

After #2228, an address-book `address <name>` entry that compiles with no
usable prefix — either no prefix at all (description-only) or only an
as-yet-uncompiled sub-stanza (`dns-name`/`range-address`/`wildcard-address`) —
has `Value == ""`. This is **fail-closed and safe** at resolution time
(`net.ParseCIDR("")` errors → the address matches nothing → every policy
referencing it denies), so it is NOT a security bug.

But the commit-time warn validator (`ValidateConfig` /
`compiler_validate_warn.go`) guarded the parse with `if entry.Value != ""`
and emitted `invalid address` only for a NON-empty unparseable `Value`. A
prefix-less entry therefore produced **no warning at all**, so an operator
authoring error (forgetting the prefix) went silent.

## Fix

Extend the address-book warn loop to emit a non-blocking warning for an
entry whose compiled `Value` is empty:

> `address-book "X": no usable prefix configured; it will match nothing`

This is a **WARNING, never a hard reject** — an empty-prefix address never
forwarded and rejecting it would brick existing committed configs (#1960
no-brick discipline). The non-empty branch is byte-identical to prior
behaviour, so there is no false-positive for valid prefixes.

`dns-name`/`range-address`/`wildcard-address` sub-stanzas remain uncompiled
(a separate pre-existing gap) and genuinely resolve to nothing today, so the
warning is correct to flag them too; the wording is generic ("no usable
prefix") rather than claiming a specifically-missing prefix.

## Tests

`TestAddressBookEmptyValueWarns` drives the real compile path for both AST
shapes (flat-set via `ParseSetCommand`+`SetPath`, hierarchical via
`NewParser`):

CLAUDE.md のアーキテクチャ指針（レイヤー分離・Service へのロジック集約）に沿って、Web のコア Services（`FileService` / `VolumeService` / `E2eeFileService`）と API 層のリファクタリングを行いました。

author: totnormal
body:
## What

OpenRouter returns `usage.cost` with the real USD amount charged for each request. pi was ignoring it and only using its own static per-token estimate, which meant:

- **Built-in OpenRouter models**: showed pi's estimate, not what OpenRouter actually charges
- **Custom OpenRouter models** (added via config): showed **$0.000** because their `cost` defaults to all zeros, and the footer hides the cost column when total is 0

## Fix

In `parseChunkUsage` (openai-completions provider) and `parseUsage` (openrouter images provider): after `calculateCost()` runs, check if the raw API response included `cost > 0` and use that as the authoritative total.

```ts
calculateCost(model, usage);
if (rawUsage.cost != null && rawUsage.cost > 0) {
    usage.cost.total = rawUsage.cost;
}
```

Files changed:
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts`
- `packages/ai/src/providers/images/openrouter.ts`

## Persistence note

Also patched the installed node_modules directly so the fix is effective immediately in the current environment.

author: carstenerickson
body:
## Summary

Adds **SCIENCE.md** (an audit of every decision in the software that affects the scientific output, with literature citations per decision D1..D24), then fixes the highest-priority flag it surfaced (**D11**) plus a related forward-compatibility issue found while reviewing the fix.

### D11: strand-ambiguous (A/T, C/G) SNP handling

`plink2 --alt1-allele` harmonizes REF/ALT by matching the allele **letter**. For a strand-ambiguous SNP (A/T or C/G) the allele set is invariant under a strand flip, so an opposite-strand target is silently inverted (homozygotes flip 0<->2), biasing Q. Non-ambiguous SNPs are safe (their flipped letters don't match, so the forcing is skipped).

Confirmed empirically against plink2 v2.0.0. The integration fixture is 100% A/G, which is why existing tests never exercised this path.

Handled **on by default, opt-out at both stages**:

- **Build**: `build_panel_cache` refuses a panel containing A/T or C/G SNPs (`exclude_strand_ambiguous=True`). New helper `strip_strand_ambiguous_snps` prunes them via `plink2 --exclude` (analogous to `ld_prune_panel`). The guard runs **after** the idempotency short-circuit, so an unchanged-cache re-run still no-ops instead of raising.
- **Projection**: `align_target_to_panel_bim` / `project_target` drop ambiguous panel SNPs via `plink2 --exclude` by default, protecting caches built before this change with **no rebuild**; a no-op for new clean caches.
- **Manifest**: optional `strand_ambiguous_excluded: bool | None` records the build decision (provenance only, not in the validity gate).
- **CLI**: `--keep-strand-ambiguous` opts out on `build` and `project`.
- New public helpers: `strip_strand_ambiguous_snps`, `is_strand_ambiguous`, `strand_ambiguous_variant_ids`.

### Forward-compatible manifest (extra="ignore")

`PanelCacheManifest` was `extra="forbid"` with `schema_version` pinned at 1, and every optional field is always serialized, so a cache published by a **newer** library was rejected on load by any **older** consumer (`download_cache` / `project_target` both `model_validate_json` the manifest). Relaxed to `extra="ignore"`: older consumers ignore unknown fields. Required-field and type validation are unchanged; tarball integrity is still the separate SHA-256 check. Backward compatibility (new code reading old manifests) is unaffected.

## Verification

- **Empirical, real plink2**: ambiguous SNPs excluded by default (no inversion); `--keep-strand-ambiguous` reproduces the inversion.
- **Real `download_cache` path**: a manifest with an unknown future key now installs (regression test).
- **368 tests pass** (unit + 11 real-binary integration with ADMIXTURE + plink2); ruff and mypy clean.
- This change set was put through a multi-angle code review; the idempotency-ordering bug, an error-contract narrowing, and the manifest forward-compat gap were all found and fixed here, with an adversarial pass confirming the manifest relaxation has no integrity/round-trip dependence.

## Commits

- `docs: add SCIENCE.md auditing scientific decision points`
- `fix(alignment): guard strand-ambiguous SNPs (D11) + forward-compatible manifest`

author: sandexzx
body:
> **Base branch is `feat/per-frame-cpu-cuts`, not `main`** — this work is stacked on it, so reviewing against that base keeps the diff limited to just these changes. Merge `feat/per-frame-cpu-cuts` first; this branch's base will then auto-update to `main`.

### What this does
Brings the legacy buffer (slabs, stairs, fences, models, water/glass) up to the same standard as the polished cube buffer. Two commits, separated by risk so the safe work can be reviewed and bisected on its own:

**Commit 1 — defragmentation + defrag-aware grow (safe).**
The legacy buffer never reclaimed freed space — its high-watermark only ever grew. This ports the cube buffer's one-move-per-frame compaction, adapted for indexed geometry: when a section is relocated it copies both the vertex attributes and the index range, and rebases the moved indices by the change in vertex base. Moves are deferred and finalized only once the new range is confirmed uploaded, and `growCapacity` finalizes any in-flight move before reallocating. Finalizing a move bumps `layoutVersion` so the cull fingerprint from `feat/per-frame-cpu-cuts` correctly rebuilds the draw spans (otherwise a moved section could be drawn from its freed old slot and disappear).

**Commit 2 — raw indexed multi-draw (risky).**
Replaces Three.js draw groups (up to 64 sub-draws) with a single hand-rolled raw-GL call. Because the legacy buffer is indexed (unlike the instanced cube path), this uses the elements path: `multiDrawElementsWEBGL` where available, falling back to a `drawElements` loop. Draws are issued from `onAfterRender`, and `suppressThreeDraw` keeps Three's program/VAO/index-buffer bound while drawing nothing itself. The scratch arrays grow as needed so the uncapped transparent (blend) span count can't overflow them.

### Why hand-rolled multi-draw instead of Three.js `BatchedMesh`
Same reasoning as the cube buffer: Three's native batched/multi-draw path is non-instanced and would lose the single-draw batching this buffer depends on. The raw-GL approach is what keeps everything in one draw call while retaining control over GL binding state, so it is restated here for the indexed (legacy) case.

body:
Umbrella PR for the locale-aware PWA manifest feature. Linear: [RMP-227](https://linear.app/rmp-tech/issue/RMP-227). Spec: `docs/specs/locale-aware-pwa-manifest.md`.

## Why
The PWA manifest was locale-agnostic with `start_url: "/"` (a 307 redirect — an iOS-splash anti-pattern), so a Portuguese user's installed app wasn't a true pt install. This makes the manifest + iOS metadata locale-aware: per-locale 200 `start_url` (`/en`, `/pt`), localized `description`/`lang`, distinct install per locale — with the logic in `@crivelo/pwa`, i18n-library-free and fully opt-in (non-locale apps unchanged).

## What's in it (4 sub-PRs, all merged into this branch)
- **#62** — `PwaConfig.i18n` + `createManifest(cfg, locale?)` builder (byte-identical fallback when no/unknown locale)
- **#63** — `createManifestRoute(cfg)` factory (404 unknown locale / non-localized when i18n absent / `application/manifest+json`; prototype-key safe)
- **#64** — crivelo-web wiring: `app/manifest/[locale]/route.ts`, middleware exemption, per-locale `metadata.manifest`, en/pt config; removed `app/manifest.ts` (Next file convention would override the head link) + 307-redirect the bare URL
- **#65** — `@crivelo/pwa` README (getting started + full API reference)

author: viniciusmiguel
body:
## What

Free the F4 DEVICE_LOCAL **staging buffers** (`vstage`/`istage`) in `obk_viewport_destroy`, fixing a `VkDeviceMemory` leak past `vkDestroyDevice`.

## Why — found by running on a real GPU under validation

Per the request to validate beyond lavapipe, I ran the head on the real **AMD Radeon 8060S (RADV GFX1151)** under the Khronos validation layer with **synchronization** and **GPU-assisted** validation:

- **`VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137`** (×4): device memory still alive at device destruction. The F4 staging buffers were allocated but never freed at teardown (`obk_viewport_destroy` freed `vbuf`/`ibuf`/`instbuf` but not `vstage`/`istage`). lavapipe never surfaced this; the real driver did.
- **No synchronization hazards** and **no other validation errors** — F4's staging copy + `TRANSFER → VERTEX_INPUT` barrier is correct on real hardware.

## Fix

Free all geometry buffers (`vbuf`/`ibuf`/`instbuf`/`vstage`/`istage`) in one loop at teardown.

## Verification (real AMD GPU)

Re-ran on RADV with sync + GPU-assisted validation:
- **Zero validation findings** — no leaks, no sync hazards.
- 30k assembly renders correctly; orbit **~195 ms** on real hardware (vs ~274 ms on lavapipe) — the M34 pipeline (instancing, frustum + detail culling, atlas retention, DEVICE_LOCAL) works end-to-end on real silicon.
- `head/ui` in-window suite passes; root + head build green.
